entries.title: Lynleit: Biography
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Biography Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Lynleit is associated with the Cult of Inanna through Fionn's lineage, without directly participating in it. She grew up close to MSF leadership. Felix and Reiner became her friends and the bodyguards Fionn trusted with her safety. At the Magi Academy, Natalia was her favourite teacher. She distrusted Helena before any open conspiracy, noticing her stepmother's questions about Fionn's schedules, visitors, trusted officers, and Lynleit's travel. At the Prosecutor General's appointment dinner, Kyrien's failed attack nearly harms her. She never tells him she attended. His represented interrogation reveals years of work paying lawyers and caring for his mother. She recognizes suppression behind his father's persecution and keeps that knowledge from him. Guilt, admiration of his competence, and her warning of approaching danger lead her to offer paid confidential service and limited help obtaining release. She tells only Felix and Reiner in her circle. After her mother's death, Lynleit resisted the family's move from Turon to Vilen and accepted it only on the condition that her study-bedroom occupy the third floor. The hillside site places thick trees close to the house and overlooks a river flowing toward the city center. Rustling leaves inspire her. She regards flowing water as life energy and seeks its emotional grounding despite her childhood fear of drowning. Days before Fionn's death, the Nameless Street leaves Lynleit with the memory of a dead boy below a broken fence. Seeing her father's body below the hill at the family house brings the memory back. Helena uses her stunned reaction to support the accusation that Lynleit killed him. Hunted and out of resources, Lynleit reaches Kyrien's hotel-room hideout. He helps her reconnect with Felix and Reiner. Fionn's old officers begin questioning Helena when Lynleit can answer his private recognition challenge and Helena cannot. During the river operation, the Drowned Choir drags Lynleit underwater and tears away her blue suede jacket. She burns the hands with blue flame, breaks the surface, and stands on the water. Kyrien sees her from the park bank. It is his first unmistakable exposure to magic; he tells nobody, and she initially only suspects what he saw. Father Mikhail later discovers that Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner know about magic. Lynleit insists on handling the breach herself. When the Church and Magiarchy send her to assist Mikhail in Cardiff, she sends Kyrien to help Myka at the Academy. She underestimates the danger there. In Cardiff, she and Mikhail protect one another despite their incompatible methods. Midway through Arc 1, after Fionn's death, Lynleit discovers that he replaced her coat with a leviathan-hide garment. Later in the second half of Arc 1, she and Kyrien survive a shared curse after an incomplete attempt at intimacy. She refuses to discuss it with him even after the curse is gone. Their sexual relationship begins later. Near the Arc 2 transition she disappears. She bears their son during her absence and keeps him hidden from Kyrien and the wider world while raising him, recovering, and seeking answers about the Spill. Years later she begins appearing around MSF missions without explaining her return. During Arc 2 they restore intimacy; this eventually leads to the conception and later birth of their daughter, their second child. Grows up as Fionn's daughter and studies magecraft under Natalia. Survives the Drowned Choir; Kyrien witnesses her walking on water. Assists Mikhail abroad without MSF's conventional resources. Sends Kyrien to help Myka while she is away. Helena blames her for Fionn's death. Escapes to Kyrien and reconnects with Felix and Reiner. Asks Kyrien why he keeps accepting danger without a promised reward. Survives a shared curse in the later part of Arc 1’s second half, after the hotel refuge. Exact placement remains open. Leaves near the Arc 2 transition to raise her son and investigate the Spill. Reappears around MSF operations without announcing her return. Development outline: continuing grief, a changing household, and school years before the main story. Months after Doom, private research and spontaneous closeness lead to a successful encounter in the park, before later intercourse. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Conflicts
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Conflicts Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Helena's accusation She must recover allies inside the agency now hunting her. Forbidden witnesses Mikhail knows she disclosed magic to Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner. She insists on handling the breach herself. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Connections
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Connections Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Felix Long-standing friend and bodyguard Their friendship allows teasing, blunt correction, and easy physical familiarity. He and Reiner accompany her and Fionn on church visits. Felix repeatedly flirts with nuns while Reiner behaves, eventually exhausting her patience. When she catches him by his tie, he answers with a declaration of attention to her. She rejects his reading of the reprimand. Their son First child Born during Lynleit's disappearance and kept hidden from Kyrien and the wider world afterward. Their daughter Second child Conceived after intimacy is restored during Arc 2 and born later. Kyrien Strategic recruit and eventual partner She recruits him deliberately for strategic reasons, without anticipating their eventual closeness. Card games, shared work, and his protection of her water-walking secret bring private familiarity. He shelters her after Fionn's death and chooses to remain when she can no longer compel him. Her initiative, pride, and curiosity meet his reserve and close observation. Gradually each allows the other to notice what they would usually conceal, and quiet companionship becomes important without displacing her duties. Natalia Favourite teacher and friend Lynleit jokes with Natalia, challenges her conclusions, and readily returns to her for help. She follows her explanations with a student's curiosity rather than a subordinate's deference. Natalia taught her at the Magi Academy, later asks her to help Myka, and identifies ego transformation as a possible way to survive the shared curse. Father Mikhail Cardiff counterpart and theological adviser The Magiarchy and Church send Lynleit to assist Mikhail abroad. They protect one another despite a moral rift, and he later finds related cases in Church records and proposes reciprocal identity change as a possible way out of the shared curse. His mock blessing names her lineage's association with the Cult of Inanna. She objects to his use of family history as a personal obligation and threatens a reprisal if he repeats the address publicly. Kyrien Kyrien's failed attack nearly harms her, but she never tells him. Their coerced alliance acquires a private familiarity through card games and shared work. He keeps her water-walking secret, shelters her after Fionn's murder, and chooses to stay when he could leave. An incomplete attempt at intimacy ends their shared curse; her embarrassment and his unanswered questions outlast it. Helena Lynleit distrusts her stepmother before the takeover, then learns Helena played a major role in Fionn's assassination even though the full conspiracy remains unclear. Potential sexual tension Kyrien Established arc Mutual, slow to surface Lynleit studies Kyrien first as a recruit whose failed attack nearly harmed her. Their card games make that scrutiny personal: she learns his tells and begins noticing his hands and breath. Later she attempts intimacy as a possible treatment for their shared curse, but remains interested after they survive without completing it. Mikhail's mock blessing exposes her family association with the Cult of Inanna. She counters with abstract principles and increasingly personal objections. His teasing does not create her attraction to Kyrien or make ancestry a reason for it. In the park, she wants to correct her private sense of failure, then finds satisfaction in knowing Kyrien as a particular person. Her theory follows an impulse already present. The preparation remains theoretical. Her attention shifts from proving competence toward learning his individual responses; the current park draft leaves that passage for the author rather than depicting it. Recruitment remains antagonistic: Kyrien's legal campaign and care obligations make paid work and release support materially important. Lynleit's concern for his mother coexists with leverage and concealed anger. Neither his agreement nor her guilt establishes attraction. The interrogation, card games, protected secret, and voluntary decision to stay give this pairing different kinds of familiarity. In Doom Has an Address, an incomplete attempt at intimacy breaks the shared curse. Lynleit loses the excuse of treatment without losing her interest in Kyrien; he is left trying to understand what happened. Their sexual relationship begins later in Arc 1. Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge precede Doom. Months afterward, a spontaneous park encounter lets Lynleit's curiosity and wounded pride become a successful private milestone. Oral intimacy, reciprocal exploration, first intercourse, and pregnancy remain separate. The family theme does not turn ancestry into an instruction or make grief itself attraction. Lynleit bears their son during her disappearance and later keeps him hidden from both Kyrien and the wider world. They restore intimacy during Arc 2 and eventually conceive a second child, a daughter, who is born later. The daughter's conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2, not within it. The author has confirmed this direction, not the scenes that restore intimacy or the timing of Kyrien's discovery of their son. Duty remains primary; a second child does not substitute for the work of reconnection. Potential sexual tension Felix Established asymmetry Felix overt, Lynleit deflecting Felix's flirting belongs to a long friendship she refuses to reorganize around his advances. Her ease with him, combined with the repeated refusal, creates visible chemistry without requiring matching sexual intent. Only Eyes for You develops a recurring problem during Lynleit and Fionn's church visits, with Felix and Reiner accompanying them. Reiner behaves, while Felix repeatedly flirts with nuns until Lynleit loses patience. He answers her eventual reprimand with 'I only have eyes for you.' The author identifies accumulated irritation as the comic cause, not jealousy. His reply redirects an objection he does not want to answer; it does not make her objection romantic. His wider flirting coexists with his persistent fixation on Lynleit and does not establish an attachment to any particular nun. The visits precede Fionn's death, but their exact placement and relation to his growing closeness with Sherie remain open. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Magecraft
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Magecraft Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Hereditary magecraft Blue flame Lynleit inherited her family's ability to manifest blue flame. It can be directed into many applications, but her control is less subtle than Fionn's. Natural tendency Unsafe volume Where Fionn relies on virtuosity and precision, Lynleit has the nerve to call forth far more flame than is safe. Force comes more readily to her than finesse. Irreplaceable force Beyond ordinary weapons Blue flame becomes indispensable when normal firearms cannot finish the threat: an immortal or rapidly regenerating Holumn, a body that moves without being alive, or a barrier that conventional force cannot breach. Accidental miracle-making Walking on water This ability appeared independently of her inherited magecraft. It manifested from her childhood fear of drowning and allows her to cross the surface of water on foot. Its resemblance to a sacred miracle places it outside tolerated magecraft. Strictly concealed Night practice Lynleit keeps the talent secret from everyone because the Church strongly punishes miracle-making that imitates acts associated with Jesus, saints, saviours, and other sacred figures, even when the effect seems harmless. She practices alone at night on secluded stretches of local lakes and rivers. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Strengths and weaknesses Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Lynleit puts MSF and her own missions first. She shares her thinking with the people she leads. When uncertain, she feels there is an answer even though she cannot yet explain it. Talking to someone she trusts helps bring it into focus; she tries not to show how much the uncertainty troubles her. In private she is reserved and reflective. Personal embarrassment makes her evasive or irritable, especially when Kyrien notices it. Mikhail gets formal objections, sharp retorts, and eventually a carefully worded threat. Relational leadership 95 She treats candid communication as a source of trust and coordinated action. A trusted objection can unsettle her even when a plan is working, making her question whether she pushed for something others were uncomfortable with. Strategic foresight 92 An unresolved sense that something is wrong can prevent her from fully committing to a plan. Trusted reassurance sometimes helps her proceed, but does not settle the unease; she may postpone without being able to explain why. Private introspection 86 In private she is comfortable disappearing into solitude, following symbolic threads, and processing difficult emotion internally. INFJ Ni-led reading; strong Fe Suspected Lynleit

Myka encounters terrors inside the Academy and must rely on Natalia for rescue and support. Natalia asks Lynleit for help, but Lynleit is being sent to Cardiff and dispatches Kyrien as her substitute. The threat turns formal study into a struggle for survival inside an institution meant to train and protect young Magi. Kyrien enters the Academy as a non-Magus undercover helper and keeps Myka safe through conventional field skills and communications with Felix and Reiner. The danger exceeds Lynleit's estimate and forces Natalia to intervene personally. This becomes Myka's first direct experience with Kyrien and MSF. Myka survives the Academy crisis and graduates at the top of her class. Her experience with Kyrien contributes to her later decision to join MSF as a Magus. Studies at the Academy and seeks advice from Natalia. Faces dangers she cannot resolve within the institution. Receives help from Kyrien and later Natalia. entries.title: Natalia: Biography
entries.subtitle: Independent magical examiner and private investigator
entries.text: Natalia: Biography Independent magical examiner and private investigator Natalia earned a professorship at the Magi Academy as a talented Magus and serious researcher. Lynleit studied under her during those years and remembers Natalia as her favourite teacher. Natalia eventually found academic life too constraining: the institution could support scholarship, but it also defined which questions were respectable and how far an inquiry was permitted to go. She resigned to continue her work independently. Natalia opens a private-investigation business to pay for her independent research. Her knowledge of Magi and magecraft attracts clients whose problems ordinary investigators cannot handle. Her one-woman office now sits between a detective agency, consultation room, and private laboratory. Clients bring suspected crimes, unstable talents, personal deviations, and magical problems they cannot safely expose. Natalia examines the person and phenomenon before deciding whether a crime has occurred at all. Lester repeatedly forces her to distinguish professional fascination with his demiholumn condition from personal attention to him. When Myka encounters terrors inside the Academy, Natalia becomes her principal source of advice, rescue, and support beyond the institution. She asks her former student Lynleit for help, then intervenes personally when the danger exceeds the protection Kyrien can provide. Natalia's work repeatedly brings her into contact with Lester. Her interest in him becomes personal as well as professional. Helping Myka renews her work with Lynleit and introduces her niece to Kyrien and MSF. Neither Natalia nor Lester knows how he became a demiholumn. She comes to recognize his contradictory chronology as an intrinsic feature of nature, without reconciling it into an ordinary causal history. Teaches Lynleit at the Magi Academy. Resigns to pursue research independently. Takes investigative and examination work to fund it. Intervenes when Kyrien can no longer contain the danger to Myka. Identifies transformation as an alternative to the shared curse's fatal solution. Works with Lester as an independent ally. Natalia

entries.title: Natalia: Connections
entries.subtitle: Independent magical examiner and private investigator
entries.text: Natalia: Connections Independent magical examiner and private investigator Lester Outside ally and source of tension Lester remains outside the business, but his demiholumn nature sometimes carries Natalia past barriers that scholarship and ordinary investigation cannot cross. Their attraction develops along the boundary between examination and being personally seen. Myka Niece, student, and friend Natalia keeps constant contact with her niece at the Magi Academy. Myka asks for advice on her studies, Natalia checks on her life, and their bond often resembles mother and daughter as much as aunt and niece. Lynleit Former student and friend Natalia teaches through examples Lynleit can work through, including her own failed approaches. Lynleit teases her, offers playful objections, and trusts her enough to keep asking difficult questions. Their friendship is informal; Natalia's greater experience remains evident in the corrections and connections Lynleit learns from her. They work together over Myka's danger and the curse Lynleit shares with Kyrien. Lester Lester is not her employee. He is an outside ally and a demiholumn whose part-Holumn nature sometimes allows him to accomplish what should be impossible for an ordinary investigator. Their repeated work carries sexual tension because her effort to understand him cannot remain entirely separate from personal attention. Institutional capture The Academy, Magiarchy, and Church can each narrow an inquiry by deciding which questions are permissible, which cases belong to them, and which answers must remain hidden. Potential sexual tension Lester Established tension Mutual, differently expressed Lester is the living exception that Natalia cannot finish classifying. Her professional attention can become personal before she recognizes the change, especially when he interrupts an examination by noticing that she is watching him rather than the phenomenon around him. Repeated cases bring Natalia's examination of Lester into conflict with his insistence on being treated as more than a case. He provokes her to act; she notices more than he expected. Their attraction does not answer her questions about his demiholumn nature. Neither knows how he came into existence. His chronology is intrinsically contradictory, not a solvable transformation history. Natalia's recognition that contradiction belongs to nature does not mean she can explain him completely or that attraction answers the contradiction. Natalia

entries.text: Natalia: Motivations Independent magical examiner and private investigator Fund and protect an independent life of magical research while giving clients an answer before hidden authorities reduce their problem to jurisdiction, secrecy, or punishment. Natalia

entries.title: Natalia: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Independent magical examiner and private investigator
entries.text: Natalia: Strengths and weaknesses Independent magical examiner and private investigator Natalia investigates private cases to pay for the research she wants to do. She left the Academy rather than keep asking permission to pursue it. When explaining a difficult idea, she reaches for an example or something she tried herself, including the attempts that failed. She asks her listener to try the next step and enjoys a good objection. Lynleit gets the lesson and the teasing of a former student who is still her friend. Natalia admits where her evidence runs out. Independent scholarship She resigned from the Academy when its environment became too restrictive for the questions and methods she wanted to pursue. Magical examination She examines unusual magecraft and personal deviations closely, studying the affected person as well as the circumstances of the incident. Selective casework The business has one employee: Natalia. Paid cases finance her research and let her choose which clients, risks, and secrets enter her office. Identity analysis When Lynleit and Kyrien inherit a shared curse, Natalia introduces the ego hypothesis and quotes Jung. A two-name diagram helps Lynleit follow its paired attachment; Natalia's own research mistakes distinguish a changed self-description from a change in decisions. She cannot measure the degree of transformation the curse requires. INTP strong Ti Confirmed Natalia

entries.text: Reiner: Biography MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Reiner is Lynleit's long-standing friend and one of the MSF officers Fionn trusts as her personal bodyguards. They also spend time together outside assignments. Lynleit reveals her secret recruitment of Kyrien only to Reiner and Felix, withholding it even from Fionn. Reiner sees the same danger Felix sees, particularly whenever neither bodyguard is near her, but recognizes that rejecting the plan would also mean rejecting Lynleit's judgment. Reiner accepts Lynleit's decision to recruit Kyrien despite the breach of protocol. His vote leaves Felix in the minority. He continues watching Kyrien. Reiner's trust does not eliminate scrutiny. After Fionn's murder and the hunt for Lynleit's arrest, Kyrien helps her contact Reiner and Felix from hiding. Reiner must protect her, preserve the covert link inside Helena's MSF, and decide how far disciplined loyalty can support the effort to reclaim the agency. Serves alongside Lynleit as a friend and trusted bodyguard. Learns she recruited Kyrien without Fionn's knowledge. Supports her decision despite his reservations. Keeps Kyrien under scrutiny while helping Lynleit. Reiner

entries.text: Reiner: Motivations MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Protect Lynleit while testing whether disciplined loyalty can accommodate the anti-protocol risk she has chosen. Reiner

entries.title: Reiner: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard
entries.text: Reiner: Strengths and weaknesses MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Reiner is stern and rarely smiles. He follows procedure, respects the chain of command, and takes duty and legitimate authority seriously. A small break in his composure is conspicuous beside Felix's constant play. In the field he commits to the direct line: the rook that holds a position or breaks through it. Protocol-focused He treats procedure as accumulated operational knowledge and notices quickly when others disregard it. Severe composure Reiner is restrained, difficult to fluster, and rarely seen smiling even among people he trusts. When he and Felix accompany Lynleit and Fionn to churches, Reiner behaves appropriately while Felix keeps flirting with the nuns. Reliable protection He expresses friendship through preparation, consistency, and remaining exactly where Lynleit needs him to be. ISTJ strong Si-Te Confirmed Reiner

entries.title: Reiner: Tradecraft
entries.subtitle: MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard
entries.text: Reiner: Tradecraft MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Direct action Brute-force intervention Reiner specializes in situations where an obstacle must be confronted directly, relying on physical power, discipline, and decisive commitment. Physical security Close protection His build and composure make him the stable physical barrier in Lynleit's security detail, able to hold position when an operation becomes chaotic. Operational geometry Rook pattern He controls clear lines, anchors a position, and applies force without unnecessary movement. Reiner is most effective when the threat has nowhere left to hide. Reiner

entries.title: Sherie: Biography
entries.subtitle: Diplomat in training and covert negotiator
entries.text: Sherie: Biography Diplomat in training and covert negotiator Sherie studies diplomacy under her uncle Drake. She is quicker at reading a room and drawing people into conversation than he is. Drake's peers ridicule his warning and the Duke remains skeptical. Sherie believes her uncle, but rejects his decision to remain inside official limits and begins designing her own approach to Lynleit. Sherie develops the unauthorized approach to Lynleit against Drake's wishes, persuades him to attend, and leads the negotiations herself. After it succeeds, she asks him to praise and pamper her. Sherie and Drake use the private agreement to ask Lynleit for a loyal team capable of covertly inspecting apparently unmanned night shipments on the Vilen river. The empty boats and the Drowned Choir prove that the suspected coup cannot be understood as a purely political operation. Trains under her uncle Drake. Proposes approaching Lynleit outside official channels. Conducts the hilltop negotiation despite Drake's reluctance. Requests the river inspection with Drake. Sherie

entries.title: Sherie: Conflicts
entries.subtitle: Diplomat in training and covert negotiator
entries.text: Sherie: Conflicts Diplomat in training and covert negotiator Unauthorized agreement Her private approach to MSF would be stopped if the Court or government discovered it. Uneven attachment Felix becomes increasingly important to her while remaining fixated on Lynleit. Sherie has limits to what attention she will accept; she wants to be seen clearly, not simply enjoyed as a diversion. Sherie

entries.title: Sherie: Connections
entries.subtitle: Diplomat in training and covert negotiator
entries.text: Sherie: Connections Diplomat in training and covert negotiator Felix Growing familiarity They have no meaningful personal relationship at the story's opening. Her diplomatic work increasingly overlaps with his duties around Lynleit and MSF. Repeated encounters bring respect, private jokes, and affection. Sherie enjoys directing their exchanges; Felix teases back and complicates her control. His continued fixation on Lynleit can hurt, even as he seeks Sherie's company. Her confidence does not spare her disappointment or doubts about whether he sees her clearly. Drake Her uncle, mentor, and strategic counterpart. He trains her for diplomacy, while her charm and quick mind carry them through situations his social skills cannot. Official oversight The government and Ducal Court would end the partnership if either discovered it. Potential sexual tension Kyrien Strong potential Situational and confrontational Kyrien's refusal to be steered threatens a skill she has internalized as part of her identity. Each failed attempt to produce a reaction can make his eventual attention feel more valuable and personally dangerous. Sherie uses language and calibrated flirtation to control the rhythm of an exchange. Kyrien answers with silence, literalism, or no usable reaction at all. Repeated negotiation could turn her professional frustration into sexual tension without making them compatible or displacing Kyrien's eventual relationship with Lynleit. Potential sexual tension Felix Author-confirmed direction Gradual familiarity, uneven recognition Sherie enjoys directing an exchange, while Felix teases back and complicates her control. As their work repeatedly overlaps, she finds room to become theatrical, petty, ridiculous, or openly delighted without losing his respect. She may recognize their intimate potential before he does. His fixation on Lynleit can hurt despite his responsive attention; her confidence does not remove disappointment, boundaries, or doubt about whether he sees her clearly. She gradually recognizes the seriousness beneath his jokes and becomes someone around whom he need not always entertain. Social play is something she enjoys off duty too. An unexpected response makes her attend to the emotional change in Felix and in the exchange, without guaranteeing that she understands its cause. They have no meaningful personal relationship at the story's opening. Sherie's diplomatic responsibilities increasingly overlap with Felix's work around Lynleit and MSF, bringing repeated encounters before either chooses closeness. Familiarity, respect, private jokes, and a compatible rhythm develop gradually. Her confident, playful dominance meets his expressiveness, improvisation, and willingness to challenge her. Humor, visible enjoyment, mutual provocation, and occasional reversals carry into affection and eventual adult intimacy. Care becomes particularly revealing when one stops performing and the other remains attentive. Readers can notice Felix building intimacy's foundations with Sherie while still imagining it with Lynleit; narration need not explain that contradiction. The later teasing challenge to Lynleit remains, but it neither starts their familiarity nor reduces Sherie's interest to winning him. This differs from Lynleit's strategic recruitment of Kyrien and their quieter recognition through restrained attention, protected secrets, and gradually accepted vulnerability. Both couples remain subplots beneath the political and supernatural story. The direction is confirmed; particular encounters, recognition, boundaries, and chronology remain unwritten. Sherie

entries.title: Sherie: Motivations
entries.subtitle: Diplomat in training and covert negotiator
entries.text: Sherie: Motivations Diplomat in training and covert negotiator Become a diplomat capable of turning Drake's strategic understanding into alliances, while tracing the suspected coup without exposing MSF cooperation. Sherie

entries.title: Sherie: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Diplomat in training and covert negotiator
entries.text: Sherie: Strengths and weaknesses Diplomat in training and covert negotiator Sherie teases and provokes mischief even off duty. She is quick to read someone's mood, relationships, and standing in a group; an unexpected reply makes her reconsider the exchange she thought she understood. She can draw out information without making a person feel interrogated and keep a difficult conversation going. With Felix she can be theatrical, petty, ridiculous, or openly delighted without losing his respect. As she gets to know him, she also learns when his jokes conceal something serious. Social play She enjoys teasing and provoking mischief even when nobody needs to be persuaded or impressed. Quietness usually means she feels unwell or uncomfortable. Emotional attention An unexpected response draws her attention to what changed in the person and in the atmosphere of the whole exchange. Persuasive judgment A useful agreement reached for the wrong reason feels like a success she cannot safely repeat. She may joke that she failed successfully while reconsidering her understanding of the other person. ENFJ strong Fe Confirmed Sherie

entries.title: Tien: Biography
entries.subtitle: Mercenary assassin and secret bodyguard
entries.text: Tien: Biography Mercenary assassin and secret bodyguard Helena secretly hires Tien, a professional mercenary and assassin, as her bodyguard and to remove her enemies. Helena deploys Tien against Lynleit and Kyrien as MSF's internal conflict leaves official channels behind. Tien and Kyrien become direct operational rivals because both begin as concealed assets serving handlers with opposing interests. Their functions overlap, but Tien exists primarily to remove Helena's enemies quietly and cleanly. His covert work for Helena puts him in repeated opposition to Kyrien. Works as a mercenary and assassin. Becomes Helena's concealed bodyguard. Opposes Kyrien during the struggle over MSF. Continues removing threats to Helena. Tien

entries.title: Yulia: Biography
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Biography Criminology student and procedural investigator Yulia and Hiyu study criminology at the same university. She stands at the top of the class through discipline, detail, and command of established method, while Hiyu makes his reputation through personal investigations that ignore the path everyone else was taught to follow. Their interaction is often painful to observe: he chases another possibility, she develops another headache, and neither notices how accustomed they are becoming to the other's company. Hiyu concludes that magic may be involved in the park disappearances despite not knowing that magic actually exists. Yulia considers the theory absurd, but joins his attempt to enter the quarantine partly to prove him wrong and partly because she does not trust him to remain safe alone. Inside the park, Yulia's meticulous observation remains valuable, but ordinary criminological protocol cannot tell her what rules the environment follows. Her attachment to Hiyu becomes a second vulnerability because protecting him can pull her deeper into a danger neither of them understands. Their original aversion gradually becomes dependence and then unacknowledged romantic tension. Yulia refuses to name it, while Hiyu remains so absorbed in ideas that he does not understand why her company has become necessary to him. Excels at criminology through careful method. Accompanies Hiyu to challenge his theory and keep him safe. Encounters events her training cannot explain. Becomes increasingly attached to Hiyu despite their disagreements. Yulia

entries.title: Yulia: Conflicts
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Conflicts Criminology student and procedural investigator Unfamiliar evidence Her training offers no established procedure for what happens in the park. Yulia

entries.title: Yulia: Connections
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Connections Criminology student and procedural investigator Hiyu Her opposite in method and temperament. He generates possibilities she would never entertain, while she gives his ideas evidentiary discipline. Over time, irritation becomes an attachment neither understands clearly. An investigation without rules Yulia can master a known procedure, but the park confronts her with evidence whose governing categories have not yet been admitted to exist. Potential sexual tension Hiyu Emerging arc Mutual, unequally conscious Hiyu irritates her into sustained attention. She keeps arguing, correcting, and following because his ideas have already occupied more of her mind than she wants to admit. Suppressed attraction can sharpen both her impatience and her awareness of his physical presence. A possible scene has them lean over the same evidence or reach for the same document while arguing. Yulia notices their proximity first; Hiyu continues the theory. Another possible beat has him keep turning toward her usual place while investigating alone. These are staging suggestions for their established attraction arc, not completed encounters or an established sexual relationship. Her objections must remain genuine, and the investigation must still matter. Yulia

entries.title: Yulia: Motivations
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Motivations Criminology student and procedural investigator Keep Hiyu alive, test his impossible theory honestly, and preserve enough reliable evidence to understand what ordinary criminology cannot explain. Yulia

entries.title: Yulia: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Strengths and weaknesses Criminology student and procedural investigator Yulia is reliable, meticulous, and most comfortable with evidence she can test against an established procedure. Hiyu's eureka moments give her a headache. She follows him anyway, checking his leaps and having to consider possibilities her usual methods would exclude. Procedural rigor She is at the top of her criminology class because she applies method consistently, respects chains of evidence, and notices when a required step has been skipped. Detail verification Yulia is strongest when a theory must be tested against the record, an observation must be preserved accurately, or an exciting conclusion must survive patient scrutiny. Reluctant loyalty She complains, resists, and wishes she were elsewhere, yet still goes with Hiyu when leaving him alone would place him in greater danger. ISTJ strong Si Confirmed Yulia

entries.title: Yulia: Tradecraft
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Tradecraft Criminology student and procedural investigator Academic strength Classical criminological method Yulia follows evidence handling, observation, reconstruction, and procedural discipline with a consistency Hiyu does not naturally possess. Team function Verification and correction She tests Hiyu's intuitive threads, separates useful anomalies from noise, and gives their investigations a record another person could actually follow. Failure condition Procedure without precedent The quarantined park is especially dangerous because its supernatural conditions do not respect the categories or safety assumptions on which her strongest methods depend. Yulia

entries.title: Arc 0: Households and the Becoming of MSF · v1
entries.subtitle: Prequel Development
entries.text: Arc 0: Households and the Becoming of MSF · v1 Prequel Development A tentative, Fionn-centered prequel outline: changing households, school years, MSF, and the younger cast’s unfinished habits. Arc 0: Households and the Becoming of MSF Status and scope This is a tentative prequel direction, not a fixed chronology or a completed account of MSF's founding. Arc 0 is a separate life period centered on Fionn, his household, and the development of MSF. The younger cast's high-school years provide parallel formation stories beneath that adult narrative. Exact dates, ages, institutional milestones, and school arrangements remain undecided. The Arc 0 outline collects its sparse scene anchor. No separate prequel Chapter is established yet. Fionn's story Fionn needs objectives, friendships, political obligations, weaknesses, and decisions that do not exist solely to explain his daughter. Follow him as a widower, father, professional, political actor, and man able to love again. His remarriage and his work should affect each other through concrete pressures rather than parallel exposition. MSF should become recognizable through people solving immediate problems. Temporary arrangements, practical necessity, threats, institutional failures, loyalties, and compromises may harden into lasting practices. Do not assign a founding date, invent a precursor organization, or assume that nothing called MSF existed before these years. The distinction between founding and later restructuring needs an author decision. Two households Lynleit, Fionn, and Helena Lynleit's mother died while she was still a junior schooler. The move from Turon to Vilen and her third-floor condition retain that existing chronology. Arc 0 can explore the continuing grief during her teenage years without moving the death or relocation into high school. The proposed domestic arc follows a household rebuilding after loss. Helena's arrival changes meals, seating, schedules, private conversations, rooms, and who can interrupt Fionn. Lynleit may understand that Helena cannot replace her mother while reacting as though a familiar gesture has erased something. Her fear concerns memory as much as possession of her father's attention. Let Helena genuinely give Fionn companionship. Lynleit then has to recognize a legitimate place for someone she resents. An apology, accepting help, or admitting Helena was right are possible scenes, not established events. Do not rewrite Helena's later actions as inevitable from her first entrance. Ordinary father-daughter familiarity matters: a late meal, an argument about school, waiting while he works, a manipulation he recognizes immediately, or discovering that he does not know an answer. Not every conversation needs a lesson or a later callback. Kyrien and his family The proposed teenage arc gives Kyrien a mother and sister whom he tries to protect after his father's death. Their names, ages, circumstances, and present-day status remain open. Show their ordinary life before the loss: meals, arguments, unwanted chores, jokes, and someone expecting him home. His father's death makes lineage a practical burden before he has the resources or authority to carry it. Money, legal standing, inherited danger, dismissive officials, and relatives are candidate pressures, not confirmed incidents. His mother and sister must retain their own judgment and sometimes reject his interference. The useful conflict is between responsibility and actual capacity. Accepting help, listening, or standing down can cost him more pride than a fight. Institutions may include people acting reasonably who still cannot help his family. Avoid making either solitary defiance or official procedure a universal answer. Adolescence and developing habits Young Lynleit should make mistakes her adult self has learned to hide. Curiosity, political awareness, competitiveness, family privilege, immature manipulation, and visible grief may coexist. Young Kyrien can be easier to read, angrier, more trusting, and quicker to mistake determination for resources. Neither is the finished adult in school clothes. The proposed contrast is specific: Lynleit learns to keep important people near after loss; Kyrien learns to function when alone. Proximity can support loyalty or become possessiveness. Independence can support survival or make help difficult to accept. These are development directions to test in scenes, not explanations for every adult action. Kyrien's whiskey flask is established adult equipment. Arc 0 may explore its beginnings through his father, an older relative, imitation, inheritance, or a difficult night. None of these origins is selected. The habit may begin awkwardly and become a measured private ritual. Do not depict alcohol as medical treatment or as the source of his competence. School and the ensemble Use classmates, family backgrounds, examinations, rivalries, meals, clubs, and ordinary boredom to make the younger ensemble socially alive. Do not assign all current characters to the same school or generation. Kyrien's later introduction to the Magi world remains intact: magical schooling and doctrine belong to characters who already have access to them, not automatically to him. For young Magi, lessons, exercises, history, doctrine, and unequal access to training can show how their institutions describe themselves. Teachers may be sincere yet transmit omissions or mistaken assumptions. A lesson is evidence of what students were taught, not automatic confirmation of the world's underlying truth. Talent should create expectations and mistakes as well as prestige. Friendships and rivalries may change without every classmate becoming an important enemy. Warmth, adolescent certainty, humor, family affection, and small victories should coexist with class, political pressure, magical privilege, and threats the adults cannot always contain. Optional forgotten encounter A brief teenage encounter between Lynleit and Kyrien remains optional. A waiting room, station, shop, school event, or corridor could let two exhausted adolescents irritate each other and inadvertently challenge a defensive assumption. No venue, dialogue, or meeting is confirmed. If used, keep it non-romantic. No secret relationship, destiny framing, promise, or compulsory later recognition follows. It must not give Fionn a meaningful relationship with adult Kyrien or give Kyrien early knowledge of magic. The adult interrogation remains their first proper meeting. Ending and retrospective effect Arc 0 need not run directly into Arc 1. A household equilibrium, departure, graduation, meal, or early MSF assignment could close the formative period. These are alternatives, not an ending montage. Let later knowledge change the reader's experience of ordinary places and habits. Avoid announcing which object or conversation will matter. Fionn never properly knows the adult Kyrien who becomes important to Lynleit; do not manufacture that missing relationship to comfort the reader. The prequel must not reveal the future child. Questions before Chapters Which MSF changes occur in these years, and what already exists beforehand? When does Fionn remarry relative to the move and Lynleit's school years? How old is Kyrien when his father dies, and what happens to his mother and sister? Which younger characters overlap in age and schooling? Which origin, if any, belongs to the flask? Does the forgotten encounter happen at all? The Nasu audit favors the conflict between useful institutions and the households affected by their decisions. Its restraint here is to keep the candidate incidents optional rather than turn a development discussion into a finished history. Author's Desk

entries.title: Archive Audit: 12 September 2026 · v1
entries.subtitle: Editorial Audit
entries.text: Archive Audit: 12 September 2026 · v1 Editorial Audit Approval-pending findings on canon consistency, chronology, prose, character development, reader knowledge, and responsive design. No audit actions have been implemented. Archive Audit: 12 September 2026 Status and scope Findings and proposals only. The author has not approved implementation of the actions below. Today's character clarifications have been integrated separately in the Cognition and Physical Competence reference. That integration does not authorize the revisions proposed here. Jump to consistency and chronology, story and writing, UI and reading, writer workflow, or recommended order. The review covered the current public pages, 18 profiles, 8 default Chapters, 24 current Moments, 14 registered documents, World records, shared registries, editorial ledgers, search, navigation, and version handling. Current narrative text received the closest editorial review. Historical revisions were checked for separation and sampled for context, not treated as current canon or exhaustively line-edited. Original artwork and audio were not altered. Automated browser checks exercised 80 routes at 390, 1024, and 1440 pixels in Chromium and WebKit: 480 views. They found no broken displayed images, page-wide horizontal overflow, or browser script errors. They did find two local text-overflow problems at 1024 pixels. Existing regression checks also covered navigation, search history, portrait thumbnails, relationship selection, and masonry hover stability. These are useful checks, not proof of complete accessibility or of behavior on a physical iPhone. Native Safari, VoiceOver, and live authenticated Page notes were not exercised by the local sweep. The Nasu audit was applied as the project's advisory framework, not as participation by Kinoko Nasu. Its principal influence is to require observable preparation, consequential limits, and earned exceptions without explaining away the mysteries. The author's established outcomes remain controlling. What is already working Natalia's worked examples give complex material a human scale. Her familiar teacher-student rhythm with Lynleit is worth preserving. The river's empty boats, submerged hands, lost jacket, and divided banks provide specific action and imagery rather than interchangeable supernatural danger. The Nameless Street has a strong sequence of objects and actions: balloon, crying, fence, body, smile, fall. Its uncertainty is productive. Mikhail and Lynleit's prolonged exchange has recognizable comic business and escalation. Length alone is not a reason to dismantle it. Sherie and Felix now have a relationship direction distinct from Lynleit and Kyrien. The difference should survive scene drafting. Shared registries, version snapshots, ordinary-looking entity links, flat styling, and the mobile archive toolbars provide a sound base. A wholesale site redesign is not justified by this audit. First priority: factual consistency and chronology R01. Lester's foundation entry has not caught up with his ontology Evidence: Hidden World Foundation still leaves open whether Lester was born a demiholumn or became one. His profile and the Holumn archive expressly reject an ordinary discoverable transformation as the explanation. The older wording reopens a route the author closed. Proposed action: Version and update the foundation document to preserve intrinsic contradiction, the limits of human comprehension, and Natalia's recognition. Keep questions about his capabilities and observable biography open. Do not invent an origin event. Decision needed: Implementation approval only; the governing author decision already exists. R02. The Drowned Choir's stated boundary is broader than the scene supports Evidence: HI-003's countermeasure summary says the hands cannot reach through the river surface. Maren appears to be pulled from the boat before she is in the water, but the blocking does not explain the first grip under that broad restriction. The incident's fuller description instead locates the impassable boundary beneath water-walking Lynleit. HI-003 also says the dead speak through the girl, although the encounter presents her as silent. Proposed action: Distinguish the observed boundary under Lynleit from a universal restriction on the hands. Check the source of the claim about speaking before retaining it as fact. Preserve the Choir and leviathan as separate Holumns. Decision needed: Approval to reconcile the wording; author confirmation if the boundary is meant to have a broader mechanism or the Choir has an established voice outside this encounter. R03. The interrogation outline contains stale exposition and repeated entry Evidence: After the Failed Attempt introduces Lynleit's entrance twice in successive paragraphs and says her authority has not been explained. Her profile already names the MSF transfer clause. An explanation deliberately withheld from Kyrien is different from an unresolved explanation in the archive. Proposed action: Remove the repeated entrance and align the outline's account of what is known with the owning records. Preserve the protected politician, the danger to Lynleit, her concealed knowledge, and the coercive initial arrangement. Do not invent interrogation dialogue merely to fill the gap. Decision needed: Implementation approval only for the consistency edit; drafting the full encounter is a separate action. R04. Some reciprocal or absolute claims need a source decision Evidence: The World index says Natalia was Lynleit's favourite teacher. Natalia's profile and the Academy Moment additionally call Lynleit Natalia's favourite student. Those are separate claims. Kyrien's later intelligence work is described as mastered completely, which exceeds a bounded account of competence. Proposed action: Confirm whether the favourite-student relationship is reciprocal. Replace unsupported absolutes with the specific work a character can accomplish, without reducing established competence. Apply the same source check to current records rather than treating every old sentence as an author decision. Decision needed: Confirm Natalia's preference if it is not already in an authoritative source. No new weaknesses should be invented to balance the wording. R05. Approximate chronology still looks more fixed than it is Evidence: Doom's approximate phase appears in the single ordered timeline after the political settlement. The text says its relation to surrounding phases is unfixed, but the visual order suggests otherwise. The flask's unknown origin receives an Arc 0 chronology entry labelled Family history even though its source and beginning remain open. The Nameless Street shares the Cardiff/Academy phase without establishing its exact relation to the journeys. Proposed action: Display approximate ranges, concurrent strands, and genuinely unplaced entries without forcing a single exact sequence. Keep the confirmed order of the hotel refuge, Doom, park encounter, later intimacy, pregnancy, and Arc 2. Remove an unearned period assignment from unknown item history; preserve stable links and flexible numbering. Decision needed: Approval for the presentation and metadata work. Exact dates, durations, and the relationship of Doom to political milestones remain author decisions. R06. Reveal order needs its own record, distinct from event order Evidence: Profiles, timelines, incident explanations, and Chapter tables contain different levels of knowledge about the first missing person, Fionn's death, the coat, the Cult connection, and Lynleit's children. The reader understanding the son is not the same event as Kyrien finding out. The current Cult naming follows the approved later Doom revisions and should not be silently returned to the earlier implied-only treatment. Proposed action: Track when an event occurs, when the reader can infer or learn it, and when each relevant character knows it. Begin with the small set of major secrets already established. Preserve the author's current revision decisions and leave undetermined revelations blank. Decision needed: Approve the model; choose any still-undecided revelation dates or audiences only when the story supplies them. Story, prose, and reader comprehension R07. Decide how much the archive should spoil for a first-time reader Evidence: The Story timeline exposes the first missing person's causal role before the Chapters. Preface tables reveal outcomes before the prose, and profiles span later life periods. These are useful writer references but can remove discovery from the reading experience. Proposed action: Keep the required preface tables, but offer a clear reading mode or a collapsed spoiler summary. Keep the complete writer view available. Separate intended chronology from recommended reading order rather than pretending the archive is already a finished novel. Decision needed: Whether this site should support spoiler-conscious reading at all, and whether that or the writer view should be the default. No spoilers have been hidden during this audit. R08. Draft status and Chapter coverage need clearer presentation Evidence: The catalog places 141-word and 225-word placeholders beside developed scenes of roughly 1,400 to 3,600 words. The status badges exist, but all entries share sequential Chapter labels and the same reader architecture. The Name Left Behind introduces a future-dated record about Fionn and self-altering archives without a matching Moment. Before the First Bell also lacks a linked Moment. Proposed action: Make outlines, drafted scenes, canon drafts, and writer gaps distinguishable in catalog filtering and reader headers. Add missing Moment links where the material is accepted. Keep the invented archive incident outside shared canon until accepted or explicitly retired; do not delete its historical source. Decision needed: Whether to keep and develop The Name Left Behind, or retain it only as an unused outline. Creating a Moment must not automatically ratify its inventions. R09. The main political and supernatural plot needs more scene work Evidence: The central recruitment remains an outline. Fionn's murder, the refuge, reclamation of MSF, the Cardiff moral conflict, and the Academy rescue mostly exist as planning records rather than Chapters. Doom has received substantially more dialogue and revision work than those turning points. Proposed action: Prioritize a small sequence of main-plot scenes before adding further intimate milestones: the interrogation, a professional encounter showing Sherie and Felix, an operational consequence of Kyrien's preparation, and a scene exposing the pressure around Fionn. Draft only where facts are sufficient; request focused decisions for missing causes. Decision needed: Which scene to develop first. This is a proposal for writing work, not permission to manufacture the missing conspiracy or chronology. R10. Doom's recovery needs more visible support in the characters Evidence: Doom v7 carefully presents the proposed cure as uncertain, then explains categorically that the incomplete attempt and aftermath changed both identities enough. The particular change in Kyrien is less visible than the explanation of the mechanism. The final assurance risks doing work the preceding behavior should carry. Proposed action: Develop observable, non-graphic changes in attention, choice, or expectation on both sides, and review the transition in narrative viewpoint around the recovery. Preserve the incomplete attempt, the successful recovery, Kyrien's incomplete knowledge, Natalia's practical teaching, and Mikhail's comic exchange. Do not introduce a new ritual, completed sexual encounter, or guaranteed cure formula. Decision needed: Approval for a new revision and, if necessary, agreement on the particular changes each character undergoes. The outcome itself is not being reopened. R11. Recheck shown and inferred labels against specific evidence Evidence: The river preface interprets physical tells as attraction and the empty boats as evidence of the crews' fate. These may be intentional readings, but they are not equally certain deductions. Elsewhere explanatory narration makes material explicit that an older outline may have left inferred. The park contains a visible writer gap, which is a different status again. Proposed action: Attach each current table claim to the passage that supports it, soften claims where the evidence supports only a possibility, and distinguish facts supplied by the author from conclusions available inside the scene. Preserve the blue/purple reader key and neutral outline facts. An undrafted passage must not be presented as delivered evidence. Decision needed: Approval for the label and wording audit. Any change to a intended reveal itself needs the author's agreement. R12. Revise explanatory habits without flattening the voices Evidence: The interrogation repeats an entrance. Institutional headings repeatedly announce abstractions such as two purposes or three degrees of distance before explaining the actual subject. Some profile claims are broad verdicts. Several scenes use the same short denial, correction, and counter-correction rhythm, which can make different speakers converge. Proposed action: Perform a passage-level edit for repetition, focalization, abstract summary, and unnecessary justification. Keep productive comic repetition, prop business, domestic detail, and the author's approved extended banter. Distinguish Felix's generated alternatives from Hiyu's investigative hypotheses, Kyrien's observation from Reiner's procedural speech, and Lynleit's familiar irreverence from Sherie's social play. Use today's behavior as attention, not dialogue explaining a type. Decision needed: Approval for selected current documents and Chapters, preserving old published revisions. No imitation of another writer's prose is required. R13. The capability graphs still imply false precision and comparison Evidence: The Capability ledger already records Lester's Magecraft score despite his inherent demiholumn nature, Mikhail's missing counter-Magus distinction, and the mixing of Kyrien's later mastery with earlier competence. Exact numbers suggest calibrated comparisons that the canon does not yet support. Proposed action: First distinguish story period and type of capability. Separate trained magecraft, Church countermeasures, and inherent anomalous ability where comparison would otherwise mislead. Use a supported descriptive scale or an explicitly bounded graph model. Keep today's agility, endurance, precision, and trained competence independent of MBTI. Do not simply reduce high scores until shapes look balanced. Decision needed: Agreement on what the graph should compare. Specific training histories, failure limits, and supernatural costs remain open. R14. Supporting characters need decisions that belong to them Evidence: Tien is strongly defined by serving Helena and opposing Kyrien; Myka's danger and eventual success have more definition than her own decisions; the Cardiff disagreement identifies moral incompatibility without establishing the act that makes it unavoidable. Broad statements about competence or morality cannot yet carry those scenes. Proposed action: Develop one consequential choice, one dependency, and one credible limit for each character when their next scene is written. For Cardiff, identify the specific solution Mikhail accepts that Lynleit cannot accept. For Myka, establish something she does that affects her survival and later recruitment. Preserve specialist distinctions rather than giving every supporting character the protagonists' skills. Decision needed: Concrete author choices. The audit should not invent Mikhail's ethics, Myka's curriculum, or Tien's private loyalties. R15. Relationship direction needs evidence across ordinary work Evidence: Sherie and Felix's confirmed gradual direction is richer than the professional encounters currently drafted. Much intimacy guidance describes anticipated behavior. A hypothetical response to Sherie's hurt is not yet a scene. Lynleit and Kyrien's rescue and secrecy milestones are better documented than their mundane repeated contact. Proposed action: Give future main-plot scenes space for small, specific interactions that accumulate. Track established encounters separately from intended development. Preserve Felix's attachment to Lynleit while Sherie acquires significance of her own, and keep Lynleit's duty primary. Do not add a confession simply to complete an audit checklist. Decision needed: Approval to develop particular encounters, with chronology kept open where it is not fixed. R16. Foundational terms need a shorter route into the setting Evidence: Definitions of magic, magecraft, miracles, Holumns, identity, and suppression are distributed across World and Docs. Human singularity appears in Lester's account without a short local explanation of what the phrase permits the reader to understand. Institutional interpretations can sound like universal physical laws when read in isolation. Proposed action: Provide a concise entry point with links to owning definitions. Distinguish observed effects, institutional doctrine, and unanswered ontology. Cross-link existing explanations before adding another large foundational essay. Move public development prompts such as the Magiarchy page's Awaiting definition section into the editorial ledgers, while retaining honest statements about unknown phenomena. Preserve unknown mechanisms rather than filling them with invented technical language. Decision needed: Approval for organization and clearer wording; any new metaphysical definition requires author confirmation. UI and reading experience R17. Fix the two confirmed intermediate-width overflows Evidence: At 1024 pixels in both engines, the Director's House heading has about 199 pixels of content in a 162-pixel column. The Holumn definition's first explanation exceeds its local column as well. The house keeps a three-column hero until a 950-pixel breakpoint; its fixed side columns and padding leave the title too narrow. The Holumn layout nests another two-column grid inside an already constrained panel. Proposed action: Collapse these compositions according to available content width, reduce unsuitable fixed minimums, and allow long text to wrap. Test the full interval around the breakpoints and browser zoom. Preserve the distinct page designs and flat palette. Decision needed: Implementation approval only. Neither issue was fixed in this audit. R18. Restore visible life-period context to profile artwork Evidence: The portrait carousel updates Arc information in image alt text, thumbnail titles, and a screen-reader-only status. A sighted touch user cannot reliably identify the displayed Arc 2 artwork from those labels. Catalog cards do display an Arc label. Proposed action: Add a small visible era label only when relevant, without restoring arrow buttons, image counters, a large overlay background, or obstructed artwork. Keep image-half taps, dragging, swiping, and thumbnails. Decision needed: Implementation approval and placement preference only if the author wants to choose it. R19. Remove misleading empty choices and distinguish music concepts Evidence: All 33 current Gallery records use unspecified location, while the location selector still offers several named places with no matching images. Music has one playable recording and four concepts; the category architecture now matches Characters, but concepts still occupy the same prominent browsing space as playable work. Proposed action: Derive available filter choices and counts from records, without inventing locations. Keep future metadata support. Offer a straightforward playable-only option or separate concepts from recordings, retaining the custom banner player and both downloads. Do not relabel a concept as available. Decision needed: Approval for filtering improvements; keeping concepts visible by default is a design choice, not a canon question. R20. Reduce navigation work in long readers Evidence: A Chapter reader places the full horizontal story timeline before the actual chapter. Long documents and profiles require substantial scrolling; the desktop layout also has an independently scrolling content pane and a Page notes column. These structures work, but they compete with sustained reading. Proposed action: Offer a compact or collapsible timeline in reader views, retain the full timeline in catalogs, add useful section navigation, and preserve back navigation and scroll position. Improve the use of the right column without adding a permanent left sidebar. Do not remove the timeline or breadcrumbs. Decision needed: Approval for reader-focused design work. A default reading mode should be chosen together with R07. R21. The local WebKit run is not native Safari certification. Proposed action: Test F/M/S notes with keyboard and assistive technology, verify text contrast and touch targets, test map and portrait interaction under zoom and reduced motion, and confirm that drag gestures do not trap vertical scrolling. Add only the controls required to make the existing interactions usable. Decision needed: Approval for the accessibility pass. A physical Safari check requires access to the target environment; until then, report that limit explicitly. Writer workflow and cohesion R22. Make the ledgers reflect evidence and actual unresolved decisions Evidence: The contradictions ledger records no unresolved contradiction despite the source drift in R01 and the boundary problem requiring review in R02. The capability ledger already holds several concerns that have not changed the graph. Confidence percentages help scan the questions but do not explain what evidence would close them. Proposed action: Register verified conflicts after approval, link them to their owning sources and required follow-up surfaces, and group questions by the decision that would answer them. Retain the required confidence and resolution bars. Separate ordinary missing information, deliberate mysteries, and genuinely incompatible statements. Do not resolve a deliberate contradiction in Lester's existence as though it were a continuity error. Decision needed: Approval for ledger maintenance. Answers remain the author's unless already established. R23. Reduce duplicated explanations and conflicting maintenance guidance Evidence: Suppression doctrine and basic ontology are explained in several World and Docs records. They serve different readers, but repeated full explanations increase drift risk. The maintenance charter still describes entity links as ordinary prose until hover, while the recorded design preference is that they remain ordinary-looking in every state, with usable keyboard focus. Large shared style sections and repeated navigation markup also make local adjustments hard to reason about. Proposed action: Keep one owning definition and concise contextual explanations elsewhere. Reconcile guidance wording, document the owner of each recurring component, and refactor only where tests demonstrate equivalent behavior. Do not force the individually designed World pages into one template or undertake a framework migration. Decision needed: Approval for focused maintenance and source consolidation, not a site rebuild. R24. Extend regression checks to the failures this audit found Evidence: Existing checks passed while the 1024-pixel text overflows and Lester's foundation drift remained. A single explicitly registered v1 document also exposed a mismatch between search URL generation and the expected version URL during today's integration; the new reference follows the existing implicit-v1 convention instead. Proposed action: Add tests for internal text overflow at intermediate widths, explicit single-version documents, visible artwork era labels, and selected cross-record canon invariants. Retain current checks for snapshots, search history, links, gradients, masonry, and mobile navigation. Keep prose judgment and unresolved canon out of false pass/fail assertions. Decision needed: Implementation approval only for tests and demonstrated defects; do not turn a hypothesis into a test that forces it to become canon. Recommended order after approval 1. Consistency and verified defects: R01-R05, R17-R19, R22-R24, excluding questions that need an author decision. 2. Reading and knowledge structure: R06-R08, R11, R16, R20-R21. 3. Prose, capability, and scene development: R09-R10, R12-R15, with a bounded plan for each revision. The decisions most likely to need the author directly are the archive's spoiler policy, the future of The Name Left Behind, reciprocal favourite-student status, exact chronology still left open, capability limits, the concrete Cardiff moral conflict, and any new scene proposed to demonstrate a relationship or a talent. Approval of cleanup alone must not be interpreted as permission to decide those facts. Archive Review

Original artwork and audio were not altered. Automated browser checks exercised 80 routes at 390, 1024, and 1440 pixels in Chromium and WebKit: 480 views. They found no broken displayed images, page-wide horizontal overflow, or browser script errors. They did find two local text-overflow problems at 1024 pixels. Existing regression checks also covered navigation, search history, portrait thumbnails, relationship selection, and masonry hover stability. These are useful checks, not proof of complete accessibility or of behavior on a physical iPhone. Native Safari, VoiceOver, and live authenticated Page notes were not exercised by the local sweep. The Nasu audit was applied as the project's advisory framework, not as participation by Kinoko Nasu. Its principal influence is to require observable preparation, consequential limits, and earned exceptions without explaining away the mysteries. The author's established outcomes remain controlling. Natalia's reciprocal favourite-student status, a broader river boundary, and any voice outside the encounter.
