entries.subtitle: Visual Production Standard
entries.text: Character Image Production · v9 Visual Production Standard Template-first production and approved-image validation after retirement of archived production sources. Character Image Production Templates come first Using approved templates is a required first step for future character image generation, not an optional finishing check. Writers and agents must inspect the relevant Gallery production resources and the target character's approved artwork before preparing a generation request. Use the actual reference images as inputs wherever the generation tool supports them. A written description or recollection of an image is not a substitute for an available visual reference. If a required reference cannot be accessed or supplied, explain the limitation and agree on an alternative with the author before generating. Anima's three roles Anima, unofficially nicknamed Inanna, has three distinct roles: the author's personal mascot, a symbolic expression of the project's tonal world, and the female anatomical production template. None makes her a character in story canon. Thematic Direction owns the symbolic role and distinguishes it from the Cult of Inanna. Her black, red, and gold palette, mask, ritual jewelry, exposed skin, flowing fabric, ornaments, and dancer-like presentation belong to her mascot design. Another character needs an independent design reason to share them. Anatomy does not prescribe clothing, personality, sexuality, sexual behavior, religious or cultural identity, social role, temperament, or a hierarchy of beauty. Female anatomical baseline Anima's approved T-pose sets are the shared anatomical starting point for future female-character design and the gold-standard presentation for their T-poses. Use them together with the target character's approved references. Black-and-gold template, front and back Red-drapery template, front and back The future male template is named Animus. No male template artwork is registered yet. Template mascots may also have unofficial nicknames; keep official names and nicknames distinct. These production identities do not establish story characters or a connection to the story's Cult of Inanna. Design individual bodies through deliberate differences from that baseline. Record the target's established height, build, musculature, body composition, proportions, age or life period, lifestyle, training, physical history, and distinguishing appearance. Differences are not improvements or deficiencies. Shared structural continuity does not require identical bodies, and an existing approved design must not be reshaped merely to resemble Anima. The template is a production tool, not in-world anatomy lore. Its costume, face, accessories, hair, color palette, sensual presentation, and cultural styling do not transfer automatically. Standardized T-pose presentation is useful for reference sheets; it does not impose the mascot's dancer-like gestures on ordinary character artwork. Reference selection and design continuity Start with the target character's established face, hair, clothing, physical features, and life period. Use a production template to guide pose and presentation while preserving that identity. For other character images, consult applicable templates and approved artwork without forcing an action scene or portrait into a T-pose. Use front, back, and other available views from the same design version together. Keep alternate costumes and revisions distinct. Do not blend incompatible versions or transfer later-Arc features into an earlier incarnation without the author's direction. If a template and a confirmed character feature conflict, preserve the confirmed feature. If the intended design or version is unclear, ask the author rather than inventing a resolution. Generation brief Record which references the request uses, what each controls, and which character-specific differences must be preserved. Distinguish the pose/proportion template from the character-identity reference. State the intended view and design version, and identify any approved change explicitly. Use this compact brief when designing a new female character or revising an existing one: Identity and period: character, approved incarnation, reference filenames, and matching-version views. Baseline: the chosen Anima set and the anatomy or pose presentation it supplies. Individual body: established height, build, musculature, body composition, and proportions, with their source. Include age, lifestyle, training, or physical history only where these establish a visible design requirement; do not derive a measurement from a personality type or profession. Separate design: face, hair, costume, accessories, palette, and pose language specific to the character. Keep the contemporary setting in view. Unspecified features: identify genuine gaps instead of inventing weight, measurements, age, or medical history. Resolve consequential ambiguity with the author before generation. For example, Lynleit's confirmed 169 cm slender build and tailored blue-and-black wardrobe remain hers. The reference does not replace them with Anima's proportions or red drapery. Consult Hidden World Foundation when changing material or historical styling. Visual review and publication Descriptive asset filenames Every image or other file pasted or attached for site integration receives a descriptive filename before publication. This applies to images, music, documents, models, and other downloadable assets. Use lowercase ASCII words separated by hyphens, with the subject or title, purpose, and relevant confirmed variant, Arc, view, or revision. Preserve the actual extension. For Anima, use anima-t-pose-black-gold-front.png , anima-t-pose-black-gold-back.png , anima-t-pose-red-drapery-front.png , and anima-t-pose-red-drapery-back.png . Do not publish random clipboard IDs or generic export names. Keep matching views and formats on consistent stems, follow the existing character-art naming conventions, and do not invent details just to fill a filename. Explicit author-requested filenames take precedence. Preserve dependency-sensitive names inside source projects unless all affected references can be updated safely. Backlog text archives follow their own timestamp rule. Rename without changing file contents, verify original bytes, avoid collisions, and update every registry entry, preview source, download, and search reference. Stable resource-page links should continue working. Separating supplied T-pose sheets Use Anima's actual portrait canvas, 1122 × 1402 pixels, when preparing separate T-pose views. It is approximately 4:5, not square. Match this aspect ratio without stretching or reshaping the character to fit it. When the author requests a sheet to be split, preserve the complete original byte-for-byte in the source archive and create separately named front/back derivatives. Retain all hair, hands, clothing, accessories, and feet. Keep the same scale and vertical alignment within each pair; add background padding where necessary. Do not redraw anatomy or manufacture missing detail. Lettering outside the figure may be omitted from the separated presentation, with that distinction recorded and the original sheet retained. Measure the split and inspect the result rather than blindly halving a sheet through touching fingertips. Record crop and padding decisions while sources remain available. Keep matching versions together and do not infer an Arc from a design version. Author-approved anatomy corrections Splitting a sheet does not authorize changes to its anatomy. When the author explicitly requests a correction, preserve both the original sheet and the previous separated views. Publish the correction as a separately named derivative, such as char-felix-t-pose-v1-arm-corrected-front.png , under the same design-version record. Keep source sheets and superseded views in the archive for reproduction, not in the public download list. Publish only the current front/back reference files unless the author requests other formats. For unequal T-pose arms, compare visible shoulder, sleeve, wrist, and fingertip positions on both sides and both views. Clothing folds are not reliable evidence of an elbow joint. Measure each design independently; do not force different characters into one reach or change their face, torso, clothing design, or life period. Use local geometric adjustments when preserving the drawing is important. A whole-figure stretch or regenerated face is not an arm-length repair. Retain the template canvas and common scale within each pair. Inspect sleeve joins, fingers, padding, front/back consistency, and visible fingertip spans. These are drawing corrections, not new canonical body measurements. Rear-view hands Judge hand orientation from the camera and pose, not by mirroring a front-view silhouette. In these palms-down T-poses, the rear camera sees the little-finger edge; the thumb sits on the far side and is largely occluded. Check all four extended fingers, their overlapping contours, the hidden thumb's plausible attachment, and wrist continuity. A thumb-like projection must not replace the little finger. For an explicitly requested hand correction, preserve approved arm lengths and use matching views. Publish reviewed hand regions on the unchanged base. Compare pixels outside the edit while both versions remain available; anatomical correctness requires visual inspection. Review checklist Compare the result with the references before registration or publication. Check identity, proportions, silhouette, costume details, pose, and front/back consistency. Inspect hands, feet, accessories, and occluded areas for discrepancies. Treat an unexplained generated difference as something to review, not as new canon. Check the recorded individual differences as deliberately as the shared anatomy. Reject accidental bodily sameness, imported mascot styling, and ancient-fantasy drift in otherwise contemporary designs. Do not turn a model's invented difference into a new character fact. Preserve approved source files. Register production views as matching-version siblings with original downloads and descriptive metadata. Keep unapproved outputs outside the published archive. Follow the production intake workflow in the archive maintenance charter. Retired production sources At the author’s request, backlog/archive was purged on 20 September 2026. Source sheets, intermediate corrections, and processed prompts remain recoverable through Git history, not in the working tree. The old source-dependent correction tools were retired. Historical document commands no longer apply. gallery/t-pose-approved.json records the current approved T-pose files. node scripts/verify-t-pose-assets.mjs verifies hashes, dimensions, and registered views without regenerating artwork. Update this baseline only after inspecting an author-requested revision. Future intakes still preserve sources unless the author requests another purge. Author's Desk

entries.title: Character Intimacy and Sexuality Reference · v1
entries.subtitle: Writer's Character Reference
entries.text: Character Intimacy and Sexuality Reference · v1 Writer's Character Reference A writer-facing reference for each character's approach to closeness, desire, sexual initiative, and established, asymmetric, or potential sexual tension. Character Intimacy and Sexuality Reference A writer's reference to affection, attraction, initiative, and particular partners. Established events and working interpretations are distinguished below. The shared tension records attached to each profile track pairings as new scenes develop. How to read the profiles Established means confirmed by the author or present in the selected canon. Working interpretation means a possibility derived from current characterization, not an event or preference the story has established. Unresolved means there is not enough information to describe it. Doom Has an Address follows Version 3. Lynleit and Kyrien survive after an incomplete attempt at intimacy. Their first completed sexual encounter occurs later in Arc 1; its exact placement is unresolved. Lynleit Basis: Established relationship; later behavior partly interpreted Natural approach Lynleit notices other people's needs and often makes herself responsible for them. Her work comes first. She usually values openness, but talking about her own desire embarrasses her. With someone she trusts, she can be playful and enjoy drawing out a reaction. Sexual expression Her attempt with Kyrien in Doom Has an Address is irritable, awkward, and incomplete. After they recover, she repeatedly insists there is no reason to try again. The unread pages and her response to Natalia suggest otherwise. Natalia keeps the familiar examination routine and deliberate silences; Lynleit's increasingly emphatic denials prolong the subject she wants to close. Their later pattern makes Lynleit the more frequent initiator. She is more vocal than Kyrien and likes teasing his reserve. The precise staging of those later encounters remains subject to the author's review. With Kyrien She knows his failed assassination nearly harmed her. He never learns she was there. That withheld fact gives the interrogation a personal edge before there is any attraction. Card games during the river watches give them something to do together outside her orders. She asks for rematches, learns his held breath before a risk, and catches him watching her hands. He protects her water-walking secret. Their recovery in the park and the later hotel refuge remain non-sexual. He eventually stays when she can no longer compel him. When she asks what reward makes the danger worthwhile, he answers, "Because there's a battle to be fought." She cannot dismiss his persistence as obedience or explain it through a promise she made him. The curse brings an incomplete attempt at intimacy, then a recovery she will not explain. Their sexual relationship begins afterward and lasts long enough to acquire private jokes and ordinary habits. A later encounter takes place in her third-floor study-bedroom. Pregnancy follows near the Arc 2 transition, with its meaning left for the reader to recognize at the next arc's opening. Her later return revives their physical awareness, but Kyrien still does not know about their son. The consequences for renewed intimacy remain a separate question. Writing guardrail Let embarrassment occasionally make her unfair or difficult. Her competence does not require an explanation defending each awkward response. Kyrien Basis: Established relationship; later behavior partly interpreted Natural approach Kyrien is slow to trust and says little about what he feels. He notices discomfort, changes in routine, and what someone is trying to hide. Staying, making preparations, or keeping a secret can express his attachment. Sexual expression The incomplete attempt in Doom Has an Address leaves him puzzled. He sees a connection with their recovery but lacks Lynleit's explanation. In their later relationship he is quieter and initiates less often than she does. The working portrayal gives him sustained attention and practical habits afterward, such as bringing water or staying beside her. These are possibilities for scenes, not a required sequence. With Lynleit Their games provoke his need to win. Her ability to read him irritates him and draws his attention back to her. Her elegance and nerve also attract him. He does not explain his decision to stay as a romantic sacrifice. He wants the battle. The question of how much he is still trying to prove to his father remains open. When she refuses to discuss the attempted intimacy, he lets the subject rest without ceasing to wonder about it. Their later sexual relationship need not settle every disagreement or make him talkative. Writing guardrail Give his silence a context. He may be watching, withholding an answer, annoyed, or simply have nothing to say. Helena Basis: Established marriage; working intimate interpretation Natural approach Helena wants to be admitted into a partner's whole life. Fionn's secrecy makes her doubt what their marriage means to him. A possible private habit is testing how much attention she has without admitting that she needs reassurance. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. The working interpretation makes her attentive to whether a partner is distracted or withholding something. With Fionn Their attraction and domestic closeness coexist with his refusal to share his deepest secrets. He believes he is protecting her. She feels excluded from her own marriage. Writing guardrail Show what Fionn withholds and what Helena does about it. The narrator need not decide the legitimacy of her grievance for the reader. Fionn Basis: Established marriage; working intimate interpretation Natural approach Fionn provides for and protects the people he loves. He also decides what they should be allowed to know. Warmth does not make that habit disappear. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. A patient, measured approach fits his present characterization, but a scene is needed before it becomes a reliable pattern. With Helena He respects and desires Helena while withholding the hidden workings of MSF, the Magiarchy, and his succession arrangements. His belief that secrecy protects her does not resolve her resentment. Writing guardrail Include ordinary companionship where the story calls for it. Every private exchange need not become a demonstration of their failed trust. Yulia Basis: Established attraction arc; working sexual interpretation Natural approach Yulia accompanies Hiyu while complaining about the reasons for going. She checks details, remembers responsibilities, and keeps him from overlooking practical risks. Sexual expression No encounter is established. A quiet and initially cautious approach is plausible; it should be tested against actual scenes rather than treated as an automatic consequence of her reserve. With Hiyu They argue over the same evidence and remain close while trying to prove each other wrong. Yulia is likely to notice that proximity before Hiyu does. Her impatience can include attraction without making her objections false. The approved development direction gives her an earlier awareness of the attachment. Hiyu continues treating the exchange as an argument about the investigation. Writing guardrail Let her be genuinely annoyed. Irritation does not have to conceal desire every time. Hiyu Basis: Established attraction arc; working sexual interpretation Natural approach Hiyu keeps seeking the person whose criticism makes his ideas more interesting. He notices the intellectual need before he understands the personal one. Sexual expression No encounter is established. Curiosity and improvisation are possible extensions of his personality, not established sexual preferences. With Yulia He seeks her corrections while resisting them. One proposed recognition scene has him enjoy investigating alone at first, then keep turning toward the place where she should be. His obliviousness delays his understanding of her attention. It does not make every concern she raises invisible to him. Writing guardrail Give him reasons to listen that arise from the case as well as the relationship. Felix Basis: Established flirtation and asymmetric tension with Lynleit Natural approach Felix flirts, jokes, and watches the response. Serious feelings can be harder for him to state plainly than a playful advance. Sexual expression The working interpretation makes him communicative, playful, and comfortable initiating. His private behavior has not yet been established in a scene. With Lynleit and Sherie Lynleit deflects his advances while remaining his close friend. His attraction does not establish a matching desire on her side. Sherie can match his wit. Their similar habits allow them to keep flirting without saying anything definite. His attachment to Lynleit complicates Sherie's interest in him. Writing guardrail An unsuccessful joke, a change of subject, or a plain answer can distinguish his sincere attention from his usual performance. Reiner Basis: Established friendship; intimate life unresolved Natural approach Reiner shows care through consistency and preparation. A working interpretation gives him more ease with practical help than courtship. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. Privacy and a deliberate pace are possibilities to explore. With a specific partner No partner is established. His long-standing friendship with Lynleit is protective. Writing guardrail His reserve leaves room for warmth. It does not prescribe how every private encounter must unfold. Sherie Basis: Established personality and flirtation; sexual behavior unresolved Natural approach Sherie enjoys attention and praise. Flirting is also part of her diplomatic skill, used so often that it can make a sincere approach difficult to distinguish from a practiced one. Sexual expression A playful, verbally expressive approach is plausible. Her actual preferences remain unwritten. With Felix and Kyrien Kyrien is a potential source of tension because he does not give her the reactions she expects. Repeated negotiation could turn that frustration personal. No relationship between them is established. Felix responds readily and can answer her teasing in kind. After learning that Lynleit has slept with Kyrien, Sherie challenges Lynleit's continuing sense of responsibility for Felix: "What exactly is this? Do you imagine every man is your permanent responsibility? Felix is not your wounded soldier. If you refuse to have him, I may very well take him myself, you shameless hussy!" Lynleit objects to her playing with him. Sherie's interest includes competition with Lynleit, but whether it becomes lasting affection for Felix remains unresolved. This exchange belongs after Lynleit and Kyrien's later completed encounter, not immediately after Doom Has an Address. Writing guardrail Allow a sincere request to sound less polished than her diplomatic speech. Drake Basis: Working interpretation; partner unresolved Natural approach Drake may try to help by removing a practical burden while missing the reassurance a person wanted. This follows his established difficulty with social situations, but no intimate scene confirms it yet. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. Reserve and overthinking are possibilities, not a complete profile. With a specific partner No partner is established. His closest recorded relationships are his friendship with the Duke and his role as Sherie's uncle and teacher. Writing guardrail Awkward timing is more specific than treating him as generally unable to understand feelings. Heyk Basis: Survivor's history established; intimate life unresolved Natural approach The loss of his squad may affect how he responds to closeness. Withdrawal, protectiveness, or vigilance are possibilities to test in a particular scene. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. There is not enough evidence to decide how his grief affects desire or private comfort. With a specific partner No partner is established. Writing guardrail Do not assign the same trauma response to every encounter. The person, timing, and circumstances matter. Natalia Basis: Established tension with Lester; sexual behavior unresolved Natural approach Natalia values solitude and independent thought. Her work makes her accustomed to asking intimate questions as an examiner. Being personally involved can make that familiar method less useful. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. An observant and selective approach is a working interpretation. With Lester She examines his demiholumn condition and is attracted to him. He notices when her attention becomes personal and provokes her to act rather than continue observing. Their work keeps bringing them together. Neither the attraction nor an eventual encounter would answer all of her questions about his nature. Writing guardrail Let her be curious about something ordinary in him too. His anomalous nature need not account for all of her interest. Tien Basis: Occupational context established; intimate life unresolved Natural approach His work requires secrecy. Whether he carries the same habits into private relationships is not established. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. With a specific partner No partner is established. Helena is his employer and protected principal. Writing guardrail Do not turn an assassin's professional methods into a ready-made sexual personality. Lester Basis: Established tension with Natalia; personal history unresolved Natural approach Lester seeks direct experience and enjoys provoking Natalia. His response to being examined is part of their friction. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. His demiholumn nature alone cannot supply it. With Natalia He wants her attention as a man as well as an unusual case. Her analytical distance gives him something to provoke, while their shared work gives the attraction repeated contact. Writing guardrail His ordinary tastes, humor, and irritation should remain available alongside the mystery of his body. Inspector Leo Basis: Marriage established; private life unresolved Natural approach His patience as an investigator offers one possible starting point. The archive does not yet establish how he behaves with his spouse. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. With a specific partner Leo is married. His spouse is not yet described. He has no established sexual tension with Natalia and remains outside the Magi world. Writing guardrail Establish the marriage through a scene before projecting his police habits onto it. Father Mikhail Basis: Clerical role established; private life unresolved Natural approach His history, personal attachments, and vows are not yet defined. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. His blunt advice to Lynleit establishes how he speaks to her, not how he behaves with a partner. With a specific partner No partner is established. Writing guardrail Neither celibacy nor a hidden romance follows from the title Father. Myka Basis: Familial closeness established; romantic history unresolved Natural approach to closeness Myka confides in Natalia about studies and personal worries. Natalia checks on her and sometimes treats her like a daughter. With a specific partner No romantic partner or sexual profile is recorded. Archive-wide writing principles Preserve each character's work, loyalties, and immediate objective. Use recurring contact specific to the pair. Shared danger can intensify attraction but does not establish it by itself. Distinguish attention from attraction and attraction from a promised relationship. Let gestures, interruptions, and choices carry implications without narrating the conclusion again. A useful encounter may leave a disagreement, an unanswered question, or a changed habit. Keep interpretations separate from confirmed preferences. Revisit them when new scenes supply evidence. Established arc Mutual, slow to surface lynleit Lynleit Lynleit studies Kyrien first as a recruit whose failed attack nearly harmed her. Their card games make that scrutiny personal: she learns his tells and begins noticing his hands and breath. Later she attempts intimacy as a possible treatment for their shared curse, but remains interested after they survive without completing it. kyrien Kyrien Kyrien wants to beat Lynleit at cards and dislikes finding that she can read him. Her elegance and nerve also attract him. He stays because he wants the battle, then finds himself facing private questions that her orders cannot answer. After the attempted intimacy, she will not tell him why their curse disappeared. The interrogation, card games, protected secret, and voluntary decision to stay give this pairing different kinds of familiarity. In Doom Has an Address, an incomplete attempt at intimacy breaks the shared curse. Lynleit loses the excuse of treatment without losing her interest in Kyrien; he is left trying to understand what happened. Their sexual relationship begins later in Arc 1. Established asymmetry Felix overt, Lynleit deflecting lynleit Lynleit Felix's flirting belongs to a long friendship she refuses to reorganize around his advances. Her ease with him, combined with the repeated refusal, creates visible chemistry without requiring matching sexual intent. felix Felix Lynleit is one of the few people his charm cannot simply move into the response he wants. Familiar affection, physical ease, and repeated deflection keep his attraction active even when he respects the boundary she has made. The tension is easy for readers to recognize because it already has a social rhythm: he advances through jokes and flirtation, she ignores or redirects him, and neither abandons the closeness underneath the exchange. It does not need to become a relationship to remain real. Emerging arc Mutual, unequally conscious yulia Yulia Hiyu irritates her into sustained attention. She keeps arguing, correcting, and following because his ideas have already occupied more of her mind than she wants to admit. Suppressed attraction can sharpen both her impatience and her awareness of his physical presence. hiyu Hiyu Yulia is the critic whose resistance makes an idea worth pursuing. He becomes dependent on her attention before he understands that the dependence is personal, leaving him oblivious to tension that is already changing how he seeks her out. Their arguments repeatedly force proximity and attention. They lean over the same evidence, reach for the same document, and forget ordinary distance while trying to prove incompatible explanations. Yulia notices first and steps away; Hiyu continues the theory and wonders why she moved. Her anger becomes disproportionate when his recklessness makes the possibility of losing him real. Hiyu recognizes the bond through absence: an investigation without her corrections becomes less interesting, and he keeps turning toward the place where she should be. Yulia and Hiyu become intimate by learning to communicate through the noise they already create together. Strong potential Situational and confrontational kyrien Kyrien Sherie's charm is too deliberate to disarm him, but the precision behind it earns his attention. He is more likely to watch for the moment her performance fails than reward the performance itself. sherie Sherie Kyrien's refusal to be steered threatens a skill she has internalized as part of her identity. Each failed attempt to produce a reaction can make his eventual attention feel more valuable and personally dangerous. Sherie uses language and calibrated flirtation to control the rhythm of an exchange. Kyrien answers with silence, literalism, or no usable reaction at all. Repeated negotiation could turn her professional frustration into sexual tension without making them compatible or displacing Kyrien's eventual relationship with Lynleit. Established marriage Mutual, damaged by exclusion fionn Fionn Fionn's affection and desire for Helena are genuine. He separates bodily and domestic closeness from the secrets he believes he must carry alone, never understanding that this division changes what their intimacy means to her. helena Helena Helena experiences desire alongside the need to be admitted into Fionn's complete life. Physical familiarity can therefore intensify resentment: she can be close enough to know his body while remaining excluded from the truth governing him. Their sexual tension survives inside a real marriage because attraction and grievance occupy the same private space. The closer they become physically, the harder it is for Helena to accept that Fionn still decides which parts of himself she is permitted to know. Established tension Mutual, differently expressed natalia Natalia Lester is the living exception that Natalia cannot finish classifying. Her professional attention can become personal before she recognizes the change, especially when he interrupts an examination by noticing that she is watching him rather than the phenomenon around him. lester Lester Natalia's analytical distance gives Lester something unusually difficult to provoke. He enjoys forcing the reserved researcher into immediate experience, but the tension changes when he wants her attention to recognize the man rather than examine the demiholumn condition. Repeated cases bring Natalia's examination of Lester into conflict with his insistence on being treated as more than a case. He provokes her to act; she notices more than he expected. Their attraction does not answer her questions about his demiholumn nature. Emerging potential Mutual play, sincerity unresolved sherie Sherie Felix gives Sherie immediate wit, visible attention, and resistance that does not become hostility. She first tests him as play and competition, including whether his attention can be drawn away from Lynleit. The tension becomes personal when winning ceases to satisfy her and she begins wanting a response that is not produced by technique. felix Felix Sherie can match Felix's teasing without mistaking it for a complete confession. Her ability to see when he hides seriousness behind a joke gives him an opponent and possible partner who can enjoy the performance while still asking for something sincere. His unresolved feelings for Lynleit prevent Sherie from winning him by charm alone. Both use social ease as protection: Felix hides seriousness behind jokes, while Sherie hides vulnerability behind charm and diplomacy. Their chemistry is immediate, but similarity makes them capable of prolonged flirtation without honest movement. Sherie begins testing the friendship after learning that Lynleit has slept with Kyrien while still feeling responsible for Felix's affection. Her refusal to treat Felix as Lynleit's permanent responsibility creates a comic rivalry with Lynleit and a more serious test of whether Sherie wants Felix himself or only wants to win his attention. tien No current pairing contains enough personal exposure beyond professional dependency or operational rivalry. heyk No current pairing is supported. Shared danger and survivor's grief do not create sexual tension on their own. drake No current pairing has the repeated personal friction needed to move beyond abstract compatibility. reiner No current pairing is supported. His long-standing bond with Lynleit remains protective rather than romantic. inspector-leo Leo is married and remains outside the hidden Magi world. No sexual-tension pairing beyond his marriage is supported. father-mikhail No current pairing is supported. His vows, private history, and relationship to desire remain undefined. myka No current record. Character Archive

entries.title: Character Intimacy and Sexuality Reference · v10
entries.subtitle: Writer's Character Reference
entries.text: Character Intimacy and Sexuality Reference · v10 Writer's Character Reference Sherie and Felix’s emotional attention, reassurance, and uneven recognition, alongside the established relationship and family directions. Character Intimacy and Sexuality Reference A writer's reference to affection, attraction, initiative, and particular partners. Established events and working interpretations are distinguished below. The shared tension records attached to each profile track pairings as new scenes develop. How to read the profiles Established means confirmed by the author or present in the selected canon. Working interpretation means a possibility derived from current characterization, not an event or preference the story has established. Unresolved means there is not enough information to describe it. Doom Has an Address follows v7. Lynleit and Kyrien survive after an incomplete attempt at intimacy. The hotel refuge precedes Doom, which belongs in the later part of Arc 1's second half. Months later, the park encounter establishes successful oral intimacy. First intercourse is a separate later milestone; its exact placement is unresolved. Two relationship directions Author-confirmed direction, 12 September 2026. Sherie and Felix have no meaningful personal relationship at the opening. Her diplomatic responsibilities increasingly overlap with his work around Lynleit and MSF. Repeated assignments bring familiarity, respect, private jokes, and an unexpectedly compatible rhythm before either chooses personal closeness. Lynleit, by contrast, deliberately recruits Kyrien for strategic reasons and cannot anticipate the emotional consequences. Pair Familiarity and private rhythm Vulnerability and unresolved pressure --- --- --- Sherie and Felix She enjoys directing the exchange; he improvises, teases back, and makes her work for the response. Humor, visible enjoyment, mutual provocation, and occasional reversals carry into affection and eventual adult intimacy. He can enjoy and seek her company while still imagining a future with Lynleit. Sherie can recognize the possibility first without being willing to accept whatever attention he offers. Their care becomes especially revealing when a joke fails or neither feels able to perform. Lynleit and Kyrien Restrained attention, private tells, protected secrets, and practical dependence gradually make quiet companionship possible. Her initiative, pride, and curiosity meet his reserve and observation. Being recognized and challenged matters alongside being protected. Both must allow the other to affect them instead of continually managing what can be noticed. Their restraint can become unnecessary without making either consistently forthcoming. These are development directions, not a fixed sequence of new scenes. Neither pair should perform its characteristic rhythm in every exchange. The political and supernatural story supplies their work, loyalties, and immediate priorities; intimacy remains a subplot. Lynleit Basis: Established relationship; later behavior partly interpreted Natural approach Lynleit notices other people's needs and often makes herself responsible for them. Her work comes first. She usually values openness, but talking about her own desire embarrasses her. With someone she trusts, she can be playful and enjoy drawing out a reaction. Sexual expression Her attempt with Kyrien in Doom Has an Address is irritable, awkward, and incomplete. After they recover, she repeatedly insists there is no reason to try again. The unread pages and her response to Natalia suggest otherwise. Natalia's practical examples and familiar teasing keep the conversation between friends, even when Lynleit objects to the lesson. The deliberate silences in their later call let Lynleit's increasingly emphatic denials prolong the subject she wants to close. In v7, Mikhail names the Cult of Inanna and her lineage's long association with it. Lynleit is an associate through her family, not a direct participant. She counters his mock praise with a general principle, takes refuge in handling her cup, and threatens a reprisal if he repeats the address publicly. The family connection is explicit; the discomfort is carried through the exchange. He lets one averted glance pass without comment before the argument resumes. His accusation is not a religious obligation or a reason for her attraction to Kyrien. After the failed attempt, Lynleit's private research grows from curiosity and wounded pride. The park opportunity is spontaneous. Satisfaction in pleasing Kyrien matters alongside proving her competence, and his particular responses matter more than general theory. The later whiskey request is a practical aftertaste problem, not regret or rejection of him. Her preparation is theoretical, not evidence of earlier physical practice. The author's park direction moves from comfortable proximity to remembered failure and renewed curiosity. Initially she wants to establish her own competence; accepting practical assistance later need not erase that independence. She discovers an interest in affecting Kyrien's usual composure, while he begins noticing what his reactions reveal about her. These are character-specific developments, not universal claims about women or men. Their ordinary work clothes and the need to find the park exit remain part of the scene. The Bench under the Lamp v2 removes the invented kiss and leaves the intimate passage as an amber Writer notice. These author-confirmed intentions remain recorded here, but the omitted sequence is not yet demonstrated by the Chapter. The original detailed source is retained in the backlog archive. Their later pattern makes Lynleit the more frequent initiator. She is more vocal than Kyrien and likes teasing his reserve. The precise staging of those later encounters remains subject to the author's review. With Kyrien She knows his failed assassination nearly harmed her. He never learns she was there. That withheld fact gives the interrogation a personal edge before there is any attraction. Card games during the river watches give them something to do together outside her orders. She asks for rematches, learns his held breath before a risk, and catches him watching her hands. He protects her water-walking secret. Their recovery in the park and the later hotel refuge remain non-sexual. Her initiative and curiosity do not spare her the discomfort of being read accurately. Kyrien's quiet company can matter without requiring a conversation about it. Their growing intimacy needs moments when she lets his attention reach her without immediately turning it into a test or taking charge of what he is allowed to see. He eventually stays when she can no longer compel him. When she asks what reward makes the danger worthwhile, he answers, "Because there's a battle to be fought." She cannot dismiss his persistence as obedience or explain it through a promise she made him. After Fionn's death, the hotel refuge gives her nonsexual comfort in Kyrien's embrace. Much later the curse brings an incomplete attempt at intimacy, then a recovery she will not explain. Their sexual relationship begins afterward and lasts long enough to acquire private jokes and ordinary habits. A later encounter takes place in her third-floor study-bedroom. Pregnancy follows near the Arc 2 transition, with its meaning left for the reader to recognize at the next arc's opening. Lynleit bears their son during her disappearance and later keeps him hidden from both Kyrien and the wider world. They restore intimacy during Arc 2 and eventually conceive a second child, a daughter, who is born later. The daughter's conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2, not within it. The circumstances of concealment, Kyrien's eventual discovery, the process of reconciliation, and the daughter's timing and later family life remain undecided. Writing guardrail Let embarrassment occasionally make her unfair or difficult. Her competence does not require an explanation defending each awkward response. Kyrien Basis: Established relationship; later behavior partly interpreted Natural approach Kyrien is slow to trust and says little about what he feels. He notices discomfort, changes in routine, and what someone is trying to hide. Staying, making preparations, or keeping a secret can express his attachment. Sexual expression The incomplete attempt in Doom Has an Address leaves him puzzled. He sees a connection with their recovery but lacks Lynleit's explanation. In their later relationship he is quieter and initiates less often than she does. The working portrayal gives him sustained attention and practical habits afterward, such as bringing water or staying beside her. These are possibilities for scenes, not a required sequence. With Lynleit Their games provoke his need to win. Her ability to read him irritates him and draws his attention back to her. Her elegance and nerve also attract him. He does not explain his decision to stay as a romantic sacrifice. He wants the battle. The question of how much he is still trying to prove to his father remains open. When she refuses to discuss the attempted intimacy, he lets the subject rest without ceasing to wonder about it. Their later sexual relationship need not settle every disagreement or make him talkative. His observation must eventually allow reciprocal exposure. Lynleit can recognize or challenge him too; he cannot always remain the unreadable person who notices everything about her. Remaining beside one another, accepting help, and allowing an unguarded response carry their trust without requiring eloquence. Writing guardrail Give his silence a context. He may be watching, withholding an answer, annoyed, or simply have nothing to say. Helena Basis: Established marriage; working intimate interpretation Natural approach Helena wants to be admitted into a partner's whole life. Fionn's secrecy makes her doubt what their marriage means to him. A possible private habit is testing how much attention she has without admitting that she needs reassurance. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. The working interpretation makes her attentive to whether a partner is distracted or withholding something. With Fionn Their attraction and domestic closeness coexist with his refusal to share his deepest secrets. He believes he is protecting her. She feels excluded from her own marriage. Writing guardrail Show what Fionn withholds and what Helena does about it. The narrator need not decide the legitimacy of her grievance for the reader. Fionn Basis: Established marriage; working intimate interpretation Natural approach Fionn provides for and protects the people he loves. He also decides what they should be allowed to know. Warmth does not make that habit disappear. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. A patient, measured approach fits his present characterization, but a scene is needed before it becomes a reliable pattern. With Helena He respects and desires Helena while withholding the hidden workings of MSF, the Magiarchy, and his succession arrangements. His belief that secrecy protects her does not resolve her resentment. Writing guardrail Include ordinary companionship where the story calls for it. Every private exchange need not become a demonstration of their failed trust. Yulia Basis: Established attraction arc; working sexual interpretation Natural approach Yulia accompanies Hiyu while complaining about the reasons for going. She checks details, remembers responsibilities, and keeps him from overlooking practical risks. Sexual expression No encounter is established. A quiet and initially cautious approach is plausible; it should be tested against actual scenes rather than treated as an automatic consequence of her reserve. With Hiyu They argue over the same evidence and remain close while trying to prove each other wrong. Yulia is likely to notice that proximity before Hiyu does. Her impatience can include attraction without making her objections false. The approved development direction gives her an earlier awareness of the attachment. Hiyu continues treating the exchange as an argument about the investigation. Writing guardrail Let her be genuinely annoyed. Irritation does not have to conceal desire every time. Hiyu Basis: Established attraction arc; working sexual interpretation Natural approach Hiyu keeps seeking the person whose criticism makes his ideas more interesting. He notices the intellectual need before he understands the personal one. Sexual expression No encounter is established. Curiosity and improvisation are possible extensions of his personality, not established sexual preferences. With Yulia He seeks her corrections while resisting them. One proposed recognition scene has him enjoy investigating alone at first, then keep turning toward the place where she should be. His obliviousness delays his understanding of her attention. It does not make every concern she raises invisible to him. Writing guardrail Give him reasons to listen that arise from the case as well as the relationship. Felix Basis: Established asymmetry with Lynleit; author-confirmed gradual relationship direction with Sherie Natural approach Felix flirts, jokes, and watches the response. He enjoys trying multiple interpretations even without a social purpose. When reassuring someone, he can offer a hopeful reading before he fully believes it, continuing to think privately. Serious feelings can be harder for him to state plainly than a playful advance. Sexual expression His eventual intimacy with Sherie retains their humor, visible enjoyment, mutual provocation, and occasional reversals. He can challenge her confident lead without needing to win every exchange. This is confirmed direction; specific encounters remain unwritten. With Lynleit and Sherie Lynleit deflects his advances while remaining his close friend. His attraction does not establish a matching desire on her side. At the opening, he and Sherie have no meaningful personal relationship. Professional overlap brings them together repeatedly. He enjoys complicating her direction of an exchange, answers her teasing, and gradually seeks out her company. Familiarity and respect accumulate alongside private jokes. He remains internally fixated on Lynleit throughout that developing chemistry. His responses to Sherie can be immediate and sincere while his interpretation remains organized around Lynleit. He may regard Sherie's interest as her usual charm or their closeness as an unusually entertaining professional friendship. He can become emotionally invested before recognizing the intimate possibility. His attachment to Lynleit carries genuine disappointment and hope; one successful flirtation cannot dissolve it. Sherie comes to recognize the seriousness beneath his jokes. With her, he need not always supply the entertainment. His eventual movement toward her requires recognizing someone he wants in her own right, not accepting a substitute after disappointment with Lynleit. If someone he respects points out that he is hurting Sherie, his first response would be stunned recognition and surprise that he did not notice. This is a confirmed hypothetical response, not an existing scene or an immediate resolution of his attachment. Writing guardrail An unsuccessful joke, a change of subject, or a plain answer can distinguish his sincere attention from his usual performance. Let readers notice the difference between whom he imagines being close to and whom he is actually becoming close to. Do not add a narrator's verdict explaining the contradiction after an exchange has made it visible. Reiner Basis: Established friendship; intimate life unresolved Natural approach Reiner shows care through consistency and preparation. A working interpretation gives him more ease with practical help than courtship. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. Privacy and a deliberate pace are possibilities to explore. With a specific partner No partner is established. His long-standing friendship with Lynleit is protective. Writing guardrail His reserve leaves room for warmth. It does not prescribe how every private encounter must unfold. Sherie Basis: Established personality; author-confirmed gradual relationship direction with Felix Natural approach Sherie enjoys attention, praise, teasing, and mischief even when she has no professional reason to perform. Flirting is also part of her diplomatic skill, used so often that it can make a sincere approach difficult to distinguish from a practiced one. If a response changes unexpectedly, she notices the emotional change in the person and the situation. That sensitivity does not make her interpretation infallible. Sexual expression With Felix, her confident, playful lead carries into affection and eventual adult intimacy. He enjoys challenging it, and she can enjoy an unexpected reversal. Humor and visible pleasure belong to their shared rhythm; no specific encounter or choreography has been established. With Felix and Kyrien Kyrien is a potential source of tension because he does not give her the reactions she expects. Repeated negotiation could turn that frustration personal. No relationship between them is established. Her connection with Felix grows slowly through recurring diplomatic and MSF work, not an immediate personal bond. He responds readily and teases back, making her work for the reaction she wants. She can become theatrical, petty, ridiculous, or openly delighted around him without losing his respect. In turn, she learns to take his seriousness as readily as his jokes. She may understand the intimate possibility before he does. His attachment to Lynleit can hurt even when he is attentive to Sherie. Her confidence leaves room for disappointment and doubt about whether he sees her clearly. She has boundaries and reasons to reconsider the closeness; she is not obliged to keep charming him until he notices her. The particular moments that expose those limits remain to be written. The already-recorded later exchange with Lynleit retains its teasing rivalry. After learning that Lynleit has slept with Kyrien, Sherie challenges Lynleit's continuing sense of responsibility for Felix: "What exactly is this? Do you imagine every man is your permanent responsibility? Felix is not your wounded soldier. If you refuse to have him, I may very well take him myself, you shameless hussy!" Lynleit objects to her playing with him. The boast does not define the origin or extent of Sherie's interest. Her own attachment develops through accumulated familiarity with Felix, and his fixation cannot be settled as a contest between the two women. This exchange belongs after Lynleit and Kyrien's later completed encounter, not immediately after Doom Has an Address; it does not date the beginning of Sherie and Felix's professional contact. Writing guardrail Allow a sincere request to sound less polished than her diplomatic speech. Keep the care reciprocal. Felix can respond when her performance falters, just as she can stay attentive when he stops entertaining her. Neither needs to turn every such moment into a confession. Drake Basis: Working interpretation; partner unresolved Natural approach Drake may try to help by removing a practical burden while missing the reassurance a person wanted. This follows his established difficulty with social situations, but no intimate scene confirms it yet. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. Reserve and overthinking are possibilities, not a complete profile. With a specific partner No partner is established. His closest recorded relationships are his friendship with the Duke and his role as Sherie's uncle and teacher. Writing guardrail Awkward timing is more specific than treating him as generally unable to understand feelings. Heyk Basis: Survivor's history established; intimate life unresolved Natural approach The loss of his squad may affect how he responds to closeness. Withdrawal, protectiveness, or vigilance are possibilities to test in a particular scene. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. There is not enough evidence to decide how his grief affects desire or private comfort. With a specific partner No partner is established. Writing guardrail Do not assign the same trauma response to every encounter. The person, timing, and circumstances matter. Natalia Basis: Established tension with Lester; sexual behavior unresolved Natural approach Natalia values solitude and independent thought. Her work makes her accustomed to asking intimate questions as an examiner. Being personally involved can make that familiar method less useful. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. An observant and selective approach is a working interpretation. With Lester She examines his demiholumn condition and is attracted to him. He notices when her attention becomes personal and provokes her to act rather than continue observing. Neither knows his origin, and attraction does not resolve his contradictory history. Natalia can recognize contradiction as natural without acquiring a complete explanation of Lester. Their work keeps bringing them together. Neither the attraction nor an eventual encounter would answer all of her questions about his nature. Writing guardrail Let her be curious about something ordinary in him too. His anomalous nature need not account for all of her interest. Tien Basis: Occupational context established; intimate life unresolved Natural approach His work requires secrecy. Whether he carries the same habits into private relationships is not established. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. With a specific partner No partner is established. Helena is his employer and protected principal. Writing guardrail Do not turn an assassin's professional methods into a ready-made sexual personality. Lester Basis: Established tension with Natalia; personal history unresolved Natural approach Lester seeks direct experience and enjoys provoking Natalia. His response to being examined is part of their friction. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. His demiholumn nature alone cannot supply it. With Natalia He wants her attention as a man as well as an unusual case. Her analytical distance gives him something to provoke, while their shared work gives the attraction repeated contact. Writing guardrail His ordinary tastes, humor, and irritation should remain available alongside the mystery of his body. Inspector Leo Basis: Marriage established; private life unresolved Natural approach His patience as an investigator offers one possible starting point. The archive does not yet establish how he behaves with his spouse. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. With a specific partner Leo is married. His spouse is not yet described. He has no established sexual tension with Natalia and remains outside the Magi world. Writing guardrail Establish the marriage through a scene before projecting his police habits onto it. Father Mikhail Basis: Clerical role established; private life unresolved Natural approach His history, personal attachments, and vows are not yet defined. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. His mock blessing and blunt advice to Lynleit establish how he teases her using knowledge of her family, not how he behaves with a partner. With a specific partner No partner is established. Writing guardrail Neither celibacy nor a hidden romance follows from the title Father. Myka Basis: Familial closeness established; romantic history unresolved Natural approach to closeness Myka confides in Natalia about studies and personal worries. Natalia checks on her and sometimes treats her like a daughter. With a specific partner No romantic partner or sexual profile is recorded. Archive-wide writing principles Preserve each character's work, loyalties, and immediate objective. Use recurring contact specific to the pair. Shared danger can intensify attraction but does not establish it by itself. Distinguish attention from attraction and attraction from a promised relationship. Let gestures, interruptions, and choices carry implications without narrating the conclusion again. A useful encounter may leave a disagreement, an unanswered question, or a changed habit. Keep interpretations separate from confirmed preferences. Revisit them when new scenes supply evidence. Development sequence and thematic limits 1. Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge. 2. Doom's incomplete attempt, late in the second half of Arc 1. 3. Months of private theoretical study, followed by the spontaneous park encounter. 4. Reciprocal exploration and learning to receive as well as initiate. 5. First intercourse by mutual choice, followed by ordinary, playful intimacy. 6. Pregnancy near the Arc 1 transition; the son is born during Lynleit's disappearance. Arc 2 makes his existence legible to the reader, not automatically to Kyrien. 7. Lynleit keeps their son hidden from Kyrien and the wider world after his birth. The timing and circumstances of Kyrien's eventual discovery are undecided. 8. Restored intimacy during Arc 2 ultimately leads to the conception of their daughter and her later birth. The conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2. They have two children by the end of the story. These are separate milestones, not a conscious program Lynleit follows. Her duty remains primary. She was already a competent adult while Fionn lived; his death changes the structure of belonging and responsibility. The family she eventually forms with Kyrien is her choice, not compliance with a Cult duty or Fionn's selection of a successor. Arc 0's possible teenage encounter is non-romantic and unconfirmed. Do not backdate this adult sexual progression into the prequel. Related characterization The Cognition and Physical Competence reference records the author’s 12 September clarifications and separates confirmed behavior from suspected types. These additions do not date a relationship milestone or replace the unresolved scenes above. Established arc Mutual, slow to surface lynleit Lynleit Lynleit studies Kyrien first as a recruit whose failed attack nearly harmed her. Their card games make that scrutiny personal: she learns his tells and begins noticing his hands and breath. Later she attempts intimacy as a possible treatment for their shared curse, but remains interested after they survive without completing it. Mikhail's mock blessing exposes her family association with the Cult of Inanna. She counters with abstract principles and increasingly personal objections. His teasing does not create her attraction to Kyrien or make ancestry a reason for it. In the park, she wants to correct her private sense of failure, then finds satisfaction in knowing Kyrien as a particular person. Her theory follows an impulse already present. The preparation remains theoretical. Her attention shifts from proving competence toward learning his individual responses; the current park draft leaves that passage for the author rather than depicting it. kyrien Kyrien Kyrien wants to beat Lynleit at cards and dislikes finding that she can read him. Her elegance and nerve also attract him. He stays because he wants the battle, then finds himself facing private questions that her orders cannot answer. After the attempted intimacy, she will not tell him why their curse disappeared. He notices her pleasure in success and answers with a joke rather than a declaration. When she later asks for his flask, he does not force an explanation. The author also intends him to notice how being able to affect him changes her confidence. This reciprocal observation is not a shift into generic dominance. Quiet companionship and private tells matter alongside practical dependence and protected secrets. Her initiative, pride, and curiosity can reach him, but both must gradually allow themselves to be affected rather than continually managing what the other notices. Their intimacy includes being quietly recognized, accompanied, and challenged without their usual defenses; restraint can become unnecessary without making them talkative. The interrogation, card games, protected secret, and voluntary decision to stay give this pairing different kinds of familiarity. In Doom Has an Address, an incomplete attempt at intimacy breaks the shared curse. Lynleit loses the excuse of treatment without losing her interest in Kyrien; he is left trying to understand what happened. Their sexual relationship begins later in Arc 1. Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge precede Doom. Months afterward, a spontaneous park encounter lets Lynleit's curiosity and wounded pride become a successful private milestone. Oral intimacy, reciprocal exploration, first intercourse, and pregnancy remain separate. The family theme does not turn ancestry into an instruction or make grief itself attraction. Lynleit bears their son during her disappearance and later keeps him hidden from both Kyrien and the wider world. They restore intimacy during Arc 2 and eventually conceive a second child, a daughter, who is born later. The daughter's conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2, not within it. The author has confirmed this direction, not the scenes that restore intimacy or the timing of Kyrien's discovery of their son. Duty remains primary; a second child does not substitute for the work of reconnection. Established asymmetry Felix overt, Lynleit deflecting lynleit Lynleit Felix's flirting belongs to a long friendship she refuses to reorganize around his advances. Her ease with him, combined with the repeated refusal, creates visible chemistry without requiring matching sexual intent. felix Felix Lynleit is one of the few people his charm cannot simply move into the response he wants. Familiar affection, physical ease, and repeated deflection keep his attraction active even when he respects the boundary she has made. He remains internally fixated on her while growing close to Sherie through work. Enjoying Sherie's company does not immediately change whom he imagines being intimate with; his attachment to Lynleit takes more than successful flirtation to loosen. The tension is easy for readers to recognize because it already has a social rhythm: he advances through jokes and flirtation, she ignores or redirects him, and neither abandons the closeness underneath the exchange. It does not need to become a relationship to remain real. Emerging arc Mutual, unequally conscious yulia Yulia Hiyu irritates her into sustained attention. She keeps arguing, correcting, and following because his ideas have already occupied more of her mind than she wants to admit. Suppressed attraction can sharpen both her impatience and her awareness of his physical presence. hiyu Hiyu Yulia is the critic whose resistance makes an idea worth pursuing. He becomes dependent on her attention before he understands that the dependence is personal, leaving him oblivious to tension that is already changing how he seeks her out. Their arguments repeatedly force proximity and attention. They lean over the same evidence, reach for the same document, and forget ordinary distance while trying to prove incompatible explanations. Yulia notices first and steps away; Hiyu continues the theory and wonders why she moved. Her anger becomes disproportionate when his recklessness makes the possibility of losing him real. Hiyu recognizes the bond through absence: an investigation without her corrections becomes less interesting, and he keeps turning toward the place where she should be. Yulia and Hiyu become intimate by learning to communicate through the noise they already create together. Strong potential Situational and confrontational kyrien Kyrien Sherie's charm is too deliberate to disarm him, but the precision behind it earns his attention. He is more likely to watch for the moment her performance fails than reward the performance itself. sherie Sherie Kyrien's refusal to be steered threatens a skill she has internalized as part of her identity. Each failed attempt to produce a reaction can make his eventual attention feel more valuable and personally dangerous. Sherie uses language and calibrated flirtation to control the rhythm of an exchange. Kyrien answers with silence, literalism, or no usable reaction at all. Repeated negotiation could turn her professional frustration into sexual tension without making them compatible or displacing Kyrien's eventual relationship with Lynleit. Established marriage Mutual, damaged by exclusion fionn Fionn Fionn's affection and desire for Helena are genuine. He separates bodily and domestic closeness from the secrets he believes he must carry alone, never understanding that this division changes what their intimacy means to her. helena Helena Helena experiences desire alongside the need to be admitted into Fionn's complete life. Physical familiarity can therefore intensify resentment: she can be close enough to know his body while remaining excluded from the truth governing him. Their sexual tension survives inside a real marriage because attraction and grievance occupy the same private space. The closer they become physically, the harder it is for Helena to accept that Fionn still decides which parts of himself she is permitted to know. Established tension Mutual, differently expressed natalia Natalia Lester is the living exception that Natalia cannot finish classifying. Her professional attention can become personal before she recognizes the change, especially when he interrupts an examination by noticing that she is watching him rather than the phenomenon around him. lester Lester Natalia's analytical distance gives Lester something unusually difficult to provoke. He enjoys forcing the reserved researcher into immediate experience, but the tension changes when he wants her attention to recognize the man rather than examine the demiholumn condition. Repeated cases bring Natalia's examination of Lester into conflict with his insistence on being treated as more than a case. He provokes her to act; she notices more than he expected. Their attraction does not answer her questions about his demiholumn nature. Neither knows how he came into existence. His chronology is intrinsically contradictory, not a solvable transformation history. Natalia's recognition that contradiction belongs to nature does not mean she can explain him completely or that attraction answers the contradiction. As their work repeatedly overlaps, she finds room to become theatrical, petty, ridiculous, or openly delighted without losing his respect. She may recognize their intimate potential before he does. His fixation on Lynleit can hurt despite his responsive attention; her confidence does not remove disappointment, boundaries, or doubt about whether he sees her clearly. She gradually recognizes the seriousness beneath his jokes and becomes someone around whom he need not always entertain. Social play is something she enjoys off duty too. An unexpected response makes her attend to the emotional change in Felix and in the exchange, without guaranteeing that she understands its cause. felix Felix Felix enjoys Sherie's company, answers her teasing, and gradually seeks her out while remaining internally fixated on Lynleit. His attention is responsive, but he may interpret Sherie's interest as habitual charm or their closeness as an entertaining professional friendship. Emotional investment can precede his recognition of its intimate possibility. His attachment to Lynleit has genuine weight and takes more than successful flirtation to loosen. Moving toward Sherie eventually means recognizing her own importance to him and wanting her without treating her as a substitute for Lynleit. He may offer a hopeful interpretation to reassure someone while still privately testing it. If a trusted person points out that his attachment to Lynleit is hurting Sherie, the author expects stunned recognition and surprise that he missed it; the actual exchange and its consequences remain unwritten. They have no meaningful personal relationship at the story's opening. Sherie's diplomatic responsibilities increasingly overlap with Felix's work around Lynleit and MSF, bringing repeated encounters before either chooses closeness. Familiarity, respect, private jokes, and a compatible rhythm develop gradually. Her confident, playful dominance meets his expressiveness, improvisation, and willingness to challenge her. Humor, visible enjoyment, mutual provocation, and occasional reversals carry into affection and eventual adult intimacy. Care becomes particularly revealing when one stops performing and the other remains attentive. Readers can notice Felix building intimacy's foundations with Sherie while still imagining it with Lynleit; narration need not explain that contradiction. The later teasing challenge to Lynleit remains, but it neither starts their familiarity nor reduces Sherie's interest to winning him. This differs from Lynleit's strategic recruitment of Kyrien and their quieter recognition through restrained attention, protected secrets, and gradually accepted vulnerability. Both couples remain subplots beneath the political and supernatural story. Character Intimacy and Sexuality Reference A writer's reference to affection, attraction, initiative, and particular partners. Established events and working interpretations are distinguished below. The shared tension records attached to each profile track pairings as new scenes develop. How to read the profiles Established means confirmed by the author or present in the selected canon. Working interpretation means a possibility derived from current characterization, not an event or preference the story has established. Unresolved means there is not enough information to describe it. Doom Has an Address follows v7. Lynleit and Kyrien survive after an incomplete attempt at intimacy. The hotel refuge precedes Doom, which belongs in the later part of Arc 1's second half. Months later, the park encounter establishes successful oral intimacy. First intercourse is a separate later milestone; its exact placement is unresolved. Two relationship directions Author-confirmed direction, 12 September 2026. Sherie and Felix have no meaningful personal relationship at the opening. Her diplomatic responsibilities increasingly overlap with his work around Lynleit and MSF. Repeated assignments bring familiarity, respect, private jokes, and an unexpectedly compatible rhythm before either chooses personal closeness. Lynleit, by contrast, deliberately recruits Kyrien for strategic reasons and cannot anticipate the emotional consequences. Sherie can recognize the possibility first without being willing to accept whatever attention he offers. Their care becomes especially revealing when a joke fails or neither feels able to perform. Her initiative, pride, and curiosity meet his reserve and observation. Being recognized and challenged matters alongside being protected. Both must allow the other to affect them instead of continually managing what can be noticed. Their restraint can become unnecessary without making either consistently forthcoming. These are development directions, not a fixed sequence of new scenes. Neither pair should perform its characteristic rhythm in every exchange. The political and supernatural story supplies their work, loyalties, and immediate priorities; intimacy remains a subplot. She usually values openness, but talking about her own desire embarrasses her. With someone she trusts, she can be playful and enjoy drawing out a reaction. The deliberate silences in their later call let Lynleit's increasingly emphatic denials prolong the subject she wants to close. She counters his mock praise with a general principle, takes refuge in handling her cup, and threatens a reprisal if he repeats the address publicly. The family connection is explicit; the discomfort is carried through the exchange. He lets one averted glance pass without comment before the argument resumes. His accusation is not a religious obligation or a reason for her attraction to Kyrien. After the failed attempt, Lynleit's private research grows from curiosity and wounded pride. The park opportunity is spontaneous. Satisfaction in pleasing Kyrien matters alongside proving her competence, and his particular responses matter more than general theory. The later whiskey request is a practical aftertaste problem, not regret or rejection of him. Her preparation is theoretical, not evidence of earlier physical practice. The author's park direction moves from comfortable proximity to remembered failure and renewed curiosity. Initially she wants to establish her own competence; accepting practical assistance later need not erase that independence. She discovers an interest in affecting Kyrien's usual composure, while he begins noticing what his reactions reveal about her. These are character-specific developments, not universal claims about women or men. Their ordinary work clothes and the need to find the park exit remain part of the scene.
