Her impatience can include attraction without making her objections false. The approved development direction gives her an earlier awareness of the attachment. Hiyu continues treating the exchange as an argument about the investigation. Writing guardrail Let her be genuinely annoyed. Irritation does not have to conceal desire every time. Hiyu Basis: Established attraction arc; working sexual interpretation Natural approach Hiyu keeps seeking the person whose criticism makes his ideas more interesting. He notices the intellectual need before he understands the personal one. Sexual expression No encounter is established. Curiosity and improvisation are possible extensions of his personality, not established sexual preferences. With Yulia He seeks her corrections while resisting them. One proposed recognition scene has him enjoy investigating alone at first, then keep turning toward the place where she should be. His obliviousness delays his understanding of her attention. It does not make every concern she raises invisible to him. Writing guardrail Give him reasons to listen that arise from the case as well as the relationship. Felix Basis: Established flirtation and asymmetric tension with Lynleit Natural approach Felix flirts, jokes, and watches the response. Serious feelings can be harder for him to state plainly than a playful advance. Sexual expression The working interpretation makes him communicative, playful, and comfortable initiating. His private behavior has not yet been established in a scene. With Lynleit and Sherie Lynleit deflects his advances while remaining his close friend. His attraction does not establish a matching desire on her side. Sherie can match his wit. Their similar habits allow them to keep flirting without saying anything definite. His attachment to Lynleit complicates Sherie's interest in him. Writing guardrail An unsuccessful joke, a change of subject, or a plain answer can distinguish his sincere attention from his usual performance. Reiner Basis: Established friendship; intimate life unresolved Natural approach Reiner shows care through consistency and preparation. A working interpretation gives him more ease with practical help than courtship. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. Privacy and a deliberate pace are possibilities to explore. With a specific partner No partner is established. His long-standing friendship with Lynleit is protective. Writing guardrail His reserve leaves room for warmth. It does not prescribe how every private encounter must unfold. Sherie Basis: Established personality and flirtation; sexual behavior unresolved Natural approach Sherie enjoys attention and praise. Flirting is also part of her diplomatic skill, used so often that it can make a sincere approach difficult to distinguish from a practiced one. Sexual expression A playful, verbally expressive approach is plausible. Her actual preferences remain unwritten. With Felix and Kyrien Kyrien is a potential source of tension because he does not give her the reactions she expects. Repeated negotiation could turn that frustration personal. No relationship between them is established. Felix responds readily and can answer her teasing in kind. After learning that Lynleit has slept with Kyrien, Sherie challenges Lynleit's continuing sense of responsibility for Felix: "What exactly is this? Do you imagine every man is your permanent responsibility? Felix is not your wounded soldier. If you refuse to have him, I may very well take him myself, you shameless hussy!" Lynleit objects to her playing with him. Sherie's interest includes competition with Lynleit, but whether it becomes lasting affection for Felix remains unresolved. This exchange belongs after Lynleit and Kyrien's later completed encounter, not immediately after Doom Has an Address. Writing guardrail Allow a sincere request to sound less polished than her diplomatic speech. Drake Basis: Working interpretation; partner unresolved Natural approach Drake may try to help by removing a practical burden while missing the reassurance a person wanted. This follows his established difficulty with social situations, but no intimate scene confirms it yet. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. Reserve and overthinking are possibilities, not a complete profile. With a specific partner No partner is established. His closest recorded relationships are his friendship with the Duke and his role as Sherie's uncle and teacher. Writing guardrail Awkward timing is more specific than treating him as generally unable to understand feelings. Heyk Basis: Survivor's history established; intimate life unresolved Natural approach The loss of his squad may affect how he responds to closeness. Withdrawal, protectiveness, or vigilance are possibilities to test in a particular scene. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. There is not enough evidence to decide how his grief affects desire or private comfort. With a specific partner No partner is established. Writing guardrail Do not assign the same trauma response to every encounter. The person, timing, and circumstances matter. Natalia Basis: Established tension with Lester; sexual behavior unresolved Natural approach Natalia values solitude and independent thought. Her work makes her accustomed to asking intimate questions as an examiner. Being personally involved can make that familiar method less useful. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. An observant and selective approach is a working interpretation. With Lester She examines his demiholumn condition and is attracted to him. He notices when her attention becomes personal and provokes her to act rather than continue observing. Neither knows his origin, and attraction does not resolve his contradictory history. Natalia can recognize contradiction as natural without acquiring a complete explanation of Lester. Their work keeps bringing them together. Neither the attraction nor an eventual encounter would answer all of her questions about his nature. Writing guardrail Let her be curious about something ordinary in him too. His anomalous nature need not account for all of her interest. Tien Basis: Occupational context established; intimate life unresolved Natural approach His work requires secrecy. Whether he carries the same habits into private relationships is not established. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. With a specific partner No partner is established. Helena is his employer and protected principal. Writing guardrail Do not turn an assassin's professional methods into a ready-made sexual personality. Lester Basis: Established tension with Natalia; personal history unresolved Natural approach Lester seeks direct experience and enjoys provoking Natalia. His response to being examined is part of their friction. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. His demiholumn nature alone cannot supply it. With Natalia He wants her attention as a man as well as an unusual case. Her analytical distance gives him something to provoke, while their shared work gives the attraction repeated contact. Writing guardrail His ordinary tastes, humor, and irritation should remain available alongside the mystery of his body. Inspector Leo Basis: Marriage established; private life unresolved Natural approach His patience as an investigator offers one possible starting point. The archive does not yet establish how he behaves with his spouse. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. With a specific partner Leo is married. His spouse is not yet described. He has no established sexual tension with Natalia and remains outside the Magi world. Writing guardrail Establish the marriage through a scene before projecting his police habits onto it. Father Mikhail Basis: Clerical role established; private life unresolved Natural approach His history, personal attachments, and vows are not yet defined. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. His mock blessing and blunt advice to Lynleit establish how he teases her using knowledge of her family, not how he behaves with a partner. With a specific partner No partner is established. Writing guardrail Neither celibacy nor a hidden romance follows from the title Father. Myka Basis: Familial closeness established; romantic history unresolved Natural approach to closeness Myka confides in Natalia about studies and personal worries. Natalia checks on her and sometimes treats her like a daughter. With a specific partner No romantic partner or sexual profile is recorded. Archive-wide writing principles Preserve each character's work, loyalties, and immediate objective. Use recurring contact specific to the pair. Shared danger can intensify attraction but does not establish it by itself. Distinguish attention from attraction and attraction from a promised relationship. Let gestures, interruptions, and choices carry implications without narrating the conclusion again. A useful encounter may leave a disagreement, an unanswered question, or a changed habit. Keep interpretations separate from confirmed preferences. Revisit them when new scenes supply evidence. Development sequence and thematic limits 1. Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge. 2. Doom's incomplete attempt, late in the second half of Arc 1. 3. Months of private theoretical study, followed by the spontaneous park encounter. 4. Reciprocal exploration and learning to receive as well as initiate. 5. First intercourse by mutual choice, followed by ordinary, playful intimacy. 6. Pregnancy near the Arc 1 transition; the son is born during Lynleit's disappearance. Arc 2 makes his existence legible to the reader, not automatically to Kyrien. 7. Lynleit keeps their son hidden from Kyrien and the wider world after his birth. The timing and circumstances of Kyrien's eventual discovery are undecided. 8. Restored intimacy during Arc 2 ultimately leads to the conception of their daughter and her later birth. The conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2. They have two children by the end of the story. These are separate milestones, not a conscious program Lynleit follows. Her duty remains primary. She was already a competent adult while Fionn lived; his death changes the structure of belonging and responsibility. The family she eventually forms with Kyrien is her choice, not compliance with a Cult duty or Fionn's selection of a successor. Arc 0's possible teenage encounter is non-romantic and unconfirmed. Do not backdate this adult sexual progression into the prequel. Established arc Mutual, slow to surface lynleit Lynleit Lynleit studies Kyrien first as a recruit whose failed attack nearly harmed her. Their card games make that scrutiny personal: she learns his tells and begins noticing his hands and breath. Later she attempts intimacy as a possible treatment for their shared curse, but remains interested after they survive without completing it. Mikhail's mock blessing exposes her family association with the Cult of Inanna. She counters with abstract principles and increasingly personal objections. His teasing does not create her attraction to Kyrien or make ancestry a reason for it. In the park, she wants to correct her private sense of failure, then finds satisfaction in knowing Kyrien as a particular person. Her theory follows an impulse already present. The preparation remains theoretical. Her attention shifts from proving competence toward learning his individual responses; the current park draft leaves that passage for the author rather than depicting it. kyrien Kyrien Kyrien wants to beat Lynleit at cards and dislikes finding that she can read him. Her elegance and nerve also attract him. He stays because he wants the battle, then finds himself facing private questions that her orders cannot answer. After the attempted intimacy, she will not tell him why their curse disappeared. He notices her pleasure in success and answers with a joke rather than a declaration. When she later asks for his flask, he does not force an explanation. The author also intends him to notice how being able to affect him changes her confidence. This reciprocal observation is not a shift into generic dominance. The interrogation, card games, protected secret, and voluntary decision to stay give this pairing different kinds of familiarity. In Doom Has an Address, an incomplete attempt at intimacy breaks the shared curse. Lynleit loses the excuse of treatment without losing her interest in Kyrien; he is left trying to understand what happened. Their sexual relationship begins later in Arc 1. Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge precede Doom. Months afterward, a spontaneous park encounter lets Lynleit's curiosity and wounded pride become a successful private milestone. Oral intimacy, reciprocal exploration, first intercourse, and pregnancy remain separate. The family theme does not turn ancestry into an instruction or make grief itself attraction. Lynleit bears their son during her disappearance and later keeps him hidden from both Kyrien and the wider world. They restore intimacy during Arc 2 and eventually conceive a second child, a daughter, who is born later. The daughter's conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2, not within it. The author has confirmed this direction, not the scenes that restore intimacy or the timing of Kyrien's discovery of their son. Duty remains primary; a second child does not substitute for the work of reconnection. Established asymmetry Felix overt, Lynleit deflecting lynleit Lynleit Felix's flirting belongs to a long friendship she refuses to reorganize around his advances. Her ease with him, combined with the repeated refusal, creates visible chemistry without requiring matching sexual intent. felix Felix Lynleit is one of the few people his charm cannot simply move into the response he wants. Familiar affection, physical ease, and repeated deflection keep his attraction active even when he respects the boundary she has made. The tension is easy for readers to recognize because it already has a social rhythm: he advances through jokes and flirtation, she ignores or redirects him, and neither abandons the closeness underneath the exchange. It does not need to become a relationship to remain real. Emerging arc Mutual, unequally conscious yulia Yulia Hiyu irritates her into sustained attention. She keeps arguing, correcting, and following because his ideas have already occupied more of her mind than she wants to admit. Suppressed attraction can sharpen both her impatience and her awareness of his physical presence. hiyu Hiyu Yulia is the critic whose resistance makes an idea worth pursuing. He becomes dependent on her attention before he understands that the dependence is personal, leaving him oblivious to tension that is already changing how he seeks her out. Their arguments repeatedly force proximity and attention. They lean over the same evidence, reach for the same document, and forget ordinary distance while trying to prove incompatible explanations. Yulia notices first and steps away; Hiyu continues the theory and wonders why she moved. Her anger becomes disproportionate when his recklessness makes the possibility of losing him real. Hiyu recognizes the bond through absence: an investigation without her corrections becomes less interesting, and he keeps turning toward the place where she should be. Yulia and Hiyu become intimate by learning to communicate through the noise they already create together. Strong potential Situational and confrontational kyrien Kyrien Sherie's charm is too deliberate to disarm him, but the precision behind it earns his attention. He is more likely to watch for the moment her performance fails than reward the performance itself. sherie Sherie Kyrien's refusal to be steered threatens a skill she has internalized as part of her identity. Each failed attempt to produce a reaction can make his eventual attention feel more valuable and personally dangerous. Sherie uses language and calibrated flirtation to control the rhythm of an exchange. Kyrien answers with silence, literalism, or no usable reaction at all. Repeated negotiation could turn her professional frustration into sexual tension without making them compatible or displacing Kyrien's eventual relationship with Lynleit. Established marriage Mutual, damaged by exclusion fionn Fionn Fionn's affection and desire for Helena are genuine. He separates bodily and domestic closeness from the secrets he believes he must carry alone, never understanding that this division changes what their intimacy means to her. helena Helena Helena experiences desire alongside the need to be admitted into Fionn's complete life. Physical familiarity can therefore intensify resentment: she can be close enough to know his body while remaining excluded from the truth governing him. Their sexual tension survives inside a real marriage because attraction and grievance occupy the same private space. The closer they become physically, the harder it is for Helena to accept that Fionn still decides which parts of himself she is permitted to know. Established tension Mutual, differently expressed natalia Natalia Lester is the living exception that Natalia cannot finish classifying. Her professional attention can become personal before she recognizes the change, especially when he interrupts an examination by noticing that she is watching him rather than the phenomenon around him. lester Lester Natalia's analytical distance gives Lester something unusually difficult to provoke. He enjoys forcing the reserved researcher into immediate experience, but the tension changes when he wants her attention to recognize the man rather than examine the demiholumn condition. Repeated cases bring Natalia's examination of Lester into conflict with his insistence on being treated as more than a case. He provokes her to act; she notices more than he expected. Their attraction does not answer her questions about his demiholumn nature. Neither knows how he came into existence. His chronology is intrinsically contradictory, not a solvable transformation history. Natalia's recognition that contradiction belongs to nature does not mean she can explain him completely or that attraction answers the contradiction. Emerging potential Mutual play, sincerity unresolved sherie Sherie Felix gives Sherie immediate wit, visible attention, and resistance that does not become hostility. She first tests him as play and competition, including whether his attention can be drawn away from Lynleit. The tension becomes personal when winning ceases to satisfy her and she begins wanting a response that is not produced by technique. felix Felix Sherie can match Felix's teasing without mistaking it for a complete confession. Her ability to see when he hides seriousness behind a joke gives him an opponent and possible partner who can enjoy the performance while still asking for something sincere. His unresolved feelings for Lynleit prevent Sherie from winning him by charm alone. Both use social ease as protection: Felix hides seriousness behind jokes, while Sherie hides vulnerability behind charm and diplomacy. Their chemistry is immediate, but similarity makes them capable of prolonged flirtation without honest movement. Sherie begins testing the friendship after learning that Lynleit has slept with Kyrien while still feeling responsible for Felix's affection. Her refusal to treat Felix as Lynleit's permanent responsibility creates a comic rivalry with Lynleit and a more serious test of whether Sherie wants Felix himself or only wants to win his attention. tien No current pairing contains enough personal exposure beyond professional dependency or operational rivalry. heyk No current pairing is supported. Shared danger and survivor's grief do not create sexual tension on their own. drake No current pairing has the repeated personal friction needed to move beyond abstract compatibility. reiner No current pairing is supported. His long-standing bond with Lynleit remains protective rather than romantic. inspector-leo Leo is married and remains outside the hidden Magi world. No sexual-tension pairing beyond his marriage is supported. father-mikhail No current pairing is supported. His vows, private history, and relationship to desire remain undefined. myka No current record. Character Archive

entries.text: Character Intimacy and Sexuality Reference · v9 Writer's Character Reference Sherie and Felix's gradual professional familiarity, Felix's unresolved attachment to Lynleit, and the distinct private rhythms of both central pairings. Character Intimacy and Sexuality Reference A writer's reference to affection, attraction, initiative, and particular partners. Established events and working interpretations are distinguished below. The shared tension records attached to each profile track pairings as new scenes develop. How to read the profiles Established means confirmed by the author or present in the selected canon. Working interpretation means a possibility derived from current characterization, not an event or preference the story has established. Unresolved means there is not enough information to describe it. Doom Has an Address follows v7. Lynleit and Kyrien survive after an incomplete attempt at intimacy. The hotel refuge precedes Doom, which belongs in the later part of Arc 1's second half. Months later, the park encounter establishes successful oral intimacy. First intercourse is a separate later milestone; its exact placement is unresolved. Two relationship directions Author-confirmed direction, 12 September 2026. Sherie and Felix have no meaningful personal relationship at the opening. Her diplomatic responsibilities increasingly overlap with his work around Lynleit and MSF. Repeated assignments bring familiarity, respect, private jokes, and an unexpectedly compatible rhythm before either chooses personal closeness. Lynleit, by contrast, deliberately recruits Kyrien for strategic reasons and cannot anticipate the emotional consequences. Pair Familiarity and private rhythm Vulnerability and unresolved pressure --- --- --- Sherie and Felix She enjoys directing the exchange; he improvises, teases back, and makes her work for the response. Humor, visible enjoyment, mutual provocation, and occasional reversals carry into affection and eventual adult intimacy. He can enjoy and seek her company while still imagining a future with Lynleit. Sherie can recognize the possibility first without being willing to accept whatever attention he offers. Their care becomes especially revealing when a joke fails or neither feels able to perform. Lynleit and Kyrien Restrained attention, private tells, protected secrets, and practical dependence gradually make quiet companionship possible. Her initiative, pride, and curiosity meet his reserve and observation. Being recognized and challenged matters alongside being protected. Both must allow the other to affect them instead of continually managing what can be noticed. Their restraint can become unnecessary without making either consistently forthcoming. These are development directions, not a fixed sequence of new scenes. Neither pair should perform its characteristic rhythm in every exchange. The political and supernatural story supplies their work, loyalties, and immediate priorities; intimacy remains a subplot. Lynleit Basis: Established relationship; later behavior partly interpreted Natural approach Lynleit notices other people's needs and often makes herself responsible for them. Her work comes first. She usually values openness, but talking about her own desire embarrasses her. With someone she trusts, she can be playful and enjoy drawing out a reaction. Sexual expression Her attempt with Kyrien in Doom Has an Address is irritable, awkward, and incomplete. After they recover, she repeatedly insists there is no reason to try again. The unread pages and her response to Natalia suggest otherwise. Natalia's practical examples and familiar teasing keep the conversation between friends, even when Lynleit objects to the lesson. The deliberate silences in their later call let Lynleit's increasingly emphatic denials prolong the subject she wants to close. In v7, Mikhail names the Cult of Inanna and her lineage's long association with it. Lynleit is an associate through her family, not a direct participant. She counters his mock praise with a general principle, takes refuge in handling her cup, and threatens a reprisal if he repeats the address publicly. The family connection is explicit; the discomfort is carried through the exchange. He lets one averted glance pass without comment before the argument resumes. His accusation is not a religious obligation or a reason for her attraction to Kyrien. After the failed attempt, Lynleit's private research grows from curiosity and wounded pride. The park opportunity is spontaneous. Satisfaction in pleasing Kyrien matters alongside proving her competence, and his particular responses matter more than general theory. The later whiskey request is a practical aftertaste problem, not regret or rejection of him. Her preparation is theoretical, not evidence of earlier physical practice. The author's park direction moves from comfortable proximity to remembered failure and renewed curiosity. Initially she wants to establish her own competence; accepting practical assistance later need not erase that independence. She discovers an interest in affecting Kyrien's usual composure, while he begins noticing what his reactions reveal about her. These are character-specific developments, not universal claims about women or men. Their ordinary work clothes and the need to find the park exit remain part of the scene. The Bench under the Lamp v2 removes the invented kiss and leaves the intimate passage as an amber Writer notice. These author-confirmed intentions remain recorded here, but the omitted sequence is not yet demonstrated by the Chapter. The original detailed source is retained in the backlog archive. Their later pattern makes Lynleit the more frequent initiator. She is more vocal than Kyrien and likes teasing his reserve. The precise staging of those later encounters remains subject to the author's review. With Kyrien She knows his failed assassination nearly harmed her. He never learns she was there. That withheld fact gives the interrogation a personal edge before there is any attraction. Card games during the river watches give them something to do together outside her orders. She asks for rematches, learns his held breath before a risk, and catches him watching her hands. He protects her water-walking secret. Their recovery in the park and the later hotel refuge remain non-sexual. Her initiative and curiosity do not spare her the discomfort of being read accurately. Kyrien's quiet company can matter without requiring a conversation about it. Their growing intimacy needs moments when she lets his attention reach her without immediately turning it into a test or taking charge of what he is allowed to see. He eventually stays when she can no longer compel him. When she asks what reward makes the danger worthwhile, he answers, "Because there's a battle to be fought." She cannot dismiss his persistence as obedience or explain it through a promise she made him. After Fionn's death, the hotel refuge gives her nonsexual comfort in Kyrien's embrace. Much later the curse brings an incomplete attempt at intimacy, then a recovery she will not explain. Their sexual relationship begins afterward and lasts long enough to acquire private jokes and ordinary habits. A later encounter takes place in her third-floor study-bedroom. Pregnancy follows near the Arc 2 transition, with its meaning left for the reader to recognize at the next arc's opening. Lynleit bears their son during her disappearance and later keeps him hidden from both Kyrien and the wider world. They restore intimacy during Arc 2 and eventually conceive a second child, a daughter, who is born later. The daughter's conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2, not within it. The circumstances of concealment, Kyrien's eventual discovery, the process of reconciliation, and the daughter's timing and later family life remain undecided. Writing guardrail Let embarrassment occasionally make her unfair or difficult. Her competence does not require an explanation defending each awkward response. Kyrien Basis: Established relationship; later behavior partly interpreted Natural approach Kyrien is slow to trust and says little about what he feels. He notices discomfort, changes in routine, and what someone is trying to hide. Staying, making preparations, or keeping a secret can express his attachment. Sexual expression The incomplete attempt in Doom Has an Address leaves him puzzled. He sees a connection with their recovery but lacks Lynleit's explanation. In their later relationship he is quieter and initiates less often than she does. The working portrayal gives him sustained attention and practical habits afterward, such as bringing water or staying beside her. These are possibilities for scenes, not a required sequence. With Lynleit Their games provoke his need to win. Her ability to read him irritates him and draws his attention back to her. Her elegance and nerve also attract him. He does not explain his decision to stay as a romantic sacrifice. He wants the battle. The question of how much he is still trying to prove to his father remains open. When she refuses to discuss the attempted intimacy, he lets the subject rest without ceasing to wonder about it. Their later sexual relationship need not settle every disagreement or make him talkative. His observation must eventually allow reciprocal exposure. Lynleit can recognize or challenge him too; he cannot always remain the unreadable person who notices everything about her. Remaining beside one another, accepting help, and allowing an unguarded response carry their trust without requiring eloquence. Writing guardrail Give his silence a context. He may be watching, withholding an answer, annoyed, or simply have nothing to say. Helena Basis: Established marriage; working intimate interpretation Natural approach Helena wants to be admitted into a partner's whole life. Fionn's secrecy makes her doubt what their marriage means to him. A possible private habit is testing how much attention she has without admitting that she needs reassurance. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. The working interpretation makes her attentive to whether a partner is distracted or withholding something. With Fionn Their attraction and domestic closeness coexist with his refusal to share his deepest secrets. He believes he is protecting her. She feels excluded from her own marriage. Writing guardrail Show what Fionn withholds and what Helena does about it. The narrator need not decide the legitimacy of her grievance for the reader. Fionn Basis: Established marriage; working intimate interpretation Natural approach Fionn provides for and protects the people he loves. He also decides what they should be allowed to know. Warmth does not make that habit disappear. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. A patient, measured approach fits his present characterization, but a scene is needed before it becomes a reliable pattern. With Helena He respects and desires Helena while withholding the hidden workings of MSF, the Magiarchy, and his succession arrangements. His belief that secrecy protects her does not resolve her resentment. Writing guardrail Include ordinary companionship where the story calls for it. Every private exchange need not become a demonstration of their failed trust. Yulia Basis: Established attraction arc; working sexual interpretation Natural approach Yulia accompanies Hiyu while complaining about the reasons for going. She checks details, remembers responsibilities, and keeps him from overlooking practical risks. Sexual expression No encounter is established. A quiet and initially cautious approach is plausible; it should be tested against actual scenes rather than treated as an automatic consequence of her reserve. With Hiyu They argue over the same evidence and remain close while trying to prove each other wrong. Yulia is likely to notice that proximity before Hiyu does. Her impatience can include attraction without making her objections false. The approved development direction gives her an earlier awareness of the attachment. Hiyu continues treating the exchange as an argument about the investigation. Writing guardrail Let her be genuinely annoyed. Irritation does not have to conceal desire every time. Hiyu Basis: Established attraction arc; working sexual interpretation Natural approach Hiyu keeps seeking the person whose criticism makes his ideas more interesting. He notices the intellectual need before he understands the personal one. Sexual expression No encounter is established. Curiosity and improvisation are possible extensions of his personality, not established sexual preferences. With Yulia He seeks her corrections while resisting them. One proposed recognition scene has him enjoy investigating alone at first, then keep turning toward the place where she should be. His obliviousness delays his understanding of her attention. It does not make every concern she raises invisible to him. Writing guardrail Give him reasons to listen that arise from the case as well as the relationship. Felix Basis: Established asymmetry with Lynleit; author-confirmed gradual relationship direction with Sherie Natural approach Felix flirts, jokes, and watches the response. Serious feelings can be harder for him to state plainly than a playful advance. Sexual expression His eventual intimacy with Sherie retains their humor, visible enjoyment, mutual provocation, and occasional reversals. He can challenge her confident lead without needing to win every exchange. This is confirmed direction; specific encounters remain unwritten. With Lynleit and Sherie Lynleit deflects his advances while remaining his close friend. His attraction does not establish a matching desire on her side. At the opening, he and Sherie have no meaningful personal relationship. Professional overlap brings them together repeatedly. He enjoys complicating her direction of an exchange, answers her teasing, and gradually seeks out her company. Familiarity and respect accumulate alongside private jokes. He remains internally fixated on Lynleit throughout that developing chemistry. His responses to Sherie can be immediate and sincere while his interpretation remains organized around Lynleit. He may regard Sherie's interest as her usual charm or their closeness as an unusually entertaining professional friendship. He can become emotionally invested before recognizing the intimate possibility. His attachment to Lynleit carries genuine disappointment and hope; one successful flirtation cannot dissolve it. Sherie comes to recognize the seriousness beneath his jokes. With her, he need not always supply the entertainment. His eventual movement toward her requires recognizing someone he wants in her own right, not accepting a substitute after disappointment with Lynleit. Writing guardrail An unsuccessful joke, a change of subject, or a plain answer can distinguish his sincere attention from his usual performance. Let readers notice the difference between whom he imagines being close to and whom he is actually becoming close to. Do not add a narrator's verdict explaining the contradiction after an exchange has made it visible. Reiner Basis: Established friendship; intimate life unresolved Natural approach Reiner shows care through consistency and preparation. A working interpretation gives him more ease with practical help than courtship. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. Privacy and a deliberate pace are possibilities to explore. With a specific partner No partner is established. His long-standing friendship with Lynleit is protective. Writing guardrail His reserve leaves room for warmth. It does not prescribe how every private encounter must unfold. Sherie Basis: Established personality; author-confirmed gradual relationship direction with Felix Natural approach Sherie enjoys attention and praise. Flirting is also part of her diplomatic skill, used so often that it can make a sincere approach difficult to distinguish from a practiced one. Sexual expression With Felix, her confident, playful lead carries into affection and eventual adult intimacy. He enjoys challenging it, and she can enjoy an unexpected reversal. Humor and visible pleasure belong to their shared rhythm; no specific encounter or choreography has been established. With Felix and Kyrien Kyrien is a potential source of tension because he does not give her the reactions she expects. Repeated negotiation could turn that frustration personal. No relationship between them is established. Her connection with Felix grows slowly through recurring diplomatic and MSF work, not an immediate personal bond. He responds readily and teases back, making her work for the reaction she wants. She can become theatrical, petty, ridiculous, or openly delighted around him without losing his respect. In turn, she learns to take his seriousness as readily as his jokes. She may understand the intimate possibility before he does. His attachment to Lynleit can hurt even when he is attentive to Sherie. Her confidence leaves room for disappointment and doubt about whether he sees her clearly. She has boundaries and reasons to reconsider the closeness; she is not obliged to keep charming him until he notices her. The particular moments that expose those limits remain to be written. The already-recorded later exchange with Lynleit retains its teasing rivalry. After learning that Lynleit has slept with Kyrien, Sherie challenges Lynleit's continuing sense of responsibility for Felix: "What exactly is this? Do you imagine every man is your permanent responsibility? Felix is not your wounded soldier. If you refuse to have him, I may very well take him myself, you shameless hussy!" Lynleit objects to her playing with him. The boast does not define the origin or extent of Sherie's interest. Her own attachment develops through accumulated familiarity with Felix, and his fixation cannot be settled as a contest between the two women. This exchange belongs after Lynleit and Kyrien's later completed encounter, not immediately after Doom Has an Address; it does not date the beginning of Sherie and Felix's professional contact. Writing guardrail Allow a sincere request to sound less polished than her diplomatic speech. Keep the care reciprocal. Felix can respond when her performance falters, just as she can stay attentive when he stops entertaining her. Neither needs to turn every such moment into a confession. Drake Basis: Working interpretation; partner unresolved Natural approach Drake may try to help by removing a practical burden while missing the reassurance a person wanted. This follows his established difficulty with social situations, but no intimate scene confirms it yet. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. Reserve and overthinking are possibilities, not a complete profile. With a specific partner No partner is established. His closest recorded relationships are his friendship with the Duke and his role as Sherie's uncle and teacher. Writing guardrail Awkward timing is more specific than treating him as generally unable to understand feelings. Heyk Basis: Survivor's history established; intimate life unresolved Natural approach The loss of his squad may affect how he responds to closeness. Withdrawal, protectiveness, or vigilance are possibilities to test in a particular scene. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. There is not enough evidence to decide how his grief affects desire or private comfort. With a specific partner No partner is established. Writing guardrail Do not assign the same trauma response to every encounter. The person, timing, and circumstances matter. Natalia Basis: Established tension with Lester; sexual behavior unresolved Natural approach Natalia values solitude and independent thought. Her work makes her accustomed to asking intimate questions as an examiner. Being personally involved can make that familiar method less useful. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. An observant and selective approach is a working interpretation. With Lester She examines his demiholumn condition and is attracted to him. He notices when her attention becomes personal and provokes her to act rather than continue observing. Neither knows his origin, and attraction does not resolve his contradictory history. Natalia can recognize contradiction as natural without acquiring a complete explanation of Lester. Their work keeps bringing them together. Neither the attraction nor an eventual encounter would answer all of her questions about his nature. Writing guardrail Let her be curious about something ordinary in him too. His anomalous nature need not account for all of her interest. Tien Basis: Occupational context established; intimate life unresolved Natural approach His work requires secrecy. Whether he carries the same habits into private relationships is not established. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. With a specific partner No partner is established. Helena is his employer and protected principal. Writing guardrail Do not turn an assassin's professional methods into a ready-made sexual personality. Lester Basis: Established tension with Natalia; personal history unresolved Natural approach Lester seeks direct experience and enjoys provoking Natalia. His response to being examined is part of their friction. Sexual expression No specific behavior is established. His demiholumn nature alone cannot supply it. With Natalia He wants her attention as a man as well as an unusual case. Her analytical distance gives him something to provoke, while their shared work gives the attraction repeated contact. Writing guardrail His ordinary tastes, humor, and irritation should remain available alongside the mystery of his body. Inspector Leo Basis: Marriage established; private life unresolved Natural approach His patience as an investigator offers one possible starting point. The archive does not yet establish how he behaves with his spouse. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. With a specific partner Leo is married. His spouse is not yet described. He has no established sexual tension with Natalia and remains outside the Magi world. Writing guardrail Establish the marriage through a scene before projecting his police habits onto it. Father Mikhail Basis: Clerical role established; private life unresolved Natural approach His history, personal attachments, and vows are not yet defined. Sexual expression No specific behavior is recorded. His mock blessing and blunt advice to Lynleit establish how he teases her using knowledge of her family, not how he behaves with a partner. With a specific partner No partner is established. Writing guardrail Neither celibacy nor a hidden romance follows from the title Father. Myka Basis: Familial closeness established; romantic history unresolved Natural approach to closeness Myka confides in Natalia about studies and personal worries. Natalia checks on her and sometimes treats her like a daughter. With a specific partner No romantic partner or sexual profile is recorded. Archive-wide writing principles Preserve each character's work, loyalties, and immediate objective. Use recurring contact specific to the pair. Shared danger can intensify attraction but does not establish it by itself. Distinguish attention from attraction and attraction from a promised relationship. Let gestures, interruptions, and choices carry implications without narrating the conclusion again. A useful encounter may leave a disagreement, an unanswered question, or a changed habit. Keep interpretations separate from confirmed preferences. Revisit them when new scenes supply evidence. Development sequence and thematic limits 1. Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge. 2. Doom's incomplete attempt, late in the second half of Arc 1. 3. Months of private theoretical study, followed by the spontaneous park encounter. 4. Reciprocal exploration and learning to receive as well as initiate. 5. First intercourse by mutual choice, followed by ordinary, playful intimacy. 6. Pregnancy near the Arc 1 transition; the son is born during Lynleit's disappearance. Arc 2 makes his existence legible to the reader, not automatically to Kyrien. 7. Lynleit keeps their son hidden from Kyrien and the wider world after his birth. The timing and circumstances of Kyrien's eventual discovery are undecided. 8. Restored intimacy during Arc 2 ultimately leads to the conception of their daughter and her later birth. The conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2. They have two children by the end of the story. These are separate milestones, not a conscious program Lynleit follows. Her duty remains primary. She was already a competent adult while Fionn lived; his death changes the structure of belonging and responsibility. The family she eventually forms with Kyrien is her choice, not compliance with a Cult duty or Fionn's selection of a successor. Arc 0's possible teenage encounter is non-romantic and unconfirmed. Do not backdate this adult sexual progression into the prequel. Established arc Mutual, slow to surface lynleit Lynleit Lynleit studies Kyrien first as a recruit whose failed attack nearly harmed her. Their card games make that scrutiny personal: she learns his tells and begins noticing his hands and breath. Later she attempts intimacy as a possible treatment for their shared curse, but remains interested after they survive without completing it. Mikhail's mock blessing exposes her family association with the Cult of Inanna. She counters with abstract principles and increasingly personal objections. His teasing does not create her attraction to Kyrien or make ancestry a reason for it. In the park, she wants to correct her private sense of failure, then finds satisfaction in knowing Kyrien as a particular person. Her theory follows an impulse already present. The preparation remains theoretical. Her attention shifts from proving competence toward learning his individual responses; the current park draft leaves that passage for the author rather than depicting it. kyrien Kyrien Kyrien wants to beat Lynleit at cards and dislikes finding that she can read him. Her elegance and nerve also attract him. He stays because he wants the battle, then finds himself facing private questions that her orders cannot answer. After the attempted intimacy, she will not tell him why their curse disappeared. He notices her pleasure in success and answers with a joke rather than a declaration. When she later asks for his flask, he does not force an explanation. The author also intends him to notice how being able to affect him changes her confidence. This reciprocal observation is not a shift into generic dominance. Quiet companionship and private tells matter alongside practical dependence and protected secrets. Her initiative, pride, and curiosity can reach him, but both must gradually allow themselves to be affected rather than continually managing what the other notices. Their intimacy includes being quietly recognized, accompanied, and challenged without their usual defenses; restraint can become unnecessary without making them talkative. The interrogation, card games, protected secret, and voluntary decision to stay give this pairing different kinds of familiarity. In Doom Has an Address, an incomplete attempt at intimacy breaks the shared curse. Lynleit loses the excuse of treatment without losing her interest in Kyrien; he is left trying to understand what happened. Their sexual relationship begins later in Arc 1. Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge precede Doom. Months afterward, a spontaneous park encounter lets Lynleit's curiosity and wounded pride become a successful private milestone. Oral intimacy, reciprocal exploration, first intercourse, and pregnancy remain separate. The family theme does not turn ancestry into an instruction or make grief itself attraction. Lynleit bears their son during her disappearance and later keeps him hidden from both Kyrien and the wider world. They restore intimacy during Arc 2 and eventually conceive a second child, a daughter, who is born later. The daughter's conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2, not within it. The author has confirmed this direction, not the scenes that restore intimacy or the timing of Kyrien's discovery of their son. Duty remains primary; a second child does not substitute for the work of reconnection. Established asymmetry Felix overt, Lynleit deflecting lynleit Lynleit Felix's flirting belongs to a long friendship she refuses to reorganize around his advances. Her ease with him, combined with the repeated refusal, creates visible chemistry without requiring matching sexual intent. felix Felix Lynleit is one of the few people his charm cannot simply move into the response he wants. Familiar affection, physical ease, and repeated deflection keep his attraction active even when he respects the boundary she has made. He remains internally fixated on her while growing close to Sherie through work. Enjoying Sherie's company does not immediately change whom he imagines being intimate with; his attachment to Lynleit takes more than successful flirtation to loosen. The tension is easy for readers to recognize because it already has a social rhythm: he advances through jokes and flirtation, she ignores or redirects him, and neither abandons the closeness underneath the exchange. It does not need to become a relationship to remain real. Emerging arc Mutual, unequally conscious yulia Yulia Hiyu irritates her into sustained attention. She keeps arguing, correcting, and following because his ideas have already occupied more of her mind than she wants to admit. Suppressed attraction can sharpen both her impatience and her awareness of his physical presence. hiyu Hiyu Yulia is the critic whose resistance makes an idea worth pursuing. He becomes dependent on her attention before he understands that the dependence is personal, leaving him oblivious to tension that is already changing how he seeks her out. Their arguments repeatedly force proximity and attention. They lean over the same evidence, reach for the same document, and forget ordinary distance while trying to prove incompatible explanations. Yulia notices first and steps away; Hiyu continues the theory and wonders why she moved. Her anger becomes disproportionate when his recklessness makes the possibility of losing him real. Hiyu recognizes the bond through absence: an investigation without her corrections becomes less interesting, and he keeps turning toward the place where she should be. Yulia and Hiyu become intimate by learning to communicate through the noise they already create together. Strong potential Situational and confrontational kyrien Kyrien Sherie's charm is too deliberate to disarm him, but the precision behind it earns his attention. He is more likely to watch for the moment her performance fails than reward the performance itself. sherie Sherie Kyrien's refusal to be steered threatens a skill she has internalized as part of her identity. Each failed attempt to produce a reaction can make his eventual attention feel more valuable and personally dangerous. Sherie uses language and calibrated flirtation to control the rhythm of an exchange. Kyrien answers with silence, literalism, or no usable reaction at all. Repeated negotiation could turn her professional frustration into sexual tension without making them compatible or displacing Kyrien's eventual relationship with Lynleit. Established marriage Mutual, damaged by exclusion fionn Fionn Fionn's affection and desire for Helena are genuine. He separates bodily and domestic closeness from the secrets he believes he must carry alone, never understanding that this division changes what their intimacy means to her. helena Helena Helena experiences desire alongside the need to be admitted into Fionn's complete life. Physical familiarity can therefore intensify resentment: she can be close enough to know his body while remaining excluded from the truth governing him. Their sexual tension survives inside a real marriage because attraction and grievance occupy the same private space. The closer they become physically, the harder it is for Helena to accept that Fionn still decides which parts of himself she is permitted to know. Established tension Mutual, differently expressed natalia Natalia Lester is the living exception that Natalia cannot finish classifying. Her professional attention can become personal before she recognizes the change, especially when he interrupts an examination by noticing that she is watching him rather than the phenomenon around him. lester Lester Natalia's analytical distance gives Lester something unusually difficult to provoke. He enjoys forcing the reserved researcher into immediate experience, but the tension changes when he wants her attention to recognize the man rather than examine the demiholumn condition. Repeated cases bring Natalia's examination of Lester into conflict with his insistence on being treated as more than a case. He provokes her to act; she notices more than he expected. Their attraction does not answer her questions about his demiholumn nature. Neither knows how he came into existence. His chronology is intrinsically contradictory, not a solvable transformation history. Natalia's recognition that contradiction belongs to nature does not mean she can explain him completely or that attraction answers the contradiction. Author-confirmed direction Gradual familiarity, uneven recognition sherie Sherie Sherie enjoys directing an exchange, while Felix teases back and complicates her control. As their work repeatedly overlaps, she finds room to become theatrical, petty, ridiculous, or openly delighted without losing his respect. She may recognize their intimate potential before he does. His fixation on Lynleit can hurt despite his responsive attention; her confidence does not remove disappointment, boundaries, or doubt about whether he sees her clearly. She gradually recognizes the seriousness beneath his jokes and becomes someone around whom he need not always entertain. felix Felix Felix enjoys Sherie's company, answers her teasing, and gradually seeks her out while remaining internally fixated on Lynleit. His attention is responsive, but he may interpret Sherie's interest as habitual charm or their closeness as an entertaining professional friendship. Emotional investment can precede his recognition of its intimate possibility. His attachment to Lynleit has genuine weight and takes more than successful flirtation to loosen. Moving toward Sherie eventually means recognizing her own importance to him and wanting her without treating her as a substitute for Lynleit. They have no meaningful personal relationship at the story's opening. Sherie's diplomatic responsibilities increasingly overlap with Felix's work around Lynleit and MSF, bringing repeated encounters before either chooses closeness. Familiarity, respect, private jokes, and a compatible rhythm develop gradually. Her confident, playful dominance meets his expressiveness, improvisation, and willingness to challenge her. Humor, visible enjoyment, mutual provocation, and occasional reversals carry into affection and eventual adult intimacy. Care becomes particularly revealing when one stops performing and the other remains attentive. Readers can notice Felix building intimacy's foundations with Sherie while still imagining it with Lynleit; narration need not explain that contradiction. The later teasing challenge to Lynleit remains, but it neither starts their familiarity nor reduces Sherie's interest to winning him. This differs from Lynleit's strategic recruitment of Kyrien and their quieter recognition through restrained attention, protected secrets, and gradually accepted vulnerability. Both couples remain subplots beneath the political and supernatural story. The direction is confirmed; particular encounters, recognition, boundaries, and chronology remain unwritten. tien No current pairing contains enough personal exposure beyond professional dependency or operational rivalry. heyk No current pairing is supported. Shared danger and survivor's grief do not create sexual tension on their own. drake No current pairing has the repeated personal friction needed to move beyond abstract compatibility. reiner No current pairing is supported. His long-standing bond with Lynleit remains protective rather than romantic. inspector-leo Leo is married and remains outside the hidden Magi world. No sexual-tension pairing beyond his marriage is supported. father-mikhail No current pairing is supported. His vows, private history, and relationship to desire remain undefined. myka No current record. Character Archive

entries.title: Content Audit: 19 September 2026
entries.subtitle: Archive Audit
entries.text: Content Audit: 19 September 2026 Archive Audit Prose, character, chronology, and scene-evidence corrections, with the remaining story decisions identified. Content Audit: 19 September 2026 Scope: the current/default eight Chapters, 25 Moments, 18 character profiles, Story phases, World records, six weapon records, two Items & Artefacts records, active writer references, and Gallery and Music descriptions. Historical revisions were checked where needed for source and version continuity, not rewritten. This is a content audit, not an interface or code-architecture review. Overall judgment The strongest material puts particular people inside an immediate problem: Felix's newspaper at the end of the Nameless Street, the river team's failed watches and card games, Natalia making Lynleit work through an example, and Mikhail letting a ceremony become a personal provocation. Those scenes already have recognizable voices. Their pauses, repetitions, and ordinary objects deserve protection. The main weakness is uneven development. The river and Doom are extensively dramatized, while the political conspiracy, the fugitive campaign, Cardiff, and the Academy still depend heavily on summaries. As a result, the archive explains several relationships and institutions more fully than the story has yet demonstrated them. Cutting the developed scenes would not fix that imbalance. The missing operations need their own decisions, setbacks, and consequences when their facts are chosen. A second weakness is drift between a scene and its summary. An interpretation becomes a rule, a later consequence becomes a witnessed event, or an open placement becomes an asserted sequence. This pass corrects those transitions without inventing the missing answers. Corrections made Scene evidence and chronology The river Chapter v2 repairs a contradictory sightline: the pair move beneath the park trees but can still see parts of the opposite embankment through gaps. Dialogue and action otherwise remain unchanged. The river Moment v3 no longer claims Kyrien saw the underwater flame. It describes his evasive answer instead of calling it a flat denial. The girl's head tilt suggests bewilderment without proving the Holumn's governing rule. Lynleit's attention to his breathing is not attributed to an unshown reciprocal thought. The Nameless Street Moment v2 separates the chapter's events from the urban legend and Fionn's later death. Felix takes her distress seriously; the chapter does not show him accepting a fully recounted supernatural explanation. The counteroffensive phase no longer makes discovering the coat a prerequisite for beginning the campaign. The battle-as-reward exchange no longer places Kyrien's voluntary decision to remain after it without evidence. Myka's recruitment is certain; its placement after Lynleit's disappearance remains open. The Moment no longer states the working Arc 2 placement as fact. Lynleit is included among the participants in Fionn's assassination Moment because finding his body and being accused are central to that record. River panels explicitly link to Chapter v2 and Moment v3. Their alternative compositions remain artwork of the same beats, not additional events. Characterization and tone Natalia is Lynleit's favourite teacher. Whether Lynleit was Natalia's favourite student remains a question; the profile and Academy record no longer answer it accidentally. Kyrien's practical escape skills no longer imply an absolute refusal of unfavorable fights or an indifference to victory. His competitive impulse can compromise otherwise careful preparation. Lynleit's Arc 2 appearance entry describes visible design. Childbirth and her absence stay in biography, where their sequence is clearer. Kyrien's profile explicitly attributes concealment of their son to Lynleit. Ash's arrival is a domestic interlude. Nothing in the scene establishes a supernatural omen. Yulia and Hiyu's scene facts describe their habits rather than MBTI codes. Proposed proximity and absence beats in the tension reference are explicitly suggestions, not completed encounters. Tien's relationship pronoun is corrected. Heyk's evacuation no longer has an unsupported duration. Lester's unknown limits are stated as unknown, not as instructions to develop him. Natalia's examination methods no longer borrow a physician analogy. No magic-aware medical profession was added. World and reference accuracy Profiles distinguish Mikhail's possible treatment from the later successful outcome in Doom. The Chapter remains v7. A Moment wording error now attributes his observation to his interpretation of Lynleit's behavior. The Holumn registry no longer calls the puzzle victim's disappearance permanent. A missing person's return remains unknown, not impossible. The Nameless Street record has the direction of recollection right: its dead boy comes back to Lynleit when she later finds Fionn. That resemblance does not establish prophecy or causation. The incident reference distinguishes possible institutional readings from completed investigations. The single puzzle case is not expanded into an unsupported cluster. Doom's illness can look ordinary to an outsider, but its attempted magical treatments are not attributed to physicians. The observed cure does not become a universal treatment for curses. The Magiarchy succession text no longer says the office itself causes Lynleit's absence. The Director's House no longer assigns unspecified bedrooms to the second floor. Real firearm comparisons stay in conceptual references rather than implying an in-world 1911/2011 lineage for the Swan or real-product membership for the Rook. Music concepts no longer describe an unavailable recording as though its musical execution exists, or imply that the Spill's danger has ended. Advisory behavior notes require author acceptance. Merely displaying a note beside a scene cannot make it canon. Questions no longer assume an unconfirmed near miss, retaliation, physical intimacy, or lasting river alteration. The two already-written surveillance anomalies are no longer requested as missing scene details. What still needs author decisions or new scenes 1. The main political chain. Choose the concrete actions by criminal Magi, foreign Magiarchates, Church actors, and Helena that converge on Fionn. Their different motives are established; their causal sequence is not. No faction was made the sole mastermind. 2. Cardiff and the Academy. The parallel dispatches and rescue structure are sound. The threat, local objective, moral choices, and lasting costs still need definition. Myka needs a consequential decision of her own, not only a summary saying she learned enough to graduate first. 3. The fugitive campaign. The refuge and reconnection are useful anchors. The operations between them and Helena's defeat need material obstacles and failures before the institutional reversal can feel earned. 4. Doom's reciprocal change. Lynleit's embarrassment is vividly dramatized; Kyrien's inner change is less visible. V7 explicitly supplies the cure explanation. A future revision could make his changed understanding more legible through one specific action, but that action and any change to the concluding explanation have not been chosen here. 5. The early archive outline. The Name Left Behind still contains temporary material about Myka, an erased record, and Fionn's name beside a future date. It should not quietly become proof for the main conspiracy, Lester, or Bone Archive. 6. Later family revelations. Preserve the two-child direction, the son's reader reveal versus Kyrien's knowledge, and the daughter's post-Arc 2 legibility. Exact scenes, timing, and arrangements are still open. 7. Sherie and Felix. Their uneven attachment is well specified as a direction. It needs repeated professional encounters, a moment of Sherie's disappointment, and Felix's recognition of her independent significance. No shortcut through successful flirting was added. 8. Holumn uncertainty. The river's surface boundary, Sleepers' meaning, Bone Archive access, and the particulars of Lester's contradictory biography need evidence before explanations. Unknown does not mean interchangeable: each new encounter should add a distinct trace, limit, or cost. The Questions ledger holds the unresolved choices. No new incompatible canon was selected; the Contradictions ledger records the reconciliations. Preserved deliberately Doom's extended banter, Natalia's practical teaching, the church comedy, the nonsexual refuge, the park writer gap, Lynleit's duty-first priorities, Felix's fixation while Sherie grows important, and the separate river Holumns remain intact. No MBTI type, capability score, magic power, family milestone, or unplaced event received a new answer. The advisory Nasu framework and sexual-tension workflow were used to test evidence, consequences, character-specific attention, and asymmetry. They did not supply an absent author's approval or authorize imitation of another writer's prose. Publication and verification Revised documents and scene records retain their earlier published versions. The river's original Chapter file is unchanged. Small copy corrections within an unchanged scene are recorded as errata rather than new plot variants. The Home feed links this audit. Validation covers generated cross-references, current and historical document dependencies, paragraph-note anchors, scene links, search entries, and browser readers. The automated prose review is a prompt for judgment, not a ban on repeated words. Remaining alerts largely concern editorial records describing version history or characters literally remaining in a place. Author's Desk

entries.text: Contradictions to Resolve Editorial Ledger Current cross-version decisions, including Doom v7 and the park v2 correction. Contradictions to Resolve This ledger contains only places where two current records cannot both be read literally without clarification. Unanswered lore and missing detail belong in Questions to Be Answered instead. Rows are ordered from least resolved to most resolved. Once a contradiction is fully resolved, its outcome should be integrated into every affected record and the row should be removed. Contradiction ledger No unresolved contradiction is currently recorded. The Bench under the Lamp v2 supersedes v1's invented kiss, which the author explicitly rejected. The current Chapter and Moment preserve the supplied approach and a marked writer gap. V1 remains an archived alternate, not evidence for the current relationship. Intimacy guidance distinguishes author-confirmed intent from the still-undrafted passage. Current version decision Doom Has an Address v7 supplies current shared canon. The Bench under the Lamp uses v2. Earlier revisions remain accessible as historical alternatives and do not override these choices. Decision history On 23 September 2026, the author selected the motorboat depicted in the new Sleepers panels for the written scene. Sleepers above the River v2 replaces rowing with an outboard motor; v1 preserves the rowing draft. The seven-panel sequence links to v2. The passive figures, unknown chronology, and unfinished downstream journey remain unchanged. On 23 September 2026, After the Failed Attempt v3 and its two matching Moments replace the earlier outline's confirmed Magus politician with a senior prosecutor promoted to Prosecutor General, whose own magical status is undecided. The failure is partly due to a concealed magical connection, not solely proof of personal magecraft. His father is a military-police commander murdered under suppression sanction. Credible legal evidence precedes institutional refusal, then an interval and the shop humiliation. MSF can support a represented release arrangement, not assume unrestricted police or judicial control. Profiles, World context, reader knowledge, and current advisory records follow v3; Chapter and Moment v1/v2 retain their incompatible earlier wording as history. Later revenge requires a separate genuine offence, not retroactive invalidation of the protected original operation. The entries below describe successive author decisions, not competing instructions for current records. On 13 September 2026, the author clarified Only Eyes for You as the culmination of Felix repeatedly flirting with nuns during church visits by Lynleit and Fionn, accompanied by Felix and Reiner. Reiner behaves; Lynleit eventually loses patience. The Moment's v2, profiles, and current advisory references replace the earlier open jealous reading with accumulated irritation. V1 and the earlier document snapshots remain historical. The visits precede Fionn's death; precise placement and church business remain questions, not contradictions. On 12 September 2026, the author established that Sherie and Felix begin without a meaningful personal relationship and grow close through repeated professional encounters. Intimacy Reference v9, the current tension registry, and their profiles replace v8's immediate-chemistry and competitive-conquest framing. Felix remains fixated on Lynleit during that development. The later teasing exchange between Sherie and Lynleit is retained, but no longer serves as the origin of Sherie's interest. Specific encounters and chronology remain questions, not contradictions. On 5 September 2026, v4 replaced v3 with practical teaching, personal examples, and Lynleit's familiar student-friend dialogue. It added Natalia's decision-diary experiment, resignation anecdote, and concern over Myka's missed call. Magi examined the curse; Natalia introduced the ego hypothesis and quoted Jung. These additions survive in v7. V1's completed encounter remains incompatible with the incomplete attempt preserved by current canon. On 6 September 2026, v5 added Mikhail's mock blessing, alluding to Fionn's Magi-lineage association with the Cult of Inanna. Lynleit remained indirectly associated without direct participation. The exchange did not change the curse mechanism or incomplete attempt. Later on 6 September 2026, v6 named Inanna and described the lineage's long Cult association openly. This replaced v5's concealed identification and remains spoken information in v7, not a reader inference. The curse outcome and Lynleit's indirect association were unchanged. On 6 September 2026, the author approved all nine proposed restorations for Doom v7. The default Chapter and Moment, character interpretation, intimacy reference, and current prose guidance follow v7. V6 remains an archived alternate. The restoration expands performance and reveals a moment of restraint without changing the named family connection, the curse mechanism, incomplete attempt, or later chronology. No new cross-version contradiction results. On 8 September 2026, the author resolved the backlog's inconsistent sequence: Fionn's death, then the nonsexual hotel refuge, then Doom in the later part of Arc 1's second half. Its exact placement remains open. The successful park encounter follows months later and is distinct from later intercourse. Current Moments, phases, profiles, intimacy records, and guidance follow this sequence; archived versions preserve their earlier wording. The prequel outline does not move Lynleit's mother's death from junior school into her teenage years, give Kyrien magical schooling, or establish an optional forgotten meeting as fact. Author clarification: 11 September 2026 The Drowned Choir and river leviathan are separate Holumns. General disappearances and returns do not share one destination or mechanism. Lester's contradictory biography is deliberate ontology, not an editorial inconsistency requiring a causal repair. These decisions are integrated into the current Holumn and character records. The family direction now includes a son born during Lynleit's disappearance and a daughter following restored intimacy in Arc 2. The daughter is understood only after Arc 2; Kyrien's discovery of the son remains undecided. Historical document and Moment versions retain their earlier wording. Character clarification: 12 September 2026 The author’s MBTI discussion supplies confirmed habits of attention and physical competence, recorded in the Cognition reference. The profiles now distinguish suspected INFJ for Lynleit and ENFP for Felix from Sherie’s retained ENFJ; Kyrien remains a suspected ISTP with INTJ open. Earlier labels are preserved in historical guidance. Type interpretation is unresolved evidence, not a conflict between two events. No new training history, scene, chronology, or capability score follows from a typing change. Consistency cleanup: 12 September 2026 Hidden World Foundation v2 now follows Lester’s established contradictory ontology; v1 preserves the superseded origin possibilities as history. The current river incident and testimony record only the boundary observed beneath water-walking Lynleit and no longer assert a speaking choir. Its mechanism remains a question. After the Failed Attempt v2 removes the duplicate entrance and uses the already-established MSF transfer clause; its two linked Moments retain matching v1 and v2 access. These are reconciliations with existing canon, not new origin or reveal decisions. Content reconciliation: 19 September 2026 The river Chapter's v2 keeps the city bank visible through gaps in the park trees; v1's contradictory sightline remains historical. Its v3 Moment and the Nameless Street v2 separate scene evidence from later events and archive explanations. The related river panels now link explicitly to those revised records. The advisers' uncertain treatment proposal and the later narrated cure remain distinct. Doom v7 is unchanged apart from a Moment wording correction that attributes Mikhail's observation to him, not to Lynleit's response. Natalia's preference among her former students, Myka's recruitment date, and the Director's House second-floor layout are unresolved choices, not established facts. Current records no longer assert answers. Ash's domestic scene does not establish a supernatural omen. Earlier Moment and document revisions preserve the superseded wording. Author's Desk

entries.title: Dread and Action Direction · v1
entries.subtitle: Writer's Direction
entries.text: Dread and Action Direction · v1 Writer's Direction The initial dread and action guidance, with external reference framing removed at the author's request. Dread and Action Direction MAGIARCHY's dangerous places should evoke isolation, apprehension, grimness, and the urgency of surviving. People enter them with work to do, incomplete knowledge, and abilities that remain useful even when their safety is uncertain. This author-approved preference supplements the story's political, supernatural, and domestic life. Read alongside Prose Style, Prose and Scene Guidance, Thematic Direction, and Hidden World Foundation. These are writing principles, not new incidents, abilities, or historical facts. Different ways to face danger Competence under pressure Useful action should be satisfying to follow. A trained person notices an opening, commits, and changes the situation. The pressure comes from what remains beyond that competence: divided attention, a person to retrieve, a narrowing route, or an incomplete understanding. Avoid making professionals forget their training merely to create fear. Composure without security A character may move elegantly and solve immediate problems while remaining uncertain about an employer, an ally, or the next room. Composure can persist because there is a task to finish, not because the person feels secure. Effective movement and a restrained expression need not conceal the situation's cost from the reader. Preserve each character's own manner rather than giving everyone the same cool response. Restricted means, meaningful initiative A limited means of affecting danger can be enough to make a frightened person's decisions compelling. Let timing, observation, persistence, or a small practical act matter. A person who cannot defeat a threat may still delay it, help someone else move, or recognize a route. Such an opportunity must fit the encounter's established properties. Vulnerability need not mean waiting for another person to solve the entire scene. Fear close to the body A threshold can become a decision. A character needs something beyond it, knows enough to be afraid, and lacks the assurance of a clean return. Fear may interfere with a hand movement, a breath, or attention, but its expression belongs to this individual. Do not give everyone visible panic or assign vulnerability by sex. Curiosity, duty, and concern for another person can keep someone moving despite fear. Learning a little from an earlier encounter can change the next attempt without granting sudden fearlessness. The same place may feel quite different to a prepared officer and a stranded witness; preserve the physical consequences of the first person's actions if another arrives later. Environment before encounter Make the place legible enough to worry about. Establish the useful arrangement: where the exit is, what interrupts sight, where another person waits, and what the protagonist must cross. Withhold the explanation of danger, not the basic blocking needed to understand an action. If a Holumn changes space, time, or perception, first provide enough ordinary reference for the violation to register. Choose a few specific sensory details that affect behavior. A sound beyond a wall or on the floor above may establish distance before its source appears. A wet surface may change footing. Light can reveal an outline without identifying it; making everything darker is not a substitute for choosing what remains visible. Silence matters when the reader has heard what normally occupies that space. Repeated vague noises and ominous adjectives cease to supply information. For a location brief, identify its ordinary purpose, the lives or work still visible there, the feature that has become unreliable, and the practical route through it. Keep Narvea's contemporary buildings, communications, domestic life, and older institutional inheritance. Grimness need not mean abandoned Gothic interiors everywhere. A maintained, occupied place can fail its inhabitants; daylight and other people do not automatically supply help.
