entries.title: Ren L17 “Sparrow”
entries.subtitle: Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm
entries.text: Ren L17 “Sparrow” Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm Ren L17 Sparrow 9×17 mm / .380 ACP Compact institutional and concealed-carry sidearm Small, discreet, elegant institutional pistol Standard-issued pistol for every MSF officer who has passed weapons certification. MSF purchases the Sparrow from Ren Arms and does not manufacture firearms. A slim silver-and-charcoal pistol built around the older Ren Arms metal-frame language. The brushed silver slide is elongated for its height, with a beveled nose, a long shallow ejection-port cut, a narrow rear serration block, and the RN shield set behind the caliber mark. The dark frame rises into an exposed hammer and a smooth, gently curved backstrap. Brushed silver slide over a dark charcoal frame Beveled muzzle and gently rounded upper profile Exposed serrated hammer and low conventional sights Deeply inset grip panels with broad, smooth palm surfaces Curved trigger, restrained slide controls, and no external manual safety Short extended magazine base that adds purchase without changing the narrow silhouette Despite the Sparrow's older design lineage, current-production models omit an external manual safety to reflect the demands and handling priorities of modern combat. The silver finish is standard to the firearm and is not an MSF customization. Routine issue gradually makes the ordinary Ren Arms product visually associated with MSF officers. Its small size, light visual presence, discretion, and modest chambering. lynleit Lynleit Carries the issued Sparrow as her personal sidearm. Walther PPK SIG Sauer P230 Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L19 “Magpie”
entries.subtitle: Heavier compact service pistol
entries.text: Ren L19 “Magpie” Heavier compact service pistol Ren L19 Magpie 9×19 mm Heavier compact service pistol Larger, louder, and heavier relative of the Sparrow An enlarged silver-and-charcoal development of the Sparrow for 9×19 mm. The longer brushed slide, taller dark frame, extended grip, and squared accessory profile give it more mass without abandoning the exposed hammer or the older Ren Arms silhouette. The illustration shows the optional muzzle compensator and extended magazine installed, making the pistol visibly longer in both directions than its base configuration. Brushed silver slide with a long upper relief cut Exposed serrated hammer and conventional raised sights Dark charcoal frame with the Sparrow family's curved backstrap and inset grip panels Restrained slide controls and no external manual safety Optional squared compensator with two open top ports Optional extended magazine projecting below the grip for added hand support Despite the Magpie's older design lineage, current-production models omit an external manual safety to reflect the demands and handling priorities of modern combat. Two optional attachments help the compact pistol remain controllable under the stronger recoil of its 9×19 cartridge. Attachable compensator Reduces muzzle rise and helps the shooter maintain control under the Magpie's greater recoil. Extended magazine Adds gripping surface for firmer recoil control while also increasing ammunition capacity. It fills the space between a discreet institutional pistol and a full modern duty handgun. Its close relationship to the Sparrow, with a larger, louder, heavier, and more noticeable character. SIG Sauer P230 aesthetic lineage SIG Sauer P225 / P239-type proportions Compact CZ influence Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L21 “Rook”
entries.subtitle: Micro-compact personal-defense and close-protection pistol
entries.text: Ren L21 “Rook” Micro-compact personal-defense and close-protection pistol Ren L21 Rook 9×19 mm Micro-compact personal-defense and close-protection pistol Smallest modern polymer-frame pistol in the family A common personal purchase for self-defense and a favored private sidearm among style-conscious MSF officers. Felix owns an L21 and later lends it to Lynleit when her continued reliance on the weaker 9×17 Sparrow concerns him. The Rook is a short, dense 9×19 mm pistol derived from the L24 Crow but reduced in slide, dust-cover, and grip length. Its black polymer frame and dark steel slide keep the mass low, while brass-colored details at the barrel, trigger, slide lock, and magazine release distinguish it from an ordinary service finish. Interlocking diagonal serrations at both ends of the slide give the small pistol a more intricate personal character than the Crow. Short dark steel slide over a compact black polymer frame Brass-colored barrel visible at the muzzle and through the ejection port Brass-colored trigger, slide lock, and magazine release Dense crossed serration fields at the front and rear of the slide Squared trigger guard with an undercut and a short accessory rail Extended magazine base that completes the firing grip without giving the pistol Crow-length proportions Ghost Comp is the Rook's compensated premium configuration. The smallest modern polymer-frame 9×19 mm pistol on the Narvean market. Its size and chambering support discreet defensive carry, while its brass details and elaborate serrations make it more individual than a standard service gun. A compact, practical, intelligent bird with more confidence and modern utility than a Sparrow. felix Felix Owns an L21 as his personal sidearm. lynleit Lynleit Later carries Felix's L21 on loan when he objects to her continued reliance on the 9×17 Sparrow. Walther P22Q SIG Sauer P365 XL SIG Sauer P365 Spectre Comp Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L24 “Crow”
entries.subtitle: Standard compact law-enforcement and military secondary sidearm
entries.text: Ren L24 “Crow” Standard compact law-enforcement and military secondary sidearm Ren L24 Crow 9×19 mm Standard compact law-enforcement and military secondary sidearm Default compact state-service pistol The Crow is the preferred default secondary sidearm for Narvean law enforcement and military service. It is widely issued because it is conventional, dependable, and easy to treat as ordinary equipment rather than a specialist selection. The Crow is the compact workhorse of the modern Ren Arms family and the parent design of the smaller L21 Rook. Its dark steel slide and black polymer frame are longer and taller than the Rook, with simpler parallel serrations, a full compact grip, and neutral metal controls. The proportions remain short enough for concealed and protective work while giving the firing hand more uninterrupted surface than the micro-compact model. Dark charcoal steel slide and black polymer frame Full compact grip with a textured central panel and sculpted finger channel Straight parallel serrations at both ends of the slide Broad central slide flats with an understated caliber mark Squared undercut trigger guard and short accessory rail Neutral silver trigger and restrained controls Flush compact magazine and conventional duty sights It is the boring default of the current service family: common, dependable, and unremarkable enough to disappear into police and military equipment. Its common, capable, dark, and practical character. Glock 19 CZ P-10 C Compact modern service pistols Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L28 “Raven”
entries.subtitle: Advanced full-size law-enforcement and military service pistol
entries.text: Ren L28 “Raven” Advanced full-size law-enforcement and military service pistol Ren L28 Raven 9×19 mm Advanced full-size law-enforcement and military service pistol Performance-oriented service upgrade Police and military officers may request the Raven in place of the standard Crow when they favor better accuracy and performance. Reiner prefers the Raven. The Raven is the advanced full-size counterpart to the standard Crow. Its long dark slide carries five rounded forward windows that expose the bright barrel, while deep rear serrations, a full-length sculpted grip, and a squared frame give it greater visual weight than the Crow. A blue trigger provides the only vivid accent within an otherwise restrained service finish. Long dark-charcoal slide with broad uninterrupted side flats Five rounded forward slide windows exposing the bright barrel Deep straight rear serrations and raised conventional sights Full-size sculpted grip with finger channels and inset textured panels Squared trigger guard, extended dust cover, and accessory rail Blue trigger set against restrained black controls Flush full-size magazine and a small lanyard loop at the heel A serious performance-focused service pistol rather than a luxury model. Its barrel windows and blue trigger distinguish an officer-selected upgrade without moving it into the Swan's crafted role. A larger, darker, and more imposing service weapon than the Rook or Crow. reiner Reiner Prefers the Raven over the standard Crow for its accuracy and performance. Glock 17 Walther PDP Full Size Full-size modern service pistols Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Ren L31 “Swan”
entries.subtitle: Luxury long-slide pistol
entries.text: Ren L31 “Swan” Luxury long-slide pistol Ren L31 Swan 9×19 mm Luxury long-slide pistol Luxury flagship of the Ren Arms pistol family The Swan is a luxury long-slide pistol with an exposed hammer. A silver slide and upper frame sit over a black grip module, while the brass-colored barrel is visible through a row of elongated side windows and at the muzzle. The extended dust cover, long sight radius, skeletonized controls, flared beavertail, and sculpted frame give it a long, narrow profile. Long brushed-silver slide with a row of elongated forward windows Brass-colored barrel visible through the slide and at the muzzle Black lower frame with an extended dust cover and accessory rail Exposed skeletonized hammer, long beavertail, and fitted thumb safety Lightened trigger and raised precision sights Deeply textured black grip with sculpted front and rear purchase Fine rear slide serrations and a polished script model mark A luxury sidearm outside ordinary standard issue. Its long slide, exposed mechanism, ported presentation, and mixed metal finishes give it a crafted appearance distinct from the modern duty line. Length, grace, refinement, and composure. A Raven remains a full-size duty weapon; a Swan is visibly crafted, controlled, and personal. Premium 2011 pistols Premium 1911 pistols Desert Eagle SIG GTO Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea

entries.title: Holumns
entries.subtitle: Manifestations, effects, and evidence
entries.text: Holumns Manifestations, effects, and evidence Holumn is a category of manifestation, not a biological species. A Holumn may be a physical creature, a natural phenomenon, a repeating event, a disembodied will, or a curse. Its shape follows the fear, memory, fixation, or psychic fracture that gives it pressure. No universal weakness exists. A useful countermeasure must answer the rule expressed by the manifestation. An incident may reveal an effect without revealing the whole Holumn behind it. Being taken means entering a state imposed by a particular Holumn. There is no universal destination, and the effect need not involve spatial travel. A Holumn can disrupt mind, memory, identity, physical continuity, chronology, or causality. Death, madness, altered reality, and contradictory conditions are among the possible results. Holumn activity can produce conditions resembling life after death or reanimate a corpse. Reanimation does not by itself restore the original person or establish ordinary resurrection. A taken person can return. The mechanism and the continuity of that person depend on the Holumn involved; neither can be assumed from their reappearance. The Drowned Choir and the river leviathan are separate Holumns, not manifestations of one river-bound intelligence. Jungian synchronicity is a conceptual analogy: a Holumn could make a synchronicity-like condition inhabitable or imprisoning. This does not establish a specific manifestation or incident. Lester's demiholumn biography contradicts chronological continuity. Neither he nor Natalia knows his origin; understanding it lies beyond the horizon of human singularity and normal human comprehension. Natalia recognizes contradiction as intrinsic to nature, not simply an error in reality. No discoverable transformation, experiment, infection, or ordinary supernatural mechanism explains his existence. Certain Holumn incidents during the Spill produce unusual amounts of fog or mist, especially around Vilen’s park and river. Ordinary Narvean fog also occurs; fog alone does not identify a Holumn or establish one shared mechanism. embodied Embodied A creature or body that occupies physical space, including forms that move without being alive. HI-003 HI-004 environmental Environmental Weather, water, terrain, or another natural system becomes the body or behavior of the manifestation. HI-003 HI-004 HI-005 event Event-bound The Holumn exists as a sequence, compulsion, rule, or occurrence with no creature that can be confronted directly. HI-002 HI-005 HI-006 HI-008 disembodied Disembodied A voice, memory, desire, or will acquires agency without a stable body of its own. HI-001 curse Curse-bound A person, object, place, or action carries a hostile rule that persists until its particular condition is interrupted. HI-001 HI-002 HI-005 HI-006 HI-008

entries.subtitle: Objects, relics, and anomalous holdings
entries.text: Items & Artefacts Objects, relics, and anomalous holdings Story-relevant objects, artefacts, and other nonhuman holdings that are not weapons or Holumns. IA-001 leviathan-hide-coat The garment chooses its appearance Protection requires action What the coat does not solve How the object enters Lynleit's life 2026-09-05 Leviathan-hide coat Anomalous garment Held by Lynleit A blue garment left to Lynleit through Fionn's concealed intervention. It changes form without accepting commands and shields only what Lynleit deliberately covers with it. Lynleit lynleit Fionn fionn Arranged the substitution before his death A material called the hide of leviathan The nature and source of the material are not identified. Blue coat Its familiar full-length form and the appearance in which Lynleit first understands what Fionn left her. Scarf A smaller form chosen by the garment without instruction from Lynleit. Blue suede jacket The garment can imitate the fitted jacket Lynleit lost during the Drowned Choir attack. Other clothing The coat can assume other wearable forms. Lynleit cannot choose which form appears on a given day. Minor magical protection The material can shield a covered body from minor magically induced damage and phenomena. Protection by coverage Wearing the garment is not sufficient. Lynleit must use it to cover the threatened part of her body. Protection of another person Lynleit can remove the garment and place or throw it over someone who needs immediate protection. Autonomous form The garment decides its own appearance. It does not respond to Lynleit's preference or tactical need. Protection is local to the area physically covered by the garment. The garment does not provide passive protection merely because Lynleit is wearing it. Lynleit cannot command its form or rely on it to assume the form most useful to the situation. How much magical force the coat can withstand is unknown. Arc 1 The river operation The lost jacket The Drowned Choir tears away Lynleit's fitted blue suede jacket while dragging her underwater. She later complains about losing it because she liked it. Arc 1 Middle of the main story Fionn's concealed substitution After Fionn's death, Lynleit discovers that he had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wore with the leviathan-hide garment. Arc 1 After the discovery An inherited protection Lynleit carries the garment after discovering its properties. It sometimes takes the form of the suede jacket she lost. Moment The Coat Fionn Left Behind moments.html?moment=the-coat-fionn-left-behind Lynleit discovers the substitution and the garment's properties. Character Lynleit character.html?character=lynleit#equipment-title Lynleit carries the coat and uses it to shield herself or others. Character Fionn character.html?character=fionn Fionn arranged the substitution without explaining it to Lynleit. IA-002 kyriens-whiskey-flask 2026-09-08 Kyrien's whiskey flask Personal field object Carried by Kyrien A small flask of whiskey that Kyrien keeps for difficult moments rather than routine drinking. Kyrien kyrien Unspecified Small personal flask Kept in a consistent pocket; Lynleit learns where to find it. Measured use Kyrien takes a small drink before or after exceptional danger, distress, exhaustion, cold field conditions, or a difficult personal decision. Private pause He opens it, drinks, closes it, and carries on. He occasionally calls the whiskey medicine. No magical properties are established. The whiskey is a personal comfort, not medical treatment or a source of combat ability. Kyrien does not drink continually during ordinary work or conversation. Unplaced Origin unconfirmed Origin The precise source of the flask and the beginning of the habit are not known. Arc 1 Field work A familiar ritual Kyrien carries it through difficult work, and Lynleit becomes familiar with it. entries.title: MSF
entries.text: MSF # msf Institutional record Known facts only World / MSF MSF Private intelligence contractor MSF MSF is a fully private intelligence business that sells its services to the government. The initials are used publicly without a formal expansion. Fionn built a second purpose beneath its contracted work, preparing mostly ordinary people to approach threats they were never told existed. Legal status Fully private business Primary client Narvean government Headquarters Turon Full name Deliberately unrevealed 01 Dual mandate What members see depends on where they stand CONTRACTED FUNCTION Government services MSF sells intelligence, investigation, security, and operational services to the government while remaining institutionally private. FOUNDER'S DESIGN Contingency structure Fionn quietly shaped MSF so it could confront magical crises. Most members were not told that this purpose, or magic itself, existed. PERMANENT CONVERGENCE Two threat domains The Spill is never fully contained. MSF must shrink into a mainly Magi-focused task force while continuing to handle the ordinary intelligence threats it was created to confront. MSF assists with security at the Prosecutor General's appointment dinner. That work gives Lynleit access to the investigation after Kyrien's failed attack. Her contract-based proposal can support his release into paid confidential service, but requires the responsible authorities' approval and his lawyer's review. MSF does not acquire unrestricted police or judicial authority over his case. Open the recruitment → When Mikhail discovers that Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner know about magic, Lynleit refuses to surrender them. She begins bringing part of MSF into the Magi world, where the agency will answer to the Magiarchy and the Church. Open the turning point → See the Church record → 02 Ownership and control The government buys access, not ownership PRIVATE GOVERNANCE Its client cannot run the company The government can negotiate contracts, purchase defined services, and decide whether to keep buying them. It has little authority over MSF's succession, command culture, internal appointments, or ordinary workings beyond the access MSF chooses to permit. MSF may also accept clients beyond the government, exposing the danger of a private contract whose obligations conflict with Narvea's interests. Government power Contract, payment, and requested scope MSF control Clients, succession, personnel, command, and internal rules POLITICAL NICKNAME “A legal mafia.” Politically savvy citizens use the joke because MSF combines private loyalty, public contracts, internal succession, and enough concentrated force to make the state uneasy, all while operating within the law. RESIDENTIAL NODE The Director's House Fionn's family residence also supports selected MSF work through its offices and library, while the formal headquarters remains in Turon. → STANDARD SIDEARM Ren L17 "Sparrow" Every MSF officer who passes weapons certification is issued the compact 9×17 pistol. MSF buys the pistol from Ren Arms and manufactures no weapons. → 03 Cryptology in plain sight Authority is worn in blue MSF · B01 ENCRYPTED M.O. A visible signal that looks ordinary Fionn built cryptology into everyday appearance. A deliberate blue garment initiates recognition, but it does not authenticate authority by itself. Top officers follow it with an innocuous challenge-response hidden inside ordinary conversation. Anyone can buy a blue coat. Only someone trusted by Fionn knows how to answer a question that sounds like small talk. Initiation Blue clothing Verification Conversational challenge-response Audience Top officers trusted by Fionn Origin Fionn's private protocol KNOWN USER Lynleit Her blue coat or jacket initiates Fionn's recognition sequence. Even while she is accused and hunted, she can complete the private exchange known to officers he personally trusted. Open Lynleit's profile → LEGITIMACY FAILURE Helena Fionn's most conservative old officers notice Helena's ignorance first. The people least inclined toward rebellion begin questioning her because strict obedience to the founder's protocol now requires disobedience toward his official successor. Open Helena's profile → 04 Command succession Fionn leaves no publicly named successor MSF is a private family enterprise, and its leaders settle succession internally. Fionn deliberately refuses to identify one uncontested successor because he believes a declared heir would become an obvious target. His death divides the inheritance: Lynleit eventually becomes the new Magiarch, while Kyrien inherits the MSF director's seat during her absence. The government has little standing to settle the vacancy, and Fionn's security measure produces the succession crisis it was intended to prevent. 01 Fionn Founder without a declared heir Distributes trust through private protocols and overlapping circles, but refuses to turn any one candidate into a visible target. 02 Helena Contested inheritance Takes control after Fionn's elimination and frames Lynleit for his death. Her ignorance of his private authority protocol gradually gives influential officers reason to doubt the legitimacy of her succession. 03 Lynleit Restoration and contraction Fights to clear her name and reclaim the agency. Because the Spill cannot be fully contained, she reshapes MSF into a smaller task force centered on Magi while preserving its intelligence function. 04 Kyrien Non-Magus director in the Magiarch's absence Inherits control while Lynleit carries the Magiarchate. He must keep a private company, its government contracts, and its permanent Spill mandate functioning without magical authority or the founder's declared succession. 05 Political footprint MSF's concentration of force in Turon MSF's concentration of officers in Turon is sufficient to make a small rebellion or secession imaginable. Officer culture, divided logistics, constitutional loyalty, and the absence of any desire to rebel keep that capacity dormant. Politicians remain uneasy because the state cannot simply command or reorganize its private contractor. The final safeguard is the belief that MSF officers are decent people. See Turon in The Duchy → 06 Operational pairing Felix and Reiner in the field ♞ KNIGHT PATTERN Felix Hacking and communications let Felix move through an operation indirectly. He finds unexpected access, redirects information, and reaches positions that a straightforward approach cannot. Open Felix's profile → ♜ ROOK PATTERN Reiner Reiner is the physically imposing brute-force specialist. He anchors protection, takes the direct route, and provides controlled power when a line must be held or broken. Open Reiner's profile → 07 Known personnel People who define the institution Founder Fionn Heir and director Lynleit Successor and rival Helena Unofficial asset, later director Kyrien Hacking and communications Felix Brute force and protection Reiner ✎ Page notes MSF Use notes to refine the agency without turning open questions into canon.

entries.title: The Church
entries.text: The Church # the-church Institutional record Known facts only World / The Church † Religious institution Knowledge kept behind doctrine Every church knows about the Magi at the highest point of its hierarchy. That knowledge descends only through controlled channels, leaving most clergy and church staff inside the same protected ignorance as the public. Public role Faith and authority Awareness Every church head Covert arm Special envoys Clergy access Highly restricted 01 Distributed knowledge The institution does not know as one body 01 MAJORITY OF THE CHURCH Ordinary faith Most clergy, staff, and worshippers operate inside the same protected ignorance as the wider public. Religious office alone does not grant access to magical knowledge. 02 HEAD OF THE HIERARCHY Guaranteed awareness The head of every church knows about the Magi and directs that church's response to the hidden world. 03 CONTROLLED OPERATORS Special envoys Each church maintains a contingent of operatives who carry the title of special envoy and act in the name of its head. OTHER RELIGIOUS TRADITIONS Pagan cults among the Magi Ancient pagan religions, including the Cult of Inanna, belong intrinsically to the Magi world. Their place in magic is distinct from the Church's official religious doctrines. Read about pagan traditions → 02 Special envoys Priesthood is the cover, not the profession OFFICIAL APPEARANCE Envoys of the heads of churches Special envoys are trained and presented as priests, allowing them to move through religious institutions with a credible public identity. Their primary training covers political operations, intelligence, combat, and covert intervention. Authority Act for a church head Cover Priesthood Structure Contingent within each church 01 Politics Institutional access, negotiation, leverage, and influence. 02 Espionage Covert placement, observation, clandestine activity, and the possible penetration of rival institutions. 03 Intelligence Collection, assessment, and controlled circulation of knowledge. 04 Combat Operational force when diplomacy and concealment fail. 05 Assassination Some envoys are trained for assassination. 06 Specialization Each envoy develops one or several operational specialties. Separate traditions Shared purpose does not mean shared doctrine. Both traditions maintain covert, assassination-capable priesthoods while regarding the other's system as dangerously unaccountable. ORTHODOX CHURCH Trust before procedure Orthodox envoys favor personal chains of trust, confession-like secrecy, and discretionary judgment. Authority moves through relationships whose moral burden rests heavily on the person exercising it. CATHOLIC CHURCH Procedure before discretion Catholic envoys favor dossiers, compartmentalized offices, and codified authorization. Authority moves through records and separated functions intended to prevent any one operative from holding the whole design. PLAUSIBLE, NOT CONFIRMED Special-envoy capabilities make covert or illegal infiltration of Magiarchates and other factions possible. The same risk also runs in reverse, because church structures may themselves be penetrated. 03 Institutional relations Every relationship is conditional WITH THE PUBLIC Protect ignorance Magic remains outside ordinary understanding, and Church knowledge is kept narrow. WITH THE MAGIARCHY Sanction, constrain, and verify Cross-national church structures face Magiarchates that are kept territorial and separate. Both sides hunt unsanctioned Magi, but the Church often doubts that Magiarchs will act decisively enough. WITH THE STATE Reveal only what is necessary Negotiations can occur near public institutions without making their magical subject visible to ordinary officials or officers. WITH RENEGADE MAGI Hunt through special envoys Magi without a jurisdiction who practice outside church supervision or permission are treated as criminals. Special envoys pursue them alongside the resources of the responsible Magiarch. 04 Accepted boundaries Not every possible act is permitted FORBIDDEN MIRACLE-MAKING Harmless effect, prohibited form The Church distinguishes pressure-based magecraft from miracle-making that resembles wizardry or imitates acts associated with Jesus, saints, saviours, and other sacred figures. Walking on water crosses that symbolic boundary. Lynleit conceals the accidental talent because exposure would bring strong punishment even if she had harmed nobody. Open Lynleit's profile → 05 Canon doctrine Suppression doctrine THE PRACTICAL RULE Protect the boundary of public knowledge Suppression doctrine is a shared responsibility of the Church and the Magiarchy for keeping witnesses of magic from carrying dangerous knowledge back into ordinary society. The Church holds final sanction over the doctrine, while Magiarchal resources may investigate, contain, absorb, or remove witnesses under that authority. It is not one fixed punishment. The response depends on what the witness knows, how credible they are, how much exposure has already occurred, and whether the witness can be contained without creating a larger crisis. 01 · IRREVERSIBLE Elimination Murder, assassination, or kidnapping may be considered when the Church believes exposure cannot be contained by other means. 02 · PRESSURE Coercion Extortion, intimidation, bribery, and threats can redirect a witness without making the magical truth public. 03 · REFRAME Discrediting A witness may be framed as mentally ill, unreliable, or otherwise incapable of persuading anyone who hears the account. 04 · ABSORPTION Church integration Some witnesses are forced into Church staff or clergy, where their access, movement, and story can be controlled from inside the institution. 05 · SERVICE Magiarchal integration Others may be absorbed into Magiarchy service staff or a supervised operational role, turning dangerous knowledge into a controlled obligation under Church-sanctioned authority. UNRESOLVED BOUNDARY Suppression can include coercion, forced service, or killing. Church sanction does not settle disagreements over whether a particular witness must be silenced. The Prosecutor General Kyrien's father's case A senior prosecutor helps government officials connected to the Magiarchy fabricate a case against Kyrien's father, a military-police commander who has silently witnessed magic. When repeated allegations fail to make him submit, the directing officials obtain sanction for his murder and present it as suicide. Some participants know the magical purpose; others act under confidential national-security instructions. The later inquiry finds distorted evidence, but a closed review protects the prosecutor, who is publicly vindicated and promoted to Prosecutor General. Read the family history → Read the Chapter → 06 Story contact Father Mikhail finds the first witness breach Early in September, Fionn and Lynleit enter a church for confidential negotiations while Felix and Reiner wait outside. Later, Father Mikhail becomes the first authority to discover that Lynleit has disclosed forbidden knowledge to Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner. When she insists on handling the breach herself, he warns her: “What you do is none of my business, but don't be surprised if I'll be sent to clean up your mess.” The confrontation begins the pressure to place part of MSF under Magiarchal and Church accountability. Open the confrontation → Meet Father Mikhail → ✎ Page notes The Church Use notes to define doctrine, hierarchy, and boundaries without treating open questions as facts.

entries.title: The Director's House
entries.text: The Director's House # director-house Residential location record Family home · discreet MSF node World / The Director's House Residence · family seat · operational node The Director's House The family keeps two houses. The original stands in Turon, where Lynleit lived with her mother during junior school. After her mother's death, Fionn moved the family to Vilen for better access to the capital. The Vilen house is a three-floor residence whose offices, library, and discreet working rooms also support MSF operations. Floors Three Family houses Turon and Vilen Setting Vilen hillside above the river Rear grounds Small park and garden Operational role Residential mini-HQ 01 Family history Two houses, one family history Distant city House on the hill Rear garden City river Behind the house, a compact private park descends toward the river-facing edge of the hill. Thick vegetation and mature trees surround the residence closely enough for wind in the leaves and branches to remain part of its daily sound. Below, the river flows toward Vilen's city center. Lynleit regards flowing water as life energy: its movement gives her emotional grounding even though she has feared drowning since childhood. 02 Vertical plan Floors and private rooms 03 Highest floor Lynleit's chosen room A desk between trees and water After the family moved from Turon to Vilen, Lynleit made a third-floor study-bedroom her condition for accepting the new house. Its height lets her look beyond the trees toward the river while she works. Wind moving through leaves and branches gives the room the natural sound she finds most inspiring. 02 Middle floor Interior The second floor The rooms on this floor have not been described. 01 Garden level Glass and greenery Glass-enclosed rooms The rear side of the first floor opens into glass-enclosed relaxation areas facing dense greenery. In summer they extend domestic life among the trees. In winter the same rooms preserve the sight and sound of the landscape while protecting everyone inside from cold, rain, and wind. READING Library The family has a substantial library for reading, study, and research. WORK Several offices Private meetings and administrative work take place in offices within the house. 03 Dual role Residence and command space occupy the same address FAMILY NEST A place that belongs to the family first The family sleeps, studies, and rests here. Fionn's work shares the house with its bedrooms, garden, and glass-enclosed relaxation rooms. SHARED THRESHOLD Privacy becomes operational access The director can receive trusted people, review sensitive work, and continue agency business without leaving the protection and familiarity of home. MINI-HQ A discreet extension of MSF The offices and library support selected meetings, planning, and confidential work. MSF's formal headquarters remains in Turon. 04 Story connections Events at the house RESIDENT Lynleit Her third-floor room brings together the distant view, surrounding trees, and flowing water she uses for inspiration and emotional grounding. → DIRECTOR Fionn His public family seat also supports the confidential demands of MSF leadership. → INSTITUTION MSF The house is a residential operational node, distinct from the agency's formal headquarters in Turon. → HOUSEHOLD Ash enters the house Lynleit catches the grey cat after a clumsy chase, then cannot bring herself to put him out in the rain. → ✎ Page notes House Use notes to refine rooms, access, and domestic details without turning open architecture into canon.

entries.title: The Duchy
entries.text: The Duchy # narvea National reference record Country profile World / The Duchy of Narvea COUNTRY RECORD NAR · 001 Primary setting The Duchy of Narvea A large, sovereign Baltic country built around two sources of legitimacy: the Ducal Crown and the parliamentary state. Sovereignty resides jointly in the Crown and the Nation. Government Constitutional duchy State identity Multinational and civic Parliamentary capital Vilen Ducal seat Rennel MSF headquarters Turon Region Eastern Baltic Story role Main country Diplomatic role European meeting ground Jump to Territory Cities Authority Diplomacy Institutions Culture Fog 01 Territory A state along the eastern Baltic Narvea reaches from the approaches to St. Petersburg toward the southwestern Baltic frontier near Gdansk. National flag Ducal standard Show details for Rennel Show details for Turon Show details for Bird's Nest Show details for Port City Show details for Vilen Map of Narvea Hover, focus, tap, or select a city Mapped roles Why these cities matter Five centers divide Narvea's political, diplomatic, and strategic life. 01 Rennel · Ducal seat Home of the Crown, Court, ceremony, and dynastic archives. It represents continuity and sovereign legitimacy. 02 Turon · MSF headquarters The private contractor's concentration of officers gives it unusual local power. Constitutional loyalty and divided logistics restrain it, but politicians know the final safeguard is the officers' own decency. 03 Bird's Nest · Diplomatic ground Rival nations meet here to negotiate. Every country uses a different name for the city. 04 Port City · Western gateway Narvea's principal western connection to Baltic trade, maritime movement, and foreign access. 05 Vilen · Parliamentary capital Parliament, Cabinet, ministries, courts, and financial institutions make it the center of the modern state. 02 Dual capital tradition One country, two political worlds Rennel is the Ducal capital, Vilen the governmental capital, and Turon the military center and home of MSF. Rennel City image unavailable THE CROWN Ducal capital Rennel Located in the old Narva region. It represents dynasty, continuity, military tradition, nobility, and ceremony. Ducal Palace and Court Privy Council Ducal Guard headquarters Dynastic and heraldic archives Formal audiences Vilen City image unavailable THE STATE Parliamentary capital Vilen Narvea's center of government, law, administration, commerce, and modern political life. Its enormous urban park becomes the first visible center of the disappearances. Parliament and Cabinet Government ministries Major courts Financial institutions Vast park at the center of the first disappearances Turon City image unavailable THE PRESSURE POINT MSF headquarters Turon Turon is home to the headquarters of MSF, a fully private intelligence business that sells services to the government while retaining control of its own succession and internal affairs. Its officers give the company enough local force to mount a small rebellion or attempt secession if it ever chose to do so. Officer culture, divided logistics, constitutional loyalty, and a genuine lack of separatist ambition keep that possibility theoretical. MSF headquarters and senior officer corps Operational strength beyond ordinary agency needs Potential leverage over the central government Political anxiety that ultimately depends on personal restraint No rebellion is openly planned. The possibility simply remains in the backrooms of Narvean political life, where senior officials cannot afford to ignore it. 03 Constitutional balance Parliament governs. The Crown safeguards. Parliament chooses and controls the government, passes laws, and authorizes public money. The Duke gives constitutional form to those decisions and intervenes only through narrowly defined reserve powers. C Ducal sphere The Duke Head of state and constitutional guardian. Formally appoints the Prime Minister who commands parliamentary confidence Promulgates laws already passed by Parliament without rewriting them Represents the state, receives ambassadors, and maintains the Court and Ducal Guard Uses narrow reserve powers only during constitutional emergencies CROWN CONSTITUTIONAL BALANCE NATION P Democratic sphere Parliament & Government Elected authority and the executive accountable to it. Parliament grants or withdraws confidence in the Prime Minister and government Parliament debates, amends, and passes laws and approves taxation and spending The Prime Minister directs Cabinet, ministries, and the civil service The government sets domestic, defence, economic, social, and ordinary foreign policy 04 Diplomatic tradition The room where Europe stepped back Narvea became a trusted meeting ground where opposing European powers could settle their differences before rivalry became open conflict. NEUTRAL GROUND Authority meets here before force. Narvea's influence rests less on commanding Europe than on keeping its rivals in the same room long enough to avoid escalation. Method Conference and settlement Legacy Borders shaped without continental war 1803 to 1815 NAPOLEONIC WARS Narvea helped contain a continental crisis Its mediation played an important and constructive role during the wars. The settlements of this period also began shaping Narvea's borders into their modern form. 1917 EASTERN SETTLEMENT Revolution was prevented Opposing powers gathered in Narvea and contained an eastern political crisis before it could become a revolution. 1939 CONTINENTAL SETTLEMENT Europe avoided a major war Another Narvean conference stopped escalation between European powers, allowing the continent's borders and history to take a different course. NOW LIVING LEGACY Diplomacy became ordinary culture The habit of mediation still shapes how Narvean institutions understand authority, legitimacy, and public service. LANGUAGE AS CIVIC PRACTICE Multilingualism is expected, not exceptional. People in authority are expected to know several languages, but the custom reaches far beyond diplomatic circles. Narveans often move between languages in ordinary conversation for precision, courtesy, emphasis, or simple habit, even when no negotiation is taking place. THE CITY WITH MANY NAMES Bird's Nest is only one of its titles. Most negotiations between rival nations take place here. Every country has its own name for the city; Narveans call it Bird's Nest. 05 Institutions Parallel systems, one state Responsibility is divided deliberately. Similar-looking institutions can answer to different centers of authority. STATE · 01 Narvean Armed Forces The national Army, Navy, Air Force, reserves, and intelligence services answer through the constitutional government. National defence CROWN · 01 Ducal Guard An elite Crown formation protecting the ducal family, residences, and selected constitutional institutions. Dynastic security STATE · 02 Narvean Police Ordinary law enforcement remains under civilian authority, most likely through the Ministry of the Interior. Public order CROWN · 02 Privy Council Advises the Duke on constitutional questions, appointments, security, foreign affairs, and emergencies. Sovereign counsel BRIDGE · 01 Council of State A standing bridge between Crown and government for constitutional review, administrative law, major appointments, disputes, and emergency continuity. Its most dangerous cases begin when ordinary state sovereignty collides with supernatural authority the public constitution cannot acknowledge. Jurisdictional paradox Service and precedence Rank is not the same as office Narvea maintains its own hierarchy of court and civil ranks. A person's rank controls formal precedence, while their actual work may be diplomatic, judicial, academic, military, or administrative. 01 Chancellor of Narvea 02 Actual Privy Councillor 03 Privy Councillor 04 Actual State Councillor 05 State Councillor Drake's rank 06 Collegiate Councillor RANK AND OFFICE Drake is a State Councillor by rank and an Official for Special Assignments by office. He serves as an elite executive troubleshooter attached to a high-ranking personal office. Free from routine administration, he carries delegated authority into confidential criminal investigations, political counter-espionage, emergency corruption audits, and diplomatic errands. Open Drake's profile → 06 Cultural character Layered, regional, distinctly Narvean Narvean is a shared political identity, not a single ethnicity. Different regions keep their own language, faith, architecture, and historical memory. CIVIC IDENTITY The state is the common ground. Regional, linguistic, religious, urban, and rural communities can all be fully Narvean. INSTITUTIONS Old military customs, ducal administration, civic government, and modern Narvean constitutionalism. FAITH Catholic and Orthodox traditions coexist across different regions. PUBLIC LIFE Baltic merchant culture, old aristocratic ceremony, and modern parliamentary politics. CENTRAL TENSION A modern country that never fully discarded inherited hierarchy. Why it matters to the story A crisis in Narvea can become an argument over who has the right to act. The Crown, government, and older institutions must cooperate, but they do not share all their knowledge or accept responsibility for the same consequences. 07 Weather and visibility Narvean fog Fog is a recurring national problem, especially in certain areas. It delays journeys, restricts observation, and makes searches harder. Much of it is ordinary weather. During the Spill Some Holumn incidents produce unusually dense or extensive fog and mist. Vilen's quarantined park and river encounters are particularly affected. Familiar routes become difficult to follow by sight, and people can lose visual contact while remaining close enough to hear one another. Fog alone cannot tell a resident whether anything supernatural is happening. Holumns and the Spill → NARVEAN STATE ARCHIVE Read Markdown ↗ Document history → ✎ Page notes The Duchy Waiting 01 Add city images Replace the Rennel, Vilen, and Turon placeholders when approved city art is available. entries.title: The Magiarchy
entries.text: The Magiarchy # the-magiarchy Magical governance framework Territorial order World / The Magiarchy Territorial magical order A hierarchy that ends at the border The highest official position a Magus can obtain is Magiarch. Each Magiarch oversees magical affairs and relations with the churches inside a defined territory, but no Magiarch may turn that authority into a larger united organization. Highest office Magiarch Jurisdiction One territory Primary relation Magiarchy and churches Higher union Explicitly forbidden 01 Highest office The Magiarch is the ceiling of lawful magical authority OFFICIAL APEX Magiarch The office is usually held by the main Magus assigned to oversee the Magiarchy within a single territorial jurisdiction. 01 Territorial oversight Each Magiarch holds authority within a defined country or district. No universal magical hierarchy exists above them. 02 Church relations The office manages the local relationship between organized Magi and the churches that monitor and counterbalance them. 03 Factional leadership A Magiarch and the Magi aligned with them become a political actor with interests, allies, rivals, and local pressures. RECOGNITION PROCESS Authority is requested, judged, or won Several methods are known, and some carry far more respect than others. 01 Formal application A Magus with a substantial network, friendships, and connections submits a claim to the Church. Church approval gives the office its ordinary seal of legitimacy. 02 Contested decision When several candidates possess credible claims, church authorities and respected Magiarchs from other jurisdictions may share the decision. 03 Fitness contest A deadlock may be settled through a duel or another controlled competition intended to measure fitness for the office. 04 Sanctioned war The radical path permits rival Magi to fight to the death under Church supervision. Innocents cannot be harmed, and the existence of magic must remain hidden from the wider world. RECOGNITION CAN BE WITHDRAWN The Church may revoke recognition and destroy a Magiarch's legitimacy, but it cannot directly install a replacement. Withdrawal of recognition can therefore leave a vacancy without giving the Church the right to choose who fills it. 02 Territorial scale Jurisdiction follows practical size COMMON MODEL One country A single Magiarch may oversee the whole territory when its size and magical population can be managed as one jurisdiction. LARGER TERRITORY One district A large country may be divided into several Magiarchates. Each governs its own district independently, with no national magical superior. WHO DRAWS THE LINE Church authorities certify Magiarchate boundaries according to practical governability. The same transnational religious hierarchy that prevents Magi from forming a transnational command therefore decides where each supposedly independent magical jurisdiction begins and ends. 03 Structural counterbalance Magiarchal power is fragmented because the churches are not MAGIARCHATES Territorial and separate Magiarchs are explicitly forbidden from uniting into a larger organization. Their lawful authority stops with their territory. COUNTERWEIGHT CHURCHES Organized across borders The churches retain cross-national organization, giving them a wider structure that counterbalances the concentrated power of Magi. WHY THE BAN EXISTS A united organization of Magiarchs would overturn the intended balance and create open conflict with the churches. Examine the church counterweight → 04 Relations without a sovereign Magiarchates exist in an anarchic order NO HIGHER MAGICAL GOVERNMENT There is no lawful authority above the Magiarchs capable of reliably settling disputes between them. Anarchy here does not mean constant chaos. It means the absence of a superior power that can compel every Magiarchate to obey. 01 Self-preservation Each faction must judge threats and protect its own position. 02 Alliance Cooperation depends on interest, trust, and temporary alignment. 03 Rivalry Competing aims can produce pressure resembling conflict between states. 04 Uncertainty No Magiarch can be certain how another faction will use its power. PLAUSIBLE METHOD · NOT CONFIRMED Institutions may penetrate one another Rival Magiarchates, criminal Magi, and church networks may covertly or illegally place operatives, informants, or influence inside one another's structures. If this occurs, visible affiliation cannot be treated as proof of who truly directed an action. 05 Outside the sanctioned order A Magus without jurisdiction becomes a common enemy CRIMINAL STATUS Unbound and unsanctioned A Magus is treated as a criminal when they belong to no territorial jurisdiction and practice outside church supervision or permission. 01 No jurisdiction The Magus does not belong to a recognized Magiarchate. 02 No church sanction Their practice proceeds without church supervision or permission. CHURCH RESPONSE Special envoys The churches use their covert operatives to identify, pursue, and suppress Magi outside the sanctioned order. Examine special envoys → SHARED TARGET MAGIARCH RESPONSE Territorial resources The responsible Magiarch is expected to use the resources under their authority to hunt the same offender. SUPPRESSION DOCTRINE Witness control is a shared responsibility of the Church and Magiarchy, but the Church holds final sanction. Magiarchal resources may carry out coercion, discrediting, forced service, kidnapping, or lethal removal according to circumstance and perceived exposure. Read the doctrine record → UNEASY COOPERATION Church authorities often doubt that a Magiarch will act decisively against another Magus, even while relying on that Magiarch to help pursue the offender. 06 Succession after Fionn The Magiarchate passes to Lynleit NARVEA Lynleit After Fionn 's death, his biological daughter eventually inherits the Magiarchate as Narvea's new Magiarch. During her later absence, Kyrien carries the directorate in her absence. The two heirs divide the offices Fionn once held together. Open Lynleit's profile → Open the MSF record → 07 Religion among the Magi Ancient pagan traditions PAGAN CULT Cult of Inanna Doom Has an Address → The Cult of Inanna and other ancient pagan cults and religions play an important role in magic. These traditions are intrinsic to the Magi world and distinct from official Church doctrine. Fionn's lineage has maintained its association with the Cult for three thousand years. Lynleit inherits that association without directly participating. Father Mikhail knows the lineage's history of covenants and the political importance of intimacy within that tradition. ✎ Page notes Magiarchy Use notes to define offices and inter-Magiarchate customs without turning open questions into canon.
